Fact.Name: SA information-return account types
Fact.Description: The three mutually exclusive account types printed in Form 1099-SA box 5 and Form 5498-SA box 6.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA box 3 distribution codes
Fact.Description: The six distribution codes Form 1099-SA box 3 prints, each option the code itself: 1 normal distribution, 2 excess contributions, 3 disability, 4 death distribution other than code 6, 5 prohibited transaction, 6 death distribution after the year of death to a nonspouse beneficiary.

Fact.Name: Forms 1099-SA
Fact.Description: Source documents received for HSA, Archer MSA, or Medicare Advantage MSA accounts, one item per document. This information-return collection records the document, not a second contribution or distribution on the income tax return.

Fact.Name: 1099-SA document owner
Fact.Description: The filer to whom this document belongs. An unanswered owner is Incomplete; no primary-filer default is assumed.

Fact.Name: 1099-SA box 5: validated account type
Fact.Description: The account type derived from this document's three printed checkbox answers. All answers must be complete and exactly one must be checked; missing, all-unchecked, or contradictory selections leave the account type Incomplete.

Fact.Name: 1099-SA box 5: HSA checkbox
Fact.Description: Whether this document's selected account type is HSA. All three checkbox facts remain Incomplete while this document's account type is unanswered.

Fact.Name: 1099-SA box 5: Archer MSA checkbox
Fact.Description: Whether this document's selected account type is Archer MSA. All three checkbox facts remain Incomplete while this document's account type is unanswered.

Fact.Name: 1099-SA box 5: MA MSA checkbox
Fact.Description: Whether this document's selected account type is MA MSA. All three checkbox facts remain Incomplete while this document's account type is unanswered.

Fact.Name: 5498-SA document owner

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA trustee or payer name
Fact.Description: The trustee or payer name printed on this source document. It belongs to this document, not to another account held by the filer.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA box 1: gross distribution
Fact.Description: The total distribution on this source document, including any earnings separately reported in box 2. This is a source amount, not a determination of taxable income.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA box 2: earnings on excess contributions
Fact.Description: The earnings separately reported in box 2 of this source document. They are already included in box 1 and must not be added to it a second time.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA box 4: fair market value on date of death
Fact.Description: The box 4 amount reported by the trustee on this document, including any adjustments already made by the trustee under the reporting instructions.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA box 5: HSA source checkbox
Fact.Description: Copy whether the HSA checkbox is checked on this document. An unchecked box is an explicit false answer, not a missing answer. Do not infer this answer from another document or a return-level account flag.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA box 5: Archer MSA source checkbox
Fact.Description: Copy whether the Archer MSA checkbox is checked on this document. An unchecked box is an explicit false answer, not a missing answer. Do not infer this answer from another document or a return-level account flag.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA box 5: MA MSA source checkbox
Fact.Description: Copy whether the MA MSA checkbox is checked on this document. An unchecked box is an explicit false answer, not a missing answer. Do not infer this answer from another document or a return-level account flag.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA belongs to primary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form 1099-SA belongs to the primary filer. Completeness-first, the shape the sibling document-intake modules carry: an unanswered ../filer resolves complete-safe FALSE rather than inheriting a primary-filer default, because a document whose recipient is unassigned belongs to neither filer. Read only by ../recipientTin.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA belongs to secondary filer
Fact.Description: The secondary twin of ../belongsToPrimaryFiler: same completeness-first shape, same complete-safe FALSE on an unanswered ../filer. Read only by ../recipientTin.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA RECIPIENT'S TIN
Fact.Description: The RECIPIENT'S TIN box, derived from this document's own recipient (../filer): the primary filer's TIN on the primary filer's Form 1099-SA, the secondary filer's TIN on the spouse's, and never the return's primary filer by default — a spouse's account would otherwise carry the wrong person. Nothing to ask; the ../filer answer decides it. Feeds no federal line; exported for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-SA register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA calendar year
Fact.Description: The "For calendar year" entry printed in the form's title block, as a four-digit year. A form for a year other than 2025 belongs on that year's return or is a corrected prior-year form. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-SA register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA VOID box
Fact.Description: The VOID checkbox in the form's header. It prints on Copy A only; the recipient's Copy B carries CORRECTED alone. An unchecked box is an explicit false answer. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-SA register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA CORRECTED box
Fact.Description: The CORRECTED checkbox in the form's header: "CORRECTED" on Copy A, "CORRECTED (if checked)" on the recipient's Copy B. A payer that fixes a form it already filed sends a new one with this box checked; copy the corrected amounts, not the original ones. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-SA register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA PAYER'S TIN
Fact.Description: The PAYER'S TIN box, recorded with fact type EIN: a trustee or payer of an HSA, Archer MSA or MA MSA distribution is an entity that files information returns, so the box carries an employer identification number, the same type formW2s:/formW2s/*/ein and formW2Gs:/formW2Gs/*/writablePayerTin give a payer identifier. The name half of the same block is ../writableTrusteeName. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-SA register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA RECIPIENT'S name
Fact.Description: The RECIPIENT'S name box, copied as the payer printed it, even where that differs from the name on this return. Which person on the return received the document is ../filer, not this box. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-SA register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA recipient street address
Fact.Description: The recipient's "Street address (including apt. no.)" box, copied as printed even where it is an old address. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-SA register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA recipient city, state and ZIP
Fact.Description: The recipient's "City or town, state or province, country, and ZIP or foreign postal code" box, copied as printed. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-SA register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA account number
Fact.Description: The "Account number (see instructions)" box: an account or other unique number the payer assigned to distinguish this account. It is required of a payer filing more than one Form 1099-SA for the same recipient. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns (it tells two documents from one payer apart) and bound in the Form 1099-SA register.

Fact.Name: Forms 1099-LTC
Fact.Description: Source documents received on Form 1099-LTC, Long-Term Care and Accelerated Death Benefits, one item per document. This information-return collection records the document; it is not a second statement of the benefits the return reports. Form 8853 Section C's line 17 and line 19 intakes remain the figures the return computes from.

Fact.Name: 1099-LTC document owner
Fact.Description: The filer to whom this document belongs — the person on this return who received the Form 1099-LTC as POLICYHOLDER. An unanswered owner is Incomplete; no primary-filer default is assumed. The INSURED is a separate person on the printed form and is recorded in ../writableInsuredName and ../writableInsuredTin, which are not filer selectors: the insured need not be on this return at all.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC belongs to primary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form 1099-LTC belongs to the primary filer. Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC belongs to secondary filer

Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC POLICYHOLDER'S TIN
Fact.Description: The POLICYHOLDER'S TIN box, derived from this document's own policyholder (../filer): the primary filer's TIN on the primary filer's Form 1099-LTC, the secondary filer's TIN on the spouse's, and never the return's primary filer by default. Nothing to ask; the ../filer answer decides it. This is the POLICYHOLDER, not the INSURED — the insured's TIN is ../writableInsuredTin, a writable, because the insured is often a parent or other person who is not on this return.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC box 1: gross long-term care benefits paid
Fact.Description: Box 1: the gross long-term care benefits the payer paid during the year. Intake only. Form 8853 line 17 asks the taxpayer for the total of the box 1 amounts on the forms whose box 3 "Per diem" is checked, and line 17 remains that taxpayer-stated total (/writableForm8853Line17GrossLtcPerDiemPayments); no line of Section C reads this collection, and wiring it up is a computation change reserved for a successor unit. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-LTC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC box 2: accelerated death benefits paid
Fact.Description: Box 2: the accelerated death benefits the payer paid during the year. Intake only, for the same reason box 1 is: Form 8853 line 19 remains the taxpayer's own figure and excludes amounts paid because the insured was terminally ill, which this box does not separate. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-LTC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC box 3: "Per diem" checkbox
Fact.Description: Box 3 prints "Check one:" over two boxes, "Per diem" and "Reimbursed amount"; this is the first of the pair, at the printed multiplicity. Per diem means the benefits were paid on a per diem or other periodic basis without regard to the actual expenses, which is the basis Form 8853 Section C's per diem limitation applies to. An unchecked box is an explicit false answer. Unanswered it is complete-safe, and nothing on Section C reads it — line 17 stays the taxpayer's own total of the per diem forms. Stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-LTC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC box 3: "Reimbursed amount" checkbox
Fact.Description: The second of the two box 3 checkboxes, at the printed multiplicity: the benefits reimbursed the actual costs of qualified long-term care, rather than being paid per diem. An unchecked box is an explicit false answer. The form says "Check one", so exactly one of this pair is expected; the dictionary does not enforce that, because a filer copying a payer's form must be able to record what the payer actually printed. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-LTC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC box 4: qualified contract (optional)
Fact.Description: Box 4, marked "(optional)" on the printed form: whether the benefits were paid under a qualified long-term care insurance contract. An unchecked box is an explicit false answer; a payer that left the optional box blank leaves this unanswered, which is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-LTC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC box 5: "Chronically ill" checkbox
Fact.Description: Box 5, "Check, if applicable (optional)", first of the two status boxes: the insured was certified chronically ill. An unchecked box is an explicit false answer; an optional box the payer left blank stays unanswered, which is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-LTC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC box 5: "Terminally ill" checkbox
Fact.Description: Box 5, second of the two status boxes: the insured was certified terminally ill. An unchecked box is an explicit false answer; an optional box the payer left blank stays unanswered, which is complete-safe. Form 8853 line 19 excludes amounts received because the insured was terminally ill, and that exclusion is honoured inside the line 19 intake itself, unchanged by this box. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-LTC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC box 5: date certified
Fact.Description: Box 5's "Date certified" entry: the date the insured was certified chronically or terminally ill. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-LTC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC INSURED'S TIN
Fact.Description: The INSURED'S TIN box, a WRITABLE and not a derivation: the insured is the chronically or terminally ill individual on whose behalf the benefits were paid, and that person is frequently not on this return at all (a parent, a former spouse). Contrast ../policyholderTin, which IS derived, because the policyholder is by construction the ../filer this document belongs to. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-LTC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-LTC INSURED'S name
Fact.Description: The INSURED'S name box, copied as the payer printed it. The insured need not be a person on this return. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-LTC register.

Fact.Description: The insured's "Street address (including apt. no.)" box — the right-hand address block, which is the INSURED'S, not the policyholder's. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Feeds no federal line; stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 1099-LTC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-SA box 3: distribution code as printed
Fact.Description: Box 3, the single distribution code 1 through 6 the payer printed on THIS document, chosen from /form1099SaDistributionCodeOptions, whose options are the printed codes themselves (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1099sa.pdf, page 3): 1 normal, 2 excess contributions, 3 disability, 4 death distribution other than code 6, 5 prohibited transaction, 6 death distribution after the year of death to a nonspouse beneficiary. It is a transcription of the box, not the graph's classification: /hsaDistributions/*/hsaDistributionCode is an Enum of option NAMES on the DISTRIBUTIONS collection the filer reports, a different collection with a different multiplicity, and this box neither feeds it nor is replaced by it. Fact.Name: Form 5498-SA box 1: Archer MSA contributions
Fact.Description: Box 1: the employee's or self-employed person's Archer MSA contributions made in 2025 and in 2026 for 2025, as the trustee printed them. Intake only — the Archer MSA deduction the federal return computes is Form 8853's, taken from the filer's own entries, and this box does not feed it. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 5498-SA register.

Fact.Name: Form 5498-SA box 2: total contributions made in 2025
Fact.Description: Box 2: the total contributions made in 2025 to this HSA or Archer MSA, including qualified HSA funding distributions from an IRA. This is the TRUSTEE's total; it is wider than /filers/*/writableHsaNonemployerContributionsTaxYear, which is the filer's NONEMPLOYER contributions alone (employer contributions arrive on Form W-2 box 12 code W), so the federal computation keeps that narrower fact as its input and this box does not feed it. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 5498-SA register.

Fact.Name: Form 5498-SA box 3: contributions made in 2026 for 2025
Fact.Description: Box 3: the total HSA or Archer MSA contributions made in 2026 for 2025. It is the trustee's counterpart of /filers/*/writableHsaNonemployerContributionsTaxYearPlusOne, which stays the federal input for the same reason box 2 does — that fact is the filer's nonemployer share and this box is the trustee's total. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 5498-SA register.

Fact.Name: Form 5498-SA box 4: rollover contributions
Fact.Description: Box 4: any rollover received into this account in 2025 — from an Archer MSA to this Archer MSA, or from an HSA or Archer MSA to this HSA. This amount is not included in boxes 1, 2 or 3. It is the RECEIVING side of a rollover; the graph carries only the paying side's attestation (../../hsaDistributions/*/writableDistributionsRolloverBool, Form 8889 line 14b), which this box does not feed. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 5498-SA register.

Fact.Name: Form 5498-SA box 5: fair market value of the account
Fact.Description: Box 5: the fair market value of this HSA, Archer MSA or MA MSA at the end of 2025, as the trustee reported it. Form 5329 lines 41 and 49 cap the 6% excise at the account value on December 31, 2025 including 2025 contributions made in 2026 (box 3), a figure this box alone does not give; those lines read the filer's typed December 31 value, and this box is the document the filer reads it from. Unanswered it is complete-safe. Stored for the state and local returns and bound in the Form 5498-SA register.

Fact.Description: Did you get an interest in a health savings account (HSA) in 2025 because the person who owned the account died? Answer yes if you were named as the beneficiary of someone else's HSA and that person died, whether or not the account paid you anything this year. A surviving spouse who is the beneficiary files Form 8889 as though the account were their own. Unanswered is read as no.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 2 ANSWERED - this filer has stated what they put in themselves
Fact.Description:
Whether BOTH Form 8889 line 2 writables are answered, whatever the amount. The two dependency guards read it: a claimable dependent whose line 2 is answered files, and a claimable dependent whose line 2 is unanswered is refused.
WHY ANSWEREDNESS AND NOT AMOUNT. A POSITIVE line 2 answer from a claimable dependent is an IRC 4973(g)(1) excess contribution that Form 5329 Part VII computes: it flows to ../hsaDependentOwnContributionExcess and on to that filer's line 47. What is unfileable is SILENCE, and silence is exactly what this fact tests for.
THE ANSWEREDNESS TEST IS LOAD-BEARING. The two line 2 writables are declared OPTIONAL by this module's own completeness fact (../hasCompletedCoverageAndContribution, "These two are optional") and their derived readers are complete-safe to $0.00, so an amount-only test would read an UNANSWERED line 2 as a stated zero and file a dependent whose own contributions are excess, untaxed. This fact is complete-safe FALSE, which is the REFUSING direction for both guards that read it.

Fact.Name: IRC 223(b)(6) - the section 223 deduction is denied to this filer (Form 8889 line 13)
Fact.Description:
Whether IRC 223(b)(6) denies this filer the HSA deduction, because another taxpayer may claim them as a dependent. Only Form 8889 line 13 reads this fact, and line 13 is $0 when it is true.
Complete-safe FALSE on an unanswered filers:/filers/*/canBeClaimed, which keeps ../hsaTotalDeductibleAmount exactly as complete as it is without this fact.
interpretation: owner ruling, see TAX-INTERPRETATIONS-FOR-EXPERT-REVIEW.md AD-02. The ruling follows the Form 8889 / Form 5329 INSTRUCTIONS: a dependent is not an eligible individual for the Line 3 Limitation Chart, so line 3 is $0 and an employer's box 12 code W contribution is a Form 5329 line 47 excess (a claimable dependent's limitation is $0 on both routes; see ../hasHsaContributionsAndCanBeClaimedAsDependent). The STATUTORY reading - that 223(b)(6) is a deduction denial and nothing else, leaving 223(c)(1)(A) eligibility, the 223(b) limitation and the section 106(d) exclusion of an employer's contribution untouched - is the rejected alternative, kept as interpretation:provisional prose. This fact's own arm, line 13 $0, is the same under both readings.

Whether this filer's HSA contributions are refused because another taxpayer may claim them as a dependent. One case refuses: the third conjunct, Not(../hsaDependentOwnContributionsAnswered), an UNANSWERED Form 8889 line 2. The two line 2 writables are optional and complete-safe to $0.00, so reading silence as a stated zero would file a dependent's excess untaxed. That residual is the only case /flowKnockoutFilerIsDependentAndContributesToHsa still refuses.
WHAT FILES. A dependent whose own (non-employer) contributions are ANSWERED at $0 files, because IRC 223(b)(6) denies them only a deduction (taken at ../hsaDeductionDeniedAsDependent, Form 8889 line 13). Their employer's contribution has no IRC 223(b) limitation left to stay excludable under IRC 106(d) up to — a claimable dependent's limitation is $0 on BOTH routes (legacy: ../wasEligibleToMakeHsaContributionsAllYear's `Not(canBeClaimed)` conjunct zeroes ../hsaBaseContributionLimit; vector: ../hsaLine3DependentZeroesLimitation) — so the employer amount is itself an IRC 4973(g)(1) excess contribution, computed in full through ../hsaEmployerExcessContributionAmount into Form 5329 Part VII. A dependent who answers line 2 with a POSITIVE amount files too: their own contributions are IRC 4973(g)(1) excess in full and are taxed at 6% through ../hsaDependentOwnContributionExcess into Form 5329 line 47.

Fact.Name: Knockout when a dependent filer's OWN HSA contributions are never answered
Fact.Description: A filer who can be claimed as another taxpayer's dependent has HSA contributions and has NOT answered Form 8889 line 2 at all. That unanswered line 2 is the only case refused. The employer-only dependent files, with the IRC 223(b)(6) denial taken at Form 8889 line 13; a dependent who answers line 2 with a POSITIVE amount files too, with that amount taxed in full as an IRC 4973(g)(1) excess contribution on Form 5329 Part VII.

Fact.Name: The return's MSA activity is beyond what this dictionary computes
Fact.Description:
Whether this return has an MSA AND that MSA is something other than a dormant legacy Archer account — i.e. it has contributions, distributions, or is a Medicare Advantage MSA. This is the predicate the two excess-contribution FLOW GATES read in place of a bare Not(/hasHsaMedicalSavingsAccountTypeDerived).
WHY THE FLOW GATES READ THIS AND NOT THE BARE MSA ANSWER. A bare gate suppresses the excess-contribution screens for EVERY MSA return, and the Form 8889 coverage-and-contribution chain reads those answers through /filers/*/mayHaveHsaContributions and /flowKnockoutHsaExcessContributions. On a dormant Archer return that is not refused, the bare gate would leave the ENTIRE chain — coverage status, HDHP type, line 3, line 5, line 6, line 8 — unresolved: a green guard over a blank form. Measured, not reasoned: with the bare gate the probe fixture on the dormant case showed /filers/*/hasHdhpCoverageAllYear, ../typeOfHdhpDerived, ../hasMadeContributionsToHsa, ../hsaInitialContributionLimit and ../hsaContributionLimitLessAddition all unresolved with the guard already false.
WHAT IT DOES, BY POPULATION. For a return with no MSA this fact is complete-safe FALSE and both gates behave exactly as the bare gate would. For an MSA return that is NOT dormant it is TRUE, and both gates stay suppressed. For the dormant cell it is FALSE, so the gates open and the filer is asked the ordinary excess-contribution questions every other HSA filer answers; a YES is handled by /flowKnockoutHsaExcessContributions on its own terms rather than by the MSA guard.
THE TWO FLOW FACTS ARE INSIDE THE /archerMsaForm8853Contributions CONTRACT'S DECLARED SURFACE, which names /flowToExcessContributionsPreviousYear and /flowToHsaExcessContributions as Dependencies.

Flow to the hsa-excess-contributions-previous-year screen.
The second operand is Not(/archerMsaBlocksHsaContributionScreens): a dormant legacy Archer MSA holder is asked the ordinary excess-contribution questions; the reason is written in full on /archerMsaBlocksHsaContributionScreens.

Whether the tp has excess HSA Contributions from the previous year after accounting for edit conditions

Fact.Name: The prior-year HSA excess carry-in whose AMOUNT this return has not collected
Fact.Description:
Refuses a return whose Form 5329 Part VII 6% excise on HSA excess contributions would be computed on MISSING INPUT. Part VII computes at /hsaExcessContributionExciseTaxForm5329PartVii.
A TIMELY-WITHDRAWN EXCESS IS NOT REFUSED. The return-of-excess machinery ships: the contributions themselves are Form 8889 line 14b (/filers/*/hsaTotalExcessContributionsWithdrawnInTime) and are subtracted on Form 5329 line 47, and the earnings on them are /hsaExcessContributionEarningsOtherIncome.
WHAT IT REFUSES, two slices and no more, both of them a MISSING INPUT rather than a missing computation: (1) the return says a prior-year excess exists and NEITHER filer has supplied the Form 5329 line 42 amount, so the 6% tax would be computed on a $0 carry-in and silently understated; (2) a filer supplied a carry-in above zero and has not answered the 2025 HSA contributions question at all, so Form 8889 line 12 - the limit Form 5329 line 43 absorbs the carry-in against - cannot be measured, and the absorption would silently be $0 (/filers/*/causesHsaPriorYearExcessAbsorptionUncomputable).
A THIRD, ANALOGOUS MISSING-INPUT DEFECT (the December 31 account value the line 49 cap needs) is deliberately NOT added here. This fact's own line 42-48 chain is gated behind ../hsaContributionsOverLimitAndComplete, which reads /hsaCoverageAndContributionsSectionIsComplete, which is downstream of ../mayHaveHsaContributions, which conjoins Not(/flowKnockoutHsaExcessContributions) itself - reading anything in that chain from THIS fact closes a resolution cycle (MEASURED: every form8889 case died with "Maximum call stack size exceeded" when a causesHsaForm5329Line49AccountValueUnsupplied operand keyed on ../hsaForm5329Line48TotalExcess was added to this Any). See /flowKnockoutHsaForm5329Line49AccountValueUnsupplied for the standalone knockout that covers it, which carries its own BlockSubmissionOnTrue and is independent of this fact.
IT IS A SWITCH WHOSE DEFAULT IS FALSE, deliberately, so it stays Complete for the filer whose upfront "yes" makes /hasHsaWithdrawnExcessContributionsYesNo Incomplete by flow construction (that fact is a Switch gated on /flowToHsaExcessContributions, which a prior-year "yes" turns off).

Fact.Name: Knockout Due to a Medical Savings Account
Fact.Description:
Has a set of facts that cause a knockout: the Archer MSA and Medicare Advantage MSA cases this dictionary does not compute.
WHAT FILES. The fifth operand is Not(Any(/archerMsaSectionAPartIFullyComputed, /archerMsaForm8853FullyComputed)) — an Any, deliberately, so that each population files on its own predicate whatever the other does. /archerMsaSectionAPartIFullyComputed frees the Archer holder — with contributions of either kind or none — whose twelve-month Line 3 Limitation Chart vector, plan deductible and line 4 compensation are answered, whose contributions are within the printed limits, who took no Section A Part II distribution and holds no Medicare Advantage MSA: their Form 8853 Section A Part I (lines 3, 4 and 5) computes, and the line 5 deduction reaches Schedule 1 line 23. /archerMsaForm8853FullyComputed frees two more cells: an Archer holder who took Section A Part II DISTRIBUTIONS (the taxable part to Schedule 1 line 8e, the additional 20% tax to Schedule 2 line 17e), and an Archer holder who OVER-CONTRIBUTED (the 6% excise to Schedule 2 line 8 through Form 5329 Part VI, and an excess EMPLOYER contribution additionally to Schedule 1 line 8z as Other income). The Archer excise is Form 5329 PART VI, lines 34 to 41, computed at /archerMsaExcessContributionExciseTaxForm5329PartVi: on disk, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f5329.pdf, page 2 is "Part VI Additional Tax on Excess Contributions to Archer MSAs", and https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f5329.pdf, page 1, "Part III Additional Tax on Excess Contributions to Traditional IRAs", is the IRA excise.
WHAT STILL REFUSES: Section B, the Medicare Advantage MSA distributions at lines 10 to 13b with their 50% additional tax; and a married return whose Form 5329 line 36 cannot be attributed to a spouse (/archerMsaForm5329PartViAllocationUnresolvable). Section C is Long-Term Care insurance contracts, is not MSA-gated, and is not in this guard's scope.
THE DORMANT LEGACY ACCOUNT. /archerMsaDormantLegacyAccountOnly is true only for a return whose Archer MSA took no contributions of either kind, made no distributions, and is not a Medicare Advantage MSA. Such a return has nothing to report on Form 8853 — the instructions' own "Who Must File" trigger is contributions — so it needs no attachment this repo cannot produce, and no Form 8889 line 4 reduction, and there is nothing to refuse it for.
THE FOURTH OPERAND IS REDUNDANT WITH THE FIFTH, AND INERT, AND IS KEPT. A dormant return satisfies /archerMsaSectionAPartIFullyComputed too: its line 1 and line 2 are zero, so ../archerMsaFilerHasNoContributions is true, so line 4 is a hard 0, line 3 is a hard 0 off an unanswered vector, line 5 is 0 and neither excess fires. It is also inert through the flow gates: /flowToExcessContributionsPreviousYear and /flowToHsaExcessContributions (the latter through /skipToHsaExcessContributions) read Not(/archerMsaBlocksHsaContributionScreens), which is D AND not-dormant, where D is /hasHsaMedicalSavingsAccountTypeDerived. On the population the guard refuses (D true, not dormant) both gates are structurally false and both Nots are automatic. On a dormant return /archerMsaBlocksHsaContributionScreens is false, so /flowToExcessContributionsPreviousYear = All(IsComplete(D), Not(false)) is TRUE, so the guard's FIRST operand Not(...) is false for EVERY dormant return, whatever else that return contains. Measured, not only argued: with the fourth operand removed, all 106 form8889 node-test cases stayed green. IT IS KEPT because the narrowing would otherwise live entirely in two SCREEN-ROUTING facts that could reasonably be rewritten without anyone reading this guard. With the operand here, a change to the flow gates cannot silently re-refuse the dormant cell — the guard states its own bound, and a reader who wants the narrowing removed must delete something that names /archerMsaDormantLegacyAccountOnly. The reason the flow gates read /archerMsaBlocksHsaContributionScreens is written on that fact.
NO HSA CONTRIBUTION ACTIVITY. When /someFilerHasSomeHsaActivityNotConsideringKos is Complete false no filer has an HSA contribution signal (W-2 box 12 code W, or a yes to the non-W-2 HSA activity question), so Form 8889 Part I, which holds line 6 and the Archer MSA line 4 coordination, is never computed, and the Archer MSA question is never asked (/hasHsaMedicalSavingsAccountTypeDerived reads the same gate). A Form 8889 filed for a distribution alone is a Part II return. This refusal cannot apply, and the outer Switch's first Case resolves it Complete false. Its When is IsComplete-first, so an unanswered activity question never takes it. The second Case's When is that first When's exact complement (activity unanswered, or answered yes) and always resolves Complete, so every return outside the no-activity population reaches the original body unchanged, value and completeness alike. Without the first Case the body would read facts whose own Switches run off the end on a return with no HSA activity, leaving this member, and so /flowIsKnockedOut, Incomplete on an ordinary return.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 10 - this filer's qualified HSA funding distributions
Fact.Description:
Total qualified HSA funding distribution for this filer, reported on their Form 8889 line 10.
AN HFD CONSUMES CONTRIBUTION ROOM. An HFD is a direct trustee-to-trustee transfer from an IRA into an HSA that the filer may elect out of income: line 11 adds it to the employer contributions, line 12 takes line 11 off the limit, and line 13 is the deduction that falls out. A return that excluded an HFD from Form 1040 line 4b while reporting $0 here would claim room the transfer had already used and a Part I deduction computed from that room - one return contradicting itself, in the taxpayer-favourable direction. So the exclusion (form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/line4cHfdExclusion, Form 1040 line 4c box 3) and this line are built together.
THE PER-FILER SUM LIVES IN THE form1099Rs MODULE because the intake does: an HFD arrives on a Form 1099-R, so its amount is a per-item writable there and the two named per-filer collections that module already ships do the aggregation. This fact only picks the right one.
WHY THE ELECTED AMOUNT RATHER THAN THE EXCLUDED ONE is argued on form1099Rs:/primaryFilerHfdTotal: line 10 reports the QUALIFIED funding distribution, a distribution is qualified because the filer elected it out of income, and on any submittable return the two figures are equal because an election this dictionary cannot honour already refuses the return. Reading the elected figure is also what keeps this fact out of a dependency cycle - the exclusion is capped by the contribution limit, and Form 8889 line 6 reaches line 11, which reaches this fact.
COMPLETE ON EVERY FILER: both per-filer totals are guarded sums that resolve Complete $0 on a return with no Form 1099-R, and the third Case keeps this fact Complete for a filer who is neither the primary nor the secondary.
WHAT PART III DOES WITH THIS NUMBER: line 19 computes off it. If the filer names a month of THIS tax year as the first month of the transfer's testing period in which they were not an eligible individual (/filers/*/writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth), this whole amount is included in income through /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome and taxed 10% through /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureAdditionalTax. "none" or a 2026 month gives $0 here, because the inclusion belongs to the year containing the first ineligible month.
WHAT IS NOT COVERED. (a) Form 8889 LINE 18, the last-month-rule leg, which needs a prior-year contribution amount no intake supplies; /flowKnockoutHsaTestingPeriodAdditionalIncomeYes refuses it. (b) A return where the testing-period question above is UNANSWERED while this total is above $0 and the filer is not eligible all year - refused by /flowKnockoutMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistribution, on the data-completeness ground. (c) The IRC 72(m)(7) death-or-disability exception, which has no intake anywhere in this dictionary and is therefore NOT applied - a taxpayer-adverse gap, named on /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome.

Whether any of this Form 1099-SA's box 1 distribution was rolled over into another HSA. Ask only when a rollover is a real possibility for this item (a non-death, non-prohibited-transaction code). Help text: a rollover counts ONLY if BOTH of these are true — you deposited the money into another HSA (or the same one) within 60 days of receiving this distribution, AND you have not made another HSA-to-HSA rollover in the 1-year period ending on the day you received this distribution. If either condition fails, answer NO here even if you moved the money between accounts — the amount is a taxable distribution instead, and you cannot roll it over as a substitute for keeping the two conditions. This module holds no distribution date and no record of a filer's other HSAs' rollover history, so the 60-day window and the 1-year once-a-year limit cannot be tested by this graph; the filer's own YES answer to this question is an attestation that both conditions were met, exactly as line 14b is a self-reported figure on the printed form. Unanswered: refused (a rollover cannot be assumed either way). Feeds ../distributionsRolloverAmount and, on an admitted death item, the document/answer contradiction check at ../isAdmittedNonspouseBeneficiaryDeathDistribution and ../isAdmittedEstateDeathDistribution (a nonspouse beneficiary or estate item can be rolled into no HSA, because the account ceased to be one on the date of death).

The dollar amount of this Form 1099-SA's box 1 distribution that was rolled over into another HSA, asked only when ../writableDistributionsRolloverBool is YES. Help text: enter the part of box 1 you rolled over under the same 60-day-and-once-a-year rule the yes/no question describes — do not include any amount you did not both redeposit within 60 days AND that falls within your one rollover per 1-year period. The amount cannot exceed the item's own box 1 gross distribution. Min $0. Unanswered on a YES-answered item: refused, the same data-completeness posture as the yes/no question, because a rollover this graph cannot see the size of cannot be subtracted from line 14a.
