UNANSWERED REFUSES, IT DOES NOT DEFAULT. Every other reading was rejected: defaulting to the filer's most common month, or to self-only, or to the December type, would put a guessed number on Form 1040 line 4b. ../hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCapComputable is complete-safe FALSE without an answer, the cap is then $0 and unused, and ../causesHsaFundingDistributionExcessIncomeUnmodeled refuses the return - the asked-and-not-answered posture that is a correct refusal. Nothing goes Incomplete on the silence.
NO Limit, NO Dependency, DELIBERATELY - a leaf (lint_writable_dependency), on ../writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth's precedent. The consistency relationship it participates in (the transfer month must be a month in which the filer was an eligible individual and not a Medicare month) is expressed as a derived sink, ../hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCapComputable, rather than as a bound here.

Fact.Name: This filer has stated the month of their qualified HSA funding distribution
Fact.Description: Complete-safe reader of ../writableHsaFundingDistributionTransferMonth: TRUE when a month was given, FALSE otherwise. The adverse direction is FALSE, which costs the filer the exclusion and keeps the return refused rather than filing a guess.

Fact.Name: The Line 3 chart amount for the transfer month, i.e. the (C)(i) coverage basis
Fact.Description:
The Form 8889 Line 3 Limitation Chart amount for the month the filer named: ../hsaLine3SelfOnlyMonthAmount or ../hsaLine3FamilyMonthAmount according to that month's post-collapse coverage type, and $0 when that month is an enter-zero month. It is the annual figure the chart prints on a month line, not a twelfth of one, which is why the divide-by-12 happens once at ../hsaHfdCapWorksheetLimitation.
$0 CARRIES A SECOND MEANING HERE and it is deliberate: a $0 transfer month is a month in which the filer was NOT an eligible individual, or was enrolled in Medicare, so no "type of coverage under the high deductible health plan covering the individual at the time of the qualified HSA funding distribution" existed to compute the limitation on. ../hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCapComputable reads that $0 as the substituted chart's own basis - every substituted month row carries it wherever the real Line 3 row is nonzero - so the cap itself resolves to a genuine, computed $0 and the whole transfer stays includible on Form 1040 line 4b through ../hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCap's ordinary LesserOf clamp, argued in full at ../hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCapComputable.
THE MONTH TEST COMES FIRST AND IN ITS OWN Case, so an unanswered intake is never read. The reads below are the shipping chart rows, which are Complete on every return.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) chart, the January row
Fact.Description: The Line 3 Limitation Chart's January row, RE-RUN under the IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) type substitution: the transfer month's amount wherever the shipping row carries one, and $0 wherever the shipping row is an enter-zero month. Testing the shipping row against $0 is what keeps the eligibility and Medicare determinations IDENTICAL to Form 8889 line 3's - only the coverage TYPE moves, which is the only thing (C)(i) moves. The eleven siblings below are the same body on their own month.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) chart, the February row
The (C)(i) chart, the March row
The (C)(i) chart, the April row
The (C)(i) chart, the May row
The (C)(i) chart, the June row
The (C)(i) chart, the July row
The (C)(i) chart, the August row
The (C)(i) chart, the September row
The (C)(i) chart, the October row
The (C)(i) chart, the November row
The (C)(i) chart, the December row
The (C)(i) chart, Total for all months
Fact.Description: The sum of the twelve substituted month rows, i.e. what the Line 3 Limitation Chart's total line would read if every eligible month had carried the transfer month's coverage type. Its shipping twin is ../hsaLine3ChartTotalAllMonths and the two agree for every filer whose eligible months all carry one type.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) chart, Limitation (divide the total by 12)
Fact.Description: The substituted chart's last line. CENTS ARE KEPT AND MUST BE, for ../hsaLine3WorksheetLimitation's reason: the worksheet prints no rounding instruction and Publication 969's own examples publish cents on this row, so no Round wraps this Divide.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) chart under the 223(b)(8)(A) last-month rule
Fact.Description:
The limitation IRC 223(b)(8)(A) produces once the type substitution is applied: the filer is treated as an eligible individual in every month, and under (C)(i) every one of those months carries the TRANSFER month's coverage type - so all twelve rows carry ../hsaFundingDistributionTransferMonthChartAmount and the divide-by-12 returns it unchanged. That is why this fact reads the transfer-month amount directly instead of rebuilding the table, which is ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleAmount's own idiom with December swapped for the transfer month.
THE LAST-MONTH RULE ENTERS BECAUSE 223(b)(8) IS INSIDE SECTION 223(b), which is the subsection (C)(i)(I) points at whole. $0 when the rule does not apply, where it is inert as the floor of the GreaterOf on ../hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCap.

Fact.Name: The IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) substituted coverage type is FAMILY
Fact.Description:
Whether the coverage type in force at the time of the transfer - after the IRC 223(b)(5)(A) collapse, which ../hsaLine3EffectiveCoverageTypeMonthNN already applies - is FAMILY rather than self-only. It is the branch selector for the married arm: a family substituted type takes the 223(b)(5)(B)(ii) equal division, a self-only substituted type does not.
THE TEST IS AN EQUALITY OF TWO CHART AMOUNTS AND THAT IS EXACT, not an approximation. ../hsaFundingDistributionTransferMonthChartAmount can only be one of three values: this filer's ../hsaLine3SelfOnlyMonthAmount, their ../hsaLine3FamilyMonthAmount, or $0 for an unanswered or ineligible month. The self-only figure is $4,300 (or $5,300 with the catch-up inside it) and the family figure is $8,550 (or $9,550), so the two can never collide, and $0 compares false against both - which is the right answer, since a $0 transfer month has no coverage type at all: neither branch of the married arm applies to it, and ../hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCapComputable and ../hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCap compute its cap as $0 directly rather than through either the family or the self-only division.
COMPLETE-SAFE OFF-POPULATION: both operands are Complete on every return, so this fact is Complete false for a filer who never answered a transfer month.

Fact.Name: An eligible, non-Medicare month in all twelve months
Fact.Description:
Whether the shipping Line 3 Limitation Chart pays a non-zero amount in every one of the twelve months, i.e. whether this filer was an eligible individual on the first day of every month and enrolled in Medicare in none of them. It reads the SHIPPING chart rows rather than the substituted ones so that it is answerable whether or not a transfer month was named.
WHY THE MARRIED ARM NEEDS IT, and it is the difference between a computable figure and a guess. Under the IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) type substitution every eligible month carries the transfer month's coverage type, so when all twelve months are eligible the filer is treated as having ONE type for the whole year - which is exactly the predicate of the Form 8889 Line 6 FIRST bullet ("If you are treated as having family coverage for each month") and, on the self-only side, of the Line 3 list item (6) ("married with self-only HDHP coverage for the entire year"). It also makes the 223(b)(3) catch-up exact: the Additional Contribution Amount Worksheet counts twelve months, which is the Line 7 TIP's printed $1,000, with no partial-month figure to invent.
A MARRIED FILER WITH A GAP MONTH IS REFUSED, NOT APPROXIMATED - see ../hsaHfdCapMarriedArmDerivable.

Fact.Name: The spouse's own HDHP monthly facts, if fully answered, settle spouse eligibility without asking
Fact.Description: Whether the SPOUSE's (the other /filers/* entry's) own twelve-month HDHP coverage vector is fully answered, so /filers/*/spouseIsHsaEligibleIndividual can be DERIVED from it rather than attested through ../writableSpouseIsHsaEligibleIndividual. Reuses ../hsaMonthlyCoverageVectorAnswered on the SPOUSE's own filer entry - the same fact that already asks "has this filer answered all twelve rows", read here about the OTHER filer. This fact does not model MFS: on an MFS return each spouse files a separate return and /flowKnockoutMFSLine6Check governs that population through its own attestation pair; this fact reads only the /primaryFiler and /secondaryFiler pointers an MFJ (or unfiled-jointly-but-married) return populates.

Fact.Name: Spouse eligibility, DERIVED from the spouse's own answered HDHP vector
Fact.Description:
Whether the spouse (the other /filers/* entry) was an IRC 223(c)(1) eligible individual - covered by an HDHP and not enrolled in Medicare - for at least one month, read from the SPOUSE'S OWN monthly facts. Only meaningful where ../spouseIsHsaEligibleIndividualDerivable is true; ../spouseIsHsaEligibleIndividual is what chooses between this fact and the attestation.
SCOPE MATCHES THE ANY-MONTH GRANULARITY of ../hsaLine3HadFamilyCoverageAnyMonth, which is what gates ../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply: this fact asks only whether the spouse was EVER an eligible individual, not whether they were one for every month the collapse applies. A finer per-month join is a NAMED GAP, STATED HERE rather than left implicit: a spouse eligible in some OTHER month but not in the specific month(s) the collapse fires reads TRUE here even though a stricter per-month join might not agree for that month. The error this coarseness can introduce runs the SAME taxpayer-favourable direction as this fact's unanswered default (the division stays on, rather than being denied on a partial mismatch this repo does not test for).
DOES NOT TEST WHETHER THE SPOUSE CAN BE CLAIMED AS A DEPENDENT. Publication 969 lists not being claimable as a dependent among the requirements to be an eligible individual, and IRC 223(b)(6) denies the deduction to such a person, but ../canBeClaimed is read on /filers/*/spouseIsHsaEligibleIndividual directly (its own conjunct), not folded into this derivation, so the dependent test applies uniformly whether the year is derived or attested.

Fact.Name: Was the spouse an HSA-eligible individual
Fact.Description:
SCREEN SPECIFICATION (the application builds this screen from this Description without opening an IRS document).
THE QUESTION: "Was your spouse an eligible individual for HSA purposes at any time in 2025?"
HELP TEXT: "The rules that let married couples share one family HSA contribution limit, and that add $1,000 for a spouse age 55 or older, apply only if BOTH spouses were eligible individuals - covered by a high-deductible health plan, not enrolled in Medicare, and not claimed as someone else's dependent - for at least part of the year. If your spouse had Medicare, other health coverage, or could be claimed as a dependent for the whole year, they were not an eligible individual and your family contribution limit is not divided or adjusted for them." (Paraphrasing Publication 969 (2025), "Caution: The rules for married people apply only if both spouses are eligible individuals."; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p969.pdf, page 6, RIGHT column.)
ASKED WHEN: ../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply's own population - married (filers:/isMarried), with family HDHP coverage in some month (../hsaLine3HadFamilyCoverageAnyMonth) - AND ONLY where ../spouseIsHsaEligibleIndividualDerivable is FALSE, i.e. the spouse's own monthly HDHP coverage vector is not fully answered on this return. Where the spouse's own vector IS fully answered, this question is skipped entirely and the application must not ask it: the answer is derived from what the spouse already told the return (../spouseIsHsaEligibleIndividualFromOwnFacts), and asking a second, possibly-conflicting question would create a document/answer contradiction with no resolution rule.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete-safe TRUE (the married-couple division and catch-up diversion apply) - not because a spouse is presumptively eligible in any statutory sense, but because defaulting the other way would withhold, on silence, a division most married HSA-contributing couples are entitled to. The division only stops once the filer affirmatively answers NO (or the spouse's own facts, once fully answered, show no eligible month).
VALIDATION: Boolean yes/no.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: ../spouseIsHsaEligibleIndividual, which in turn is a conjunct of ../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply (the IRC 223(b)(5) married-only refinements of the 408(d)(9)(C)(i) HSA-funding-distribution exclusion cap). A NO answer stops the equal division and the Line 3 Note's catch-up diversion from applying to this filer, so the full, undivided family limitation (plus this filer's own catch-up, undiverted) governs instead.

Fact.Name: Whether the spouse is an HSA-eligible individual (Pub. 969 married-couple Caution)
Fact.Description:
The spouse-eligibility conjunct of ../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply. Pub. 969's Caution reads "The rules for married people apply only if both spouses are eligible individuals"; without this test the IRC 223(b)(5) equal division and the Line 3 Note's catch-up diversion would fire for a married filer whose spouse was Medicare-enrolled, otherwise covered, or a dependent, halving a limitation the statute says should not be divided at all.
THREE ARMS, IN ORDER. (1) NOT A DEPENDENT, tested directly rather than asked: Publication 969 makes not being claimable as a dependent a requirement of eligible-individual status, and ../canBeClaimed is already known return-wide once the dependents section is answered, so this arm costs no extra question. (2) DERIVED, where the spouse's own twelve- month HDHP vector is fully answered (../spouseIsHsaEligibleIndividualDerivable): the spouse told the return whether they had HDHP coverage each month, and ../spouseIsHsaEligibleIndividualFromOwnFacts reads it directly - a second, attested answer would risk contradicting the spouse's own coverage rows. (3) ATTESTED, where the spouse's vector is not fully answered: ../writableSpouseIsHsaEligibleIndividual, complete-safe TRUE (see that writable's own Description for why).
THE DEPENDENT ARM APPLIES REGARDLESS OF THE OTHER TWO: a spouse cannot be an eligible individual while claimable as a dependent, so this fact is the dependent test ANDed with the derived-or-attested Switch, rather than folding the dependent test into either branch separately.

Fact.Name: The two married-only refinements of Form 8889 line 3 bite for this filer
Fact.Description:
Whether this filer is one of a married couple who, after the IRC 223(b)(5)(A) collapse, held family coverage in at least one month, AND whose spouse is (derivably or attestedly) an HSA-eligible individual. That predicate pair is what turns BOTH married-only refinements on, and the dictionary already proves the coverage half: it is precisely the conjunction ../hsaLine3AdditionalContributionIncluded negates, so when this fact is TRUE the shipping Line 3 chart amounts carry NO 223(b)(3) catch-up (the Line 3 Note moved it to line 7) and the IRC 223(b)(5)(B) equal division is live; when it is FALSE the catch-up rides inside the chart amounts exactly as it does for an unmarried filer and no division applies, because 223(b)(5) opens "if either spouse has family coverage" and neither spouse has any - or because the spouse is not an eligible individual (../spouseIsHsaEligibleIndividual), and Pub. 969's own Caution says the married rules "apply only if both spouses are eligible individuals".
THE /isMarried READ IS FENCED WITH IsComplete, so a return that has not answered marital status resolves Complete false here rather than Incomplete.
THE SPOUSE-ELIGIBILITY CONJUNCT. The spouse's coverage reaches this fact through the return-level collapse /hsaLine3MarriedFamilyCollapseMonthNN, which ../hsaLine3HadFamilyCoverageAnyMonth consumes, and the collapse fires whenever EITHER spouse has family coverage, without asking whether the SPOUSE (as opposed to the reading filer) is otherwise eligible - not Medicare-enrolled, not claimable as a dependent. Pub. 969 (2025) carries an explicit Caution beside the married-couple rules this fact turns on - "The rules for married people apply only if both spouses are eligible individuals" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p969.pdf, page 6, RIGHT column). Without the conjunct a married filer whose spouse fails that test would resolve TRUE here, halving a limitation the Caution says should not be divided at all - understating this filer's (C)(i) exclusion cap and overstating Form 1040 line 4b. ../spouseIsHsaEligibleIndividual supplies it: derived from the spouse's OWN monthly HDHP facts where fully answered, from ../writableSpouseIsHsaEligibleIndividual (complete-safe TRUE until answered NO) otherwise, and ANDed with Not(spouse ../canBeClaimed) regardless of branch. NAMED RESIDUAL, not built here: the SAME Caution is very likely live on the real-basis Line 3/Line 6 chain too - /hsaLine3MarriedFamilyCollapseMonthNN's own Description calls the Caution "satisfied structurally... a spouse whose month type is family is by construction an eligible individual", which tests only that the spouse answered a coverage TYPE, not that they clear the Medicare or dependent prongs of IRC 223(c)(1). That gap is on the shipping chain and is not closed by this fact.

Fact.Name: The married refinements of the (C)(i) cap are derivable for this filer
Fact.Description:
Conjunct (c) of ../hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCapComputable. It is TRUE on every return: of its four arms, arms 1, 3 and 4 cover every return between them.
(1) THE REFINEMENTS DO NOT BITE. ../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply is false - an unmarried filer, or a married filer with no family coverage in any month. Neither the equal division nor the Line 3 Note reaches them, so the substituted chart is the whole answer.
(2) THE REFINEMENTS BITE AND BOTH ARE COMPUTABLE. The filer was an eligible, non-Medicare individual in all twelve months (../hsaHfdCapEligibleEveryMonth) AND the couple was married on the first day of every month (/hsaMarriedEveryMonth). Under the type substitution the first makes the filer treated as having ONE coverage type for the entire year, which is the Line 6 FIRST bullet's predicate on the family side and the Line 3 item (6) predicate on the self-only side; the second is what makes the couple's shared limitation the couple's for the whole of that year. The shipping ../hsaLine3EqualDivisionApplies and ../hsaLine6EqualDivisionApplies both carry /hsaMarriedEveryMonth for the same reason.
(3) THE NON-UNIFORM AND MID-YEAR-MARRIAGE YEARS: ../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply AND Not(LastMonthRuleAmount greater than WorksheetLimitation).
(4) THE DEEMED YEAR: ../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply AND the same GreaterThan UNNEGATED (../hsaHfdCapDeemedYearGoverns).
COMPLETE-SAFE: every operand is Complete on every return.
THIS FACT IS A TAUTOLOGY, AND THAT IS AN HONEST STATEMENT RATHER THAN A SMELL. Arm 1 is Not(../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply), and arms 3 and 4 split its complement on one GreaterThan, so arms 1, 3 and 4 cover every return; arm 2 is subsumed by arm 3 - an EligibleEveryMonth filer's twelve substituted rows all carry the transfer month's amount, so their worksheet limitation IS that amount and the last-month-rule amount can never exceed it. A MARRIED filer is therefore never refused here, and what remains of the (C)(i) residual is carried by the OTHER three conjuncts of ../hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCapComputable.
A TAUTOLOGY IS NOT A PRICING GUARANTEE. Pub. 969 (2025): "The rules for married people apply only if both spouses are eligible individuals" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p969.pdf, page 6, RIGHT column). That condition is tested in ../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply, through ../spouseIsHsaEligibleIndividual, and not here.
THE FOUR ARMS ARE KEPT RATHER THAN COLLAPSED TO True, because each names the population it serves - the unmarried filer, the uniform married year, the non-uniform and mid-year-marriage years, the deemed year - and collapsing them would leave the next reader unable to tell a tautology that is EARNED from one that was always there. The residual population (iii), the 223(b)(5)(B)(ii) different division by agreement, has no writable anywhere in this dictionary, and is not an arm of this fact because the equal division is the only computable reading.

Fact.Name: The Line 6 SECOND-bullet refigure is derivable on the substituted basis
Fact.Description:
The THIRD arm of ../hsaHfdCapMarriedArmDerivable, and the branch selector for the substituted twin of the Form 8889 Line 6 SECOND bullet. TRUE for a married filer whose family coverage bit at some point in the year (../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply) and whose substituted limitation comes from the CHART rather than from IRC 223(b)(8)(A).
THE SECOND CONJUNCT COMPARES TWO ROUTES; IT DOES NOT ASK WHETHER THE LAST-MONTH RULE APPLIES. ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleApplies asks only about December 1, so it is TRUE for the large majority of eligible married filers - including every filer the EligibleEveryMonth arm above already serves - and gating on it would refuse almost everyone this fact exists to free. What matters is whether the rule ELEVATES the figure. Where ../hsaHfdCapLastMonthRuleAmount does not exceed ../hsaHfdCapWorksheetLimitation the chart total governs, the twelve substituted rows are the months the filer actually had, and Step 1's "the total of the worksheet amounts only for the months you were treated as having family coverage" decomposes them exactly.
THE EQUALITY CASE IS INSIDE THE SERVED POPULATION AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. GreaterThan is used rather than GreaterOrEqual because a mid-year marriage with full-year eligibility lands exactly on equality: under the substitution every eligible month carries the transfer month's amount, so twelve eligible months make ../hsaHfdCapWorksheetLimitation equal to that amount and ../hsaHfdCapLastMonthRuleAmount equal to it as well. That filer is the largest slice of the population this fact frees. The same identity is why this conjunct NEVER narrows the arm above it: an EligibleEveryMonth filer's last-month-rule amount can never exceed their worksheet limitation, so no filer that arm serves is excluded by it, and Any only ever widens.
ONE QUANTITY, ONE FACT - THE SHIPPING SIBLING IS A DIFFERENT QUANTITY AND WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleIncreasedLimitation asks the SAME question on the SHIPPING basis ("whether the last-month-rule amount strictly exceeds the worksheet limitation") and is deliberately not reused here: its operands are ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleAmount and ../hsaLine3WorksheetLimitation, which carry each month's OWN coverage type, while this fact's operands carry the transfer month's type in every month. The two disagree for exactly the filers this fact exists to serve, so borrowing it would import the wrong month set. The substituted pair is a genuinely distinct quantity, not a twin of an existing one.
COMPLETE-SAFE, AND NO IsComplete IS OWED. Both operands of the GreaterThan are Derived Dollar facts built from the substituted chart rows and ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleApplies, every one of which is Complete on every return; ../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply carries the only cross-filer read on this path and keeps its own fence.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) limitation runs over the DEEMED twelve-month year, not the chart's months
Fact.Description:
The substituted twin of ../hsaLine6DeemedFamilyYearGoverns, and the branch selector for "a filer who became an eligible individual late enough in the year that December's rate, annualized by 223(b)(8)(A), STRICTLY EXCEEDS the literal chart total". For that filer the months the four steps have to count are the DEEMED months, not the chart's.
IT IS THE EXACT COMPLEMENT OF ../hsaHfdCapNonUniformArmDerivable INSIDE THE MARRIED POPULATION, by construction rather than by coincidence: that fact is All(../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply, Not(GreaterThan(LastMonthRuleAmount, WorksheetLimitation))) and this one is All(the same first conjunct, the same GreaterThan UNNEGATED). The two exhaust the married population, which is why ../hsaHfdCapMarriedArmDerivable is a tautology with this fact appended to it - stated there rather than hidden.
WHY THE NAME DROPS "FAMILY". ../hsaLine6DeemedFamilyYearGoverns names a deemed year of FAMILY coverage because Form 8889 Line 6 only ever runs on a filer who had family coverage. Under the IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) substitution the deemed year carries the TRANSFER month's type, which may be self-only, so the deeming here is about the MONTH SET and not about the type. The type is answered once, return-wide, by ../hsaHfdCapTransferMonthIsFamily, exactly as it is for ../hsaHfdCapSharedFamilyMonthsChartTotal.
THE TWIN'S Not(/hsaMarriedEveryMonth) CONJUNCT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, AND ITS WORK IS DONE BY CASE ORDER. The Line 6 twin needs that conjunct because its consumers are the Line 6 FIRST bullet and the SECOND bullet's month set, and something has to send a couple married every month to the first. Here ../hsaHfdCapEqualDivisionApplies is Case 1 of ../hsaHfdCapDividedLimitation and already carries /hsaMarriedEveryMonth, so this fact answers only "is the year the deemed one" and the Switch answers "which bullet". Writing the marital test twice would be one predicate in two places.
DECEMBER'S ELIGIBILITY IS INSIDE THE GreaterThan AND IS NOT TESTED AGAIN. ../hsaHfdCapLastMonthRuleAmount is $0 unless ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleApplies, and $0 can never strictly exceed ../hsaHfdCapWorksheetLimitation, which is a sum of non-negative rows over 12. A Medicare-onset filer is therefore outside this fact by construction - the Medicare latch makes ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleApplies false - which is the same reading ../hsaHfdCapNonUniformArmDerivable already records for its own conjunct.
THE PRORATION DISPUTE IS INERT ON THIS POPULATION, which is worth recording because every other dollar-bearing fact in this family carries interpretation:provisional for it. The two readings of the (C)(i) ceiling separate only a filer whose line 3 is NOT already lifted to the flat annual figure by the 223(b)(8)(A) last-month rule; every filer this fact is true for is lifted by it, by the definition of the GreaterThan. Both readings give the same number here.
COMPLETE-SAFE, and no IsComplete is owed on it or written. Both operands of the GreaterThan are Derived Dollar facts that are hard $0 on a return that never answered the monthly vector, and ../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply carries the only cross-filer read on this path behind its own fence. An IsComplete on a complete-safe fact is always true.

Fact.Name: IRC 223(b)(5)(B)(ii) divides this filer's (C)(i) limitation in half
Fact.Description:
The equal division is the branch this filer takes for the 408(d)(9)(C)(i) cap: the married refinements bite, the arm is derivable, and the substituted coverage type is FAMILY.
THE SELF-ONLY BRANCH IS NOT AN INFERENCE, IT IS THE LINE 6 SECOND BULLET RUN TO ITS END. Where the substituted type is self-only, no month is a month the filer is "treated as having family coverage", so Step 1's refigured limit is $0, Step 2 divides $0, Step 3 subtracts the spouse's $0 share from that $0, and Step 4 adds back "any other contribution limits that apply for the tax year" - the whole self-only figure, undivided. The statute reads the same way: 223(b)(5) is conditioned on "if either spouse has family coverage", and a post-collapse self-only transfer month is a month in which neither spouse had any.
IT KEYS ON MARRIAGE, NOT ON THE JOINT RETURN. 223(b)(5) says "In the case of individuals who are married to each other" and the Line 6 instruction says "Spouses who have separate HSAs"; neither mentions the filing status, and the shipping ../hsaLine3EqualDivisionApplies and ../hsaLine6EqualDivisionApplies read filers:/isMarried for exactly that reason. A married-filing-separately filer divides. No filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ gate appears here, and none is owed, because no /secondaryFiler fact is read on this path.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) chart, Line 6 Step 1 - the shared family months only
Fact.Description:
The substituted twin of ../hsaLine6SharedFamilyMonthsChartTotal: the total of the substituted chart's month rows, counting ONLY the months in which this filer was treated as having family coverage AND was married to the other spouse on the first day of the month. Step 1 of the Form 8889 Line 6 SECOND bullet asks for exactly that restricted total, and the worksheet's own divide-by-12 is applied to it at ../hsaHfdCapStep1RefiguredLine3.
THE PER-MONTH TEST IS NOT THE SHIPPING ONE AND CANNOT BE. The real chain tests a per-month coverage-type enum (../hsaLine3EffectiveCoverageTypeMonthNN equals family). Under the IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) substitution there is no per-month type left to test: every eligible month carries the transfer month's type, so the type question is answered once, return-wide, by ../hsaHfdCapTransferMonthIsFamily. What remains per month is WHICH MONTHS COUNT, and that is two tests: the month was an eligible, non-Medicare month (../hsaHfdCapChartAmountMonthNN above $0, which is the same literal eligibility the shipping chart row determines - the substituted row is $0 in exactly the months the shipping row is), and the couple was married on its first day (/hsaMarriedOnFirstDayMonthNN).
A SELF-ONLY SUBSTITUTED TYPE MAKES THIS $0 FOR ALL TWELVE MONTHS BY CONSTRUCTION, and that is the reading rather than a missing branch: with no month treated as having family coverage, Steps 1 through 3 all resolve $0 and Step 4 returns the whole substituted worksheet limitation undivided - the Line 6 SECOND bullet run to its end, which is the answer ../hsaHfdCapEqualDivisionApplies already argues for that population.
COMPLETE-SAFE: the twelve substituted rows are Complete on every return, /hsaMarriedOnFirstDayMonthNN falls back to filers:/isMarried behind its own IsComplete, and ../hsaHfdCapTransferMonthIsFamily is Complete false off-population. No fence is owed here and none is written.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) chart, Line 6 Step 1 - the month set Step 1 counts, DEEMED year included
Fact.Description:
The substituted twin of ../hsaLine6Step1MonthSetChartTotal, and the number Step 1 refigures the substituted line 3 from: "the total of the worksheet amounts only for the months you were treated as having family coverage", intersected with the months of the marriage because IRC 223(b)(5) shares a limitation only between "individuals who are married to each other". Outside the deemed year it is ../hsaHfdCapSharedFamilyMonthsChartTotal.
IT DIVERGES ON ONE POPULATION, the one ../hsaHfdCapDeemedYearGoverns names: a married filer whose December rate, annualized by IRC 223(b)(8)(A), strictly exceeds the literal substituted chart total. There the months the filer is "treated as having family coverage" are not the chart's - the Line 3 narrative rule 2 treats them as holding December's plan for the entire year and the (C)(i) substitution replaces its TYPE with the transfer month's - so Step 1's total is the transfer month's chart amount counted once for each month of the marriage.
THE AMOUNT COUNTED IS ../hsaFundingDistributionTransferMonthChartAmount AND NOT DECEMBER'S ROW, and that is the one place this fact departs from its Line 6 twin. The twin's deemed arm counts ../hsaLine3ChartAmountMonth12 because on the REAL basis rule 2 deems December's own coverage. Under 408(d)(9)(C)(i) the basis is "the type of coverage ... at the time of the qualified HSA funding distribution", so every deemed month carries the TRANSFER month's amount. Where the transfer month IS December the two readings coincide; where it is not, only this one is the statute's. The shipping ../hsaHfdCapLastMonthRuleAmount already rests on the same substitution, so no new claim is made here.
THE PER-MONTH FAMILY TEST IS THE RETURN-WIDE ONE, for the reason ../hsaHfdCapSharedFamilyMonthsChartTotal records: under the substitution there is no per-month type left to test, so ../hsaHfdCapTransferMonthIsFamily answers it once. A SELF-ONLY SUBSTITUTED TYPE THEREFORE MAKES THIS $0 FOR ALL TWELVE MONTHS, Steps 1 to 3 resolve $0, and Step 4 returns the whole deemed limitation undivided - the Line 6 SECOND bullet run to its end, which is the same answer the chart-governs basis gives.
NO ELIGIBILITY TEST APPEARS IN THE DEEMED ARM, and its absence is the deeming itself. Under 223(b)(8)(A)(i) the filer "shall be treated ... as having been an eligible individual during each of the months in such taxable year", so there is no ineligible month left to exclude; the only per-month question is the marital one. That is the same identity ../hsaHfdCapLastMonthRuleAmount is built on, applied to the month set rather than to the total.
WHY A SEPARATE FACT AND NOT A WIDENING OF ../hsaHfdCapSharedFamilyMonthsChartTotal. The same separation, for the same reason, that put ../hsaLine6Step1MonthSetChartTotal beside ../hsaLine6SharedFamilyMonthsChartTotal: the literal restricted total is still asked for by committed node tests at that meaning (hsa-hfd-cap-nonuniform-joint-return-both-spouses-now-compute and -mid-year-marriage-shares-only-the-married-months both pin it at $51,300.00), so the deeming is composed beside it rather than folded into it. What differs is which total Step 1 divides.
COMPLETE-SAFE. The gate is complete-safe false, so an unanswered return takes the else arm and this fact is ../hsaHfdCapSharedFamilyMonthsChartTotal, a hard $0 on a return that never answered the monthly vector.

Fact.Name: The whole-year substituted chart total the four steps decompose, DEEMED year included
Fact.Description:
The substituted twin of ../hsaLine6ChartTotalAllMonths: the twelve-month total ../hsaHfdCapStep4OtherContributionLimits takes its remainder out of. Outside the deemed year it is ../hsaHfdCapChartTotalAllMonths. On the deemed year ../hsaHfdCapDeemedYearGoverns names, it is the transfer month's chart amount counted twelve times, which is exactly twelve times ../hsaHfdCapLastMonthRuleAmount and therefore twelve times that filer's substituted line 3.
WHY STEP 4 NEEDS IT, and it is the property that makes a deemed filer decomposable at all. Step 4's "any other contribution limits that apply for the tax year" are read by this dictionary as the months Step 1 excluded, and for a deemed filer those months are deemed too: their limitation for January is the transfer month's plan, not the nothing the substituted chart records. Reading ../hsaHfdCapChartTotalAllMonths here would subtract a shared total built out of deemed months from a whole-year total built out of real ones, and the two halves would not sum to the filer's own limitation. With this fact they do: (this total less ../hsaHfdCapStep1MonthSetChartTotal) / 12 plus that total / 12 is the deemed limitation itself, which is the identity the four steps need.
THE ARITHMETIC IS THE ONE ../hsaHfdCapLastMonthRuleAmount ALREADY SHIPS, not a new claim: twelve rows each carrying the transfer month's amount, divided by 12, is that amount. The Add of twelve identical rows is written out rather than multiplied because every other total in this family is summed that way and a reader comparing them should see the same shape.
COMPLETE-SAFE for the same reason as its sibling: the gate is complete-safe false and the else arm is a hard $0 on an unanswered return.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) chart, Line 6 Step 1 - the refigured line 3
Fact.Description:
Step 1's month-set total (../hsaHfdCapStep1MonthSetChartTotal) divided by 12: what the substituted line 3 would have been had the worksheet counted only those months. CENTS ARE KEPT AND NO Round WRAPS THIS Divide, for ../hsaHfdCapWorksheetLimitation's reason - the worksheet prints no rounding instruction and Publication 969's own examples publish cents on this row.
THE LAST-MONTH RULE IS NOT APPLIED HERE AS A GREATER-OF. Step 1 names the number it wants ("the total of the worksheet amounts"), so it displaces the rule-4 greater-of that ../hsaHfdCapDividedLimitation's other arms carry. Where the substituted limitation comes from IRC 223(b)(8)(A) instead of the chart, the deeming enters through the month set itself: ../hsaHfdCapDeemedYearGoverns selects the deemed month set in ../hsaHfdCapStep1MonthSetChartTotal, the substituted twin of the real chain's ../hsaLine6DeemedFamilyYearGoverns and ../hsaLine6Step1MonthSetChartTotal.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) chart, Line 6 Step 1 - the refigured line 5
Fact.Description: The refigured line 3 less line 4, floored at zero, which is line 5's own printed arithmetic. THE ARCHER SUBTRAHEND IS NOT REFIGURED WITH IT and the step says so: "When refiguring line 5, use the same amount you previously entered on line 4" - so the same ../hsaLine4ArcherMsaContributions the shipping ../hsaLine6Step1RefiguredLine5 uses is subtracted here unchanged. NOTE the consequence, named rather than left to be found: because the whole of line 4 is subtracted inside the shared part, the Archer reduction is effectively halved for this population, which is what the printed step says to do and is the same consequence the real chain already carries. It is inert on every committed return, since ../hsaLine4ArcherMsaContributions is complete-safe $0 without an Archer MSA.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) chart, Line 6 Step 2 - the spouse's half of the refigured limit
Fact.Description: Step 2 divides the Step 1 amount equally between the spouses. THE "DIFFERENT ALLOCATION" THE STEP ALSO ALLOWS IS NOT OFFERED: this dictionary has no writable for it, so the equal split is imposed rather than chosen. That gap is pre-existing - it is the same gap ../hsaLine6Step2SpouseShare names for the real chain and the same population (iii) the /flowHsaContributionsOverLimitKnockout contract calls an application intake rather than a document - and this fact neither widens nor closes it. NO Round, for ../hsaHfdCapDividedLimitation's reason: the whole-dollar convention is elected once, downstream.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) chart, Line 6 Step 3 - Step 1 less the spouse's share
Fact.Description: Step 3 subtracts "the part of the contribution limit allocated to your spouse in Step 2 from the amount determined in Step 1". It is written as the printed subtraction rather than as a second halving so that a Step 1 amount with an odd half-cent lands wholly on this filer instead of being rounded twice - the same reason ../hsaLine6Step3OwnShare gives.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) chart, Line 6 Step 4 - the other contribution limits that apply
Fact.Description:
Step 4 says to "determine any other contribution limits that apply for the tax year and add that amount to the result in Step 3". THE READING IS THE SHIPPING CHAIN'S, carried across the substitution unchanged: the months Step 1 excluded are the months whose limitation is this filer's alone - nobody else's coverage put a limit on them - so the "other contribution limits" are the substituted worksheet amounts for exactly those months, divided by 12 like every other worksheet total.
NO IRS EXAMPLE WORKS THESE STEPS NUMERICALLY and none works them on the substituted basis, so every figure here is derived from the printed chart amounts by this dictionary and is labelled ai-only.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) limitation under the Line 6 SECOND bullet - Step 3 plus Step 4
Fact.Description:
"Enter the total on line 6", on the IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) substituted basis. THE LANDING FACT OF THE NON-UNIFORM ARM: the substituted twin of ../hsaLine6NonUniformFamilyMonthsAmount, and what ../hsaHfdCapDividedLimitation reads for a married filer whose family-coverage months and eligible months do not fill the year.
IT IS THE LIMITATION ONLY AND THE CATCH-UP IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN IT. IRC 223(b)(5)(B) operates on the paragraph (1) limitation "without regard to any additional contribution amount under paragraph (3)", so the 223(b)(3) amount is added afterwards by ../hsaHfdCapCatchUpAmount - the same separation of concerns the ../hsaHfdCapDividedLimitation / ../hsaHfdCapCatchUpAmount split already uses, and the same one ../hsaLine6NonUniformFamilyMonthsAmount gets structurally from ../hsaLine3AdditionalContributionIncluded being false for this whole population.
NOT ROUNDED, matching ../hsaHfdCapDividedLimitation's other arms and the cents-keeping worksheet above it.

Fact.Name: The (C)(i) limitation after the IRC 223(b)(5)(B) reduction and division
Fact.Description:
The substituted annual limitation as 223(b)(5)(B) leaves it, and the catch-up is deliberately NOT in it: (B) operates on the paragraph (1) limitation "after the application of subparagraph (A) and without regard to any additional contribution amount under paragraph (3)". The 223(b)(3) amount is added afterwards, by ../hsaHfdCapCatchUpAmount, which is why these are two facts and not one.
THE SENTENCE IS TAKEN WHOLE. (B)(i) reduces by "the aggregate amount paid to Archer MSAs of such spouses for the taxable year" and only then does (B)(ii) divide, so the same subtrahend Form 8889 line 5 subtracts - ../hsaLine4ArcherMsaContributions - is subtracted here, floored at zero on line 5's own printed floor. Taking (B)(ii) without (B)(i) would overstate the cap for an MSA-contributing married couple, which is the taxpayer-favourable direction. The subtrahend is complete-safe $0 whenever /archerMsaOnThisReturn is false, so no return without an Archer MSA moves by a cent.
THE REDUCTION IS INSIDE THE DIVIDED BRANCH ONLY, and that is a reading rather than an oversight. The undivided branch keeps the substituted chart arithmetic exactly, because (C)(i)(I) points at the limitation "computed on the basis of the type of coverage", which the Form 8889 Line 10 instruction states as age and coverage and nothing else; 223(b)(4)'s reductions for contributions actually made are not in it. (B)(i) is applied where it is applied because it is the same sentence (B)(ii) supplies, and because 223(b)(4)'s own flush text switches subparagraph (A) off for an individual to whom paragraph (5) applies.
NO ROUND. Cents are kept for ../hsaLine6EqualDivisionHalfShare's reason: no printed rounding instruction on the division, and the whole-dollar convention is elected once, downstream.
THE FOUR STEPS COMPUTE THE FIRST BULLET'S OWN ANSWER ON THE MARRIED-EVERY-MONTH DEEMED FILER, and that identity was checked rather than assumed: with twelve deemed family months all inside the marriage, Step 1's month set is the whole substituted total, Step 4's remainder is $0, and Step 3 is half of (the deemed limitation less line 4), which is Case 1 to the cent. Case 1 still wins for that filer by order, because the Line 6 instruction puts them in the FIRST bullet and the fact names should say so.

Fact.Name: The 223(b)(3) additional contribution amount, summed over the eligible months
Fact.Description:
$1,000 for each month in which this filer was an eligible, non-Medicare individual, summed the way every other total in this family is summed - twelve month arms and an Add - so that ../hsaHfdCapProratedCatchUpAmount can divide it by 12 exactly as the worksheet divides its own total.
THE MONTH TEST IS ELIGIBILITY AND NOT FAMILY COVERAGE, and that is the same statutory reading ../hsaHfdCapCatchUpAmount's flat arm already stands on rather than a new one. 223(b)(3)(A) increases "the applicable limitation under subparagraphs (A) and (B) of paragraph (2)" - the MONTHLY limitation, self-only and family alike - and 223(b)(1) sums the monthly limitations over the months the individual is an eligible individual. That chain is TYPE-BLIND, which is what the 408(d)(9)(C)(i) substitution needs.
THE ROW READ IS THE SUBSTITUTED ONE AND IT DOES NOT MATTER WHICH. ../hsaHfdCapChartAmountMonthNN is above $0 in exactly the months ../hsaLine3ChartAmountMonthNN is, by that fact's own body, so this total is the literal eligible-month count either way; the substituted row is read because every other member of this family reads it.
COMPLETE-SAFE: the twelve rows are Complete on every return and the constant is a constant. The age-55 test is NOT here - it lives on ../hsaHfdCapProratedCatchUpAmount, with the same IsComplete fence the flat arm uses, so that this fact stays one quantity.

Fact.Name: The IRC 223(b)(3) catch-up prorated to this filer's eligible months
Fact.Description:
$1,000 times the eligible months over twelve: the 223(b)(3)(A) increase run through 223(b)(1)'s own sum for a filer whose eligible months do NOT fill the year, which is the case ../hsaHfdCapCatchUpAmount's flat arm could not reach and answered with $0.
IT IS AN EXTENSION OF THE SHIPPING READING, NOT A NEW ONE. ../hsaHfdCapCatchUpAmount already argues the whole figure from 223(b)(3)(A) plus 223(b)(1) - "the applicable limitation ... shall be increased by the additional contribution amount", summed "for months during such taxable year that the individual is an eligible individual" - and observes that the chain gives $1,000 x 12 / 12 = $1,000 flat on twelve eligible months. Ten eligible months give $1,000 x 10 / 12 = $833.33 by the same sentence. Nothing about that argument was specific to twelve; the flat arm was flat because its Case was reached only when ../hsaHfdCapEligibleEveryMonth held.
THE $0 IT REPLACES WAS TAXPAYER-ADVERSE, WHICH IS WHY IT WAS SAFE TO SHIP AND IS STILL WRONG. A gap-month filer's cap was understated by the whole catch-up, overstating Form 1040 line 4b.
THE AGE-55 FENCE IS THE FLAT ARM'S, COPIED VERBATIM. filers:../age55OrOlder is read behind IsComplete because it is a writable-backed read; 223(b)(3)(A) keys the amount to "an individual who has attained age 55", so it is this filer's own age and never the spouse's, and 223(b)(5)(B) divides the limitation "without regard to any additional contribution amount under paragraph (3)" so it is never halved.
NOT ROUNDED. Cents are kept for ../hsaHfdCapWorksheetLimitation's reason; the whole-dollar convention is elected once, downstream.

Fact.Name: The IRC 223(b)(3) additional contribution amount inside the (C)(i) cap
Fact.Description:
The age-55 catch-up this filer's cap gets ON TOP of ../hsaHfdCapDividedLimitation, and it is $0 for everyone except the married filers whose chart amounts do not already carry it.
WHY IT IS $0 ALMOST EVERYWHERE. When ../hsaHfdCapMarriedRefinementsApply is false, ../hsaLine3AdditionalContributionIncluded is true for every age-55 filer, so the $1,000 already rides inside ../hsaLine3SelfOnlyMonthAmount and ../hsaLine3FamilyMonthAmount, hence inside every substituted chart row this cap sums. Adding it again here would double it.
WHY IT IS $1,000 EXACTLY, AND THE GROUND IS THE STATUTE RATHER THAN THE LINE 7 WORKSHEET. 223(b)(3)(A) increases "the applicable limitation under subparagraphs (A) and (B) of paragraph (2)" - the MONTHLY limitation, self-only and family alike - by the additional contribution amount, for an individual who attained age 55 before the close of the year; 223(b)(1) then sums the monthly limitations over the months the individual is an eligible individual. This Case is reached only when ../hsaHfdCapEligibleEveryMonth holds, so that sum runs over twelve months and the increase is $1,000 x 12 / 12 = $1,000 flat. That chain is TYPE-BLIND, which is exactly what the 408(d)(9)(C)(i) substitution needs: it holds on the self-only substituted basis word for word as it does on the family one. Publication 969 states the same ceiling in the Service's words as coverage "plus any additional contribution to which you are entitled".
THE LINE 7 WORKSHEET IS NOT THAT GROUND AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT CITED AS ONE. Its item (1) is "You or your spouse had family coverage under an HDHP and were, or were considered to be, an eligible individual on the first day of the month", so the worksheet counts FAMILY months, not eligible months, and on the self-only branch those are different numbers.
THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, RECORDED FOR THE ANALYSIS. The Line 3 Note keys on ACTUAL coverage - "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3" - and that predicate survives the type substitution untouched, because it asks about the year the filer actually had rather than about the hypothetical basis (C)(i) builds. Read that way the catch-up never enters the substituted line 3 at all; it sits on a line 7 computed from ACTUAL family months (itself subject to the rule 2 deeming, exactly as the substituted chain is) - a divergence between the two readings survives only on a return whose TRANSFER month's substituted type disagrees with its DECEMBER's real-basis type (e.g. a family transfer month with a self-only or Medicare December), which no committed fixture exercises for THIS cap. THIS FACT TAKES THE STATUTORY READING, because 408(d)(9)(C)(i)(I) points at "the annual limitation under section 223(b)" and not at a Form 8889 line, and because the Line 3 Note is a presentation rule for the return the filer actually files rather than for the hypothetical limitation the cap is computed on. The alternative is the SMALLER, taxpayer-adverse figure, which is why the divergence is recorded here and on the contract instead of being settled silently, and why this fact and ../hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCap keep interpretation:provisional.
IT IS NEVER HALVED AND IT IS NEVER THE SPOUSE'S. 223(b)(5)(B) divides the limitation "without regard to any additional contribution amount under paragraph (3)", and the printed instruction says the same in the Service's words: "The $1,000 additional contribution amount is not allocable among spouses, unlike the $8,550 family contribution". 223(b)(3)(A) keys it to "an individual who has attained age 55", so the read is this filer's own filers:../age55OrOlder, IsComplete-fenced, and never the spouse's.
WHY FLAT AND NOT ../hsaHfdCapProratedCatchUpAmount, which is the arm this population would otherwise have fallen through to $0 past. The proration is 223(b)(1)'s sum over "months during such taxable year that the individual is an eligible individual", counted by ../hsaHfdCapCatchUpMonthsChartTotal from the substituted chart rows. On a deemed year IRC 223(b)(8)(A)(i) makes every month such a month, so the sum is twelve of the additional contribution amount and the divide-by-12 returns the whole of it. Routing the deemed filer through the prorated fact would have counted the LITERAL eligible months and charged them a catch-up cut to a twelfth per uncovered month - on a DECEMBER-only filer, $83.33 instead of $1,000.00 - which is the same category error as using the Line 7 worksheet's FAMILY-month count in this chain. The flat constant is written rather than a twelve-row total because a total of twelve identical rows divided by twelve IS the constant, and the shorter expression is the one a reader can check.

Fact.Name: This filer's IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) cap can be computed on this return
Fact.Description:
The population gate on the cap, and the fact that decides whether the last arm of /flowHsaContributionsOverLimitKnockout files or keeps refusing. THREE conjuncts, each of them a real refusal rather than a formality, and every one complete-safe; a transfer month with no coverage is not a fourth refusal but a computed $0, argued below the third.
(a) /hsaLine3VectorGoverns. The (C)(i) basis is a PER-MONTH coverage type, and the monthly vector is the only place this dictionary carries one. Where the vector does not govern, every ../hsaCoverageTypeMonthNN reads its complete-safe `none` default and the substituted chart would total $0 - a cap of zero that would tax the whole transfer off a default nobody answered. This conjunct is what makes that impossible.
(b) ../hsaFundingDistributionTransferMonthAnswered. The month is the intake; its silence refuses.
(c) ../hsaHfdCapMarriedArmDerivable. Two married-only refinements sit between the chart and a married filer's line 3 - the IRC 223(b)(5)(B) equal division and the Line 3 Note that moves the 223(b)(3) catch-up onto Form 8889 line 7 - and this conjunct is the test that both are derivable under the type substitution. It is true for an unmarried filer outright.
A TRANSFER MONTH WITH NO COVERAGE IS NOT A FOURTH CONJUNCT: it is a computable $0. 408(d)(9)(A) opens "In the case of an individual who is an eligible individual (as defined in section 223(c))", and (C)(i)(I) computes the limitation on "the type of coverage under the high deductible health plan covering the individual AT THE TIME OF the ... distribution": a filer who names a month in which no HDHP covered them has named a month with no such type, so the section 223(b) annual limitation this cap substitutes into is $0 for every month. That is not an approximation of the cap, it is the substituted chart's own arithmetic: every ../hsaHfdCapChartAmountMonthNN row reads ../hsaFundingDistributionTransferMonthChartAmount wherever the real Line 3 row is nonzero, so a $0 transfer-month amount drives ../hsaHfdCapChartTotalAllMonths, ../hsaHfdCapWorksheetLimitation, ../hsaHfdCapLastMonthRuleAmount and ../hsaHfdCapCatchUpMonthsChartTotal all to $0 without any special-cased branch - the four-step Line 6 machinery and the 223(b)(3) catch-up read the same substituted rows, so they land on $0 too. ../hsaFundingDistributionExclusionCap is therefore a genuine, computed $0 for this population, not the fact's own not-computable fallback arm. The route out is form1099Rs's existing clamp: ../line4cHfdExclusion (via form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/hfdExclusionCap) is a LesserOf against this cap already, so the whole line 10 amount stays includible on Form 1040 line 4b exactly as an over-the-cap transfer already routes - no new fact and no form1099Rs edit. THE READING IS TAGGED PROVISIONAL because 408(d)(9)(A)'s own opening clause ("In the case of an individual who is an eligible individual") reaches the identical $0-excluded number by a different route - the transfer would not be a "qualified HSA funding distribution" AT ALL rather than one with a $0 cap - which has different consequences for Form 8889 line 10 itself (still reported vs. not a QHFD at all) that this unit does not adjudicate; the cap reading is taken because it leaves line 10 as the filer reported it, which is what ../isSupportedHfdElection and ../line4cHfdExclusion already assume for every other population this fact serves.

Fact.Name: The IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) ceiling on this filer's excluded funding distribution
Fact.Description:
The most of a qualified HSA funding distribution this filer may keep out of gross income: the section 223(b) annual limitation computed on the coverage type in force in the transfer month, which is the substituted chart's Limitation line or, where 223(b)(8)(A) gives more, the last-month-rule amount. The GreaterOf is the Line 3 narrative's own rule 4, carried across the substitution unchanged.
WHAT IT IS NOT: it is not Form 8889 line 8, and the difference is the whole reason this unit exists. Line 8 is the year's contribution limitation with each month's own coverage type; this is the same limitation with the transfer month's type in every month. The two agree for a filer whose type did not change, and where they differ the statute names this one.
The name displayed on the HSA form 8889 used for PDF to combine MFJ names when applicable
Whether the filer has a self-only HDHP.
Whether the filer has a family HDHP.
Whether the filer selected either Self-Only or Family HDHP coverage.
Whether the filer can be considered covered by the family coverage HDHP

Form 8889 Line 1 checkbox for PDF, XML export.
FORM 8889 PART I GATE. Read through ../hsaForm8889PartIRequired, not ../hasMadeContributionsToHsa alone: Part I is also owed to a filer who made no 2025 contributions but carries a prior-year excess into Form 5329 line 42, because Form 5329 line 43 measures the absorption against Form 8889 line 12.
Whether the filer can be considered covered by the self-only coverage HDHP

Form 8889 Line 1 checkbox for PDF, XML export.
FORM 8889 PART I GATE. Read through ../hsaForm8889PartIRequired, not ../hasMadeContributionsToHsa alone: Part I is also owed to a filer who made no 2025 contributions but carries a prior-year excess into Form 5329 line 42, because Form 5329 line 43 measures the absorption against Form 8889 line 12.
The HSA distribution belongs to the primary filer
The HSA distribution belongs to the secondary filer

Fact.Name: Primary Filer HSA distributions

Fact.Description: Primary filer total HSA distributions rollover amount

Fact.Name: Secondary Filer HSA distributions

Fact.Description: Secondary filer total HSA distributions rollover amount

Whether THIS filer is the reason the unqualified-distributions refusal fires: their collection-route Form 8889 line 16 is positive, so they owe the 20%-tax exception attestation, and they have not answered it.
THIS IS THE REFUSAL'S WHOLE CONTENT. The engine computes the printed line 16, routes it to Schedule 1 line 8f, and computes the printed lines 17a/17b — but line 17b is only correct if the exception amount is known, and unanswered reads as 0, which taxes a filer who was over 65 and simply never asked. That is the ONE input the engine cannot supply for itself, so it is the one thing refused.
NOT DERIVABLE, WHICH IS WHY IT IS AN ATTESTATION AND NOT A COMPUTATION: see ../writableHsaCollectionExceptionAmount's own Description. An attested 0 ("no exception applies") clears this fact exactly as an attested full amount does, PROVIDED the reason beside it is answered too — what is refused is a MISSING HALF OF THE PAIR, not a particular answer.
THE ANSWER IS TWO FIELDS, NOT ONE: the amount AND the statutory ground it rests on (../writableHsaCollectionExceptionReason, whose options are the instructions' own three reasons plus "none"). Either one missing refuses, and the conjunction is deliberately symmetric — an amount with no reason behind it is an unsupported number, and a reason with no amount beside it sizes nothing. The only refusal is data-completeness when a required reason or amount is missing.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT REFUSE, so the refusal is bounded and legible: it does not test whether the two answers AGREE (a "none" beside a positive amount is complete), and it does not reach any filer ../flowShouldAskHsaCollectionExceptionAmount does not ask — which excludes every filer whose age already derives the whole exception. The population refused is exactly: asked, with the amount or the reason (or both) unanswered.

Whether any filer on the return has a positive collection-route Form 8889 line 16 with no 20%-tax exception attestation behind it. The return-level form of /filers/*/causesUnattestedTaxableHsaDistributionKnockout, consumed by the per-item leg of /flowKnockoutHsaUnqualifiedDistributions below.

Whether this Form 1099-SA is a reason to refuse the return: it reports a distribution larger than the qualified medical expenses paid out of it AND the taxable amount that results has no 20%-tax exception attestation behind it.
THE SECOND CONJUNCT IS WHAT KEEPS THIS NARROW. The engine computes the tax on the unqualified portion — the printed line 16 routed to Schedule 1 line 8f, and the printed lines 17a/17b routed to Schedule 2 line 17c — so what is refused is only the input the engine cannot supply, the exception attestation (/someFilerOwesHsaExceptionAttestation). Once every filer with a positive line 16 has answered, this item stops causing a refusal and the return COMPUTES.
THE CONJUNCTION IS DELIBERATELY ACROSS DIFFERENT SCOPES, per item on the left and per return on the right, and the direction of that looseness is toward REFUSAL: on an MFJ return where one spouse has the over-spending item and the other has the unattested line 16, the return is refused. The alternative, a purely per-filer refusal, would WIDEN the knockout onto the one-dollar rounding residue named on /filers/*/taxableHsaDistributionTotal, where a filer's line 16 is positive while no item exceeds its own expenses.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT REFUSE, stated so it is not rediscovered as a bug: (a) a filer whose line 16 nets to 0 because a second Form 1099-SA over-spent on medical care - the printed aggregate says no tax is due; (b) every filer who answers the exception questions — the amount AND the statutory reason beside it — including with an amount of 0 and a reason of "none", which together mean "no exception applies".
ADMITTED DEATH ITEMS ARE NEVER A CAUSE. An admitted nonspouse-beneficiary death item of EITHER code, and an admitted estate item, are excluded from this fact by the Not() conjuncts in its own Derived body; the Not() reads the admission, not the code.
WHAT REFUSES ELSEWHERE: a box-3 code this dictionary does not admit (/flowKnockoutHsaDistributionCode; the admitted codes and cases are listed on /filers/*/hsaDistributionNotNormalKnockout) - though the disability and death EXCEPTIONS reach this route as the filer's own attestation on a code-1 distribution: IRC 223(f)(4)(B) does not condition on the box-3 code. See /filers/*/writableHsaCollectionExceptionReason. And a box-4 fair market value on an item that is not admitted (/flowKnockoutHsaDistributionFMV).
ONE GAP THIS FACT DOES NOT CREATE AND DOES NOT CLOSE: i8889 cautions that "You cannot take a deduction on Schedule A (Form 1040) for any amount you include on line 15", and scheduleA /writableMedicalExpenses is a separate intake with no cross-check against ../writableQualifiedMedExpenses. That double-deduction is reachable on any return with a positive line 15 (any 1099-SA fully spent on qualified care), so it is not this fact's in kind; it is named because a reader of this fact will otherwise look for it.

Knockout because some Form 1099-SA in /hsaDistributions reports a distribution larger than the qualified medical expenses the filer paid out of it — i.e. the return carries an unqualified, taxable portion — and the 20%-tax exception attestation behind it is missing. (The box-4 knockout is the sibling /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionFMV; this fact's own dependency is the per-item modifiedDistribution vs writableQualifiedMedExpenses comparison.)
WHAT IT REFUSES lives in the per-item leg above. The engine computes the tax on the unqualified portion: hsa /filers/*/taxableHsaDistributionTotal (printed line 16) computes, /hsaCollectionRouteTaxableDistributions carries it to Schedule 1 line 8f beside the top-level scalar route, and /filers/*/hsaCollectionRouteAdditionalTax20Pct plus /hsaCollectionRouteAdditionalTax20PctTotal carry the printed lines 17a/17b to Schedule 2 line 17c. What the engine cannot supply for itself is the 20%-tax exception amount, so the refusal is exactly /someFilerOwesHsaExceptionAttestation: a filer with a positive line 16 who has not answered BOTH exception questions — the amount and the statutory reason beside it.
WHY THE MISSING ANSWER IS WORTH A REFUSAL AT ALL. Unanswered reads as no exception, which taxes the whole of line 16 at 20%. The box-3 code does not carry the exception grounds: IRC 223(f)(4)(B) excepts a distribution made after the account beneficiary becomes disabled or dies and does not condition on the box-3 code at all, so a filer holding either ground on a code-1 distribution can say so — and the only way they say so is by attesting it on /filers/*/writableHsaCollectionExceptionReason. Age 65 (223(f)(4)(C)) is the third ground and is attested for the same reason: it is date-of-distribution scoped and this dictionary holds no distribution date, so the mid-year turner cannot be derived either way. Letting the return compute on a missing answer would OVER-tax every one of them silently, which is a wrong return rather than a refused one.

Whether this Form 1099-SA's box 4 fair market value on the date of death causes a refusal. Box 4 on an item that is NOT admitted refuses, complete-safely: an unanswered recipient, an unanswered box 4 or pre-death expense, the code-4 estate case on a return that is not the decedent's final return, the rollover/withdrawn-excess contradictions, and a stray box 4 on a non-death code. The code-4 estate case on such a return is refused through the guard this fact feeds; THIS fact is the per-item term that refuses it.
THREE ADMISSIONS ARE EXCLUDED, and the exclusions must not be collapsed, because they hold for different reasons. (A) THE SURVIVING SPOUSE (../isAdmittedSurvivingSpouseDeathDistribution): under IRC 223(f)(8)(A) the account is treated as if the spouse were the account beneficiary, so nothing is includible by reason of the death and box 4 is informational. (B) THE NONSPOUSE BENEFICIARY, on a code-6 or a code-4 form (../isAdmittedNonspouseBeneficiaryDeathDistribution): box 4 is not informational on it, it IS the printed Form 8889 line 14a (i8889 "Death of Account Beneficiary", "On Part II, line 14a, enter the fair market value of the HSA as of the date of death"). (A) excludes because nothing is includible, (B) because the inclusion is computed. An item whose box-1 rollover question or withdrawn-excess-contributions question is answered YES is not admitted - both are document/answer contradictions (IRC 223(f)(5)'s rollover is a payment into a health savings account "of such beneficiary", and 223(f)(8)(B)(i)(I) ended the account on the date of death) - so its box-4 value stays an unmodelled inclusion and this refusal stands (see /filers/*/hsaDistributionNotNormalKnockout). (C) THE ESTATE, ON THE DECEDENT'S OWN FINAL RETURN (../isAdmittedEstateDeathDistribution argues the full population): the item's owning filer is the one marked deceased on THIS return, and box 4 is the DECEDENT's own printed Form 8889 line 14a rather than an unmodelled inclusion. An estate item belonging to a filer this return does not mark deceased refuses, correctly and permanently: that estate's own Form 1099-SA reports to a return this dictionary does not file.

The refusal on a fair market value this graph cannot route. Two arms, and they now refuse two quite different residues.
THE BOX-4 ARM refuses a Form 1099-SA box 4 fair market value on an item that is NOT an admitted death distribution, counted through /hsaDistributions/*/causesFmvKnockout. An admitted item's box 4 is not an unmodelled inclusion: on the surviving-spouse item IRC 223(f)(8)(A) treats the account as if the spouse were the account beneficiary, so no inclusion arises at all, and on an admitted nonspouse-beneficiary OR admitted estate item box 4 IS the printed Form 8889 line 14a - the decedent's own line 14a for the estate item, because the estate admission (/hsaDistributions/*/isAdmittedEstateDeathDistribution) fires only where the item's owning filer is the one marked deceased on THIS return, i.e. where this return IS "the account beneficiary's final income tax return" i8889 names (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 3), with no line-15 reduction (223(f)(8)(B)(ii)(I) excludes the estate from it) and no 20% additional tax. WHAT THIS ARM STILL REFUSES, named: an ESTATE item belonging to a filer this return does not mark deceased, or on a return with no deceased filer at all; an unanswered recipient; an unanswered box 4 or pre-death qualified expense on either death code; the box-1 rollover and withdrawn-excess-contribution contradictions; and a stray box 4 typed on a non-death code. Every one of these is a permanent data-completeness or document-contradiction refusal, or the estate's own Form 1099-SA reporting to a return this dictionary does not file.
THE PLEDGE ARM refuses a return that attests a pledge under IRC 223(e)(2) / 408(e)(4) and has not answered BOTH of the questions a pledge needs: form8889 /writableHsaPledgedAssetsFairMarketValue, the value of what was pledged, and /writableHsaPledgeAdditionalTaxExceptionReason, which of IRC 223(f)(4)'s exceptions the pledge meets, if any. THAT IS PURE DATA COMPLETENESS and it is the whole of what this arm refuses: the income leg form8889 /schedule1Line8fPledgedHsaFmvIncome and the 20% additional tax /hsaPledgeSchedule2Line17zAdditional20PctTax are both COMPUTED, so an answered pledge FILES. Neither answer can be defaulted. An unanswered amount is refused because the graph cannot tell whether an amount exists at all, not because a $0 return would be unfilable: an attested pledge whose fair market value is ANSWERED as $0 already files today, refused only by its own unanswered exception reason where that is also missing. An unanswered exception reason would either charge a 65-year-old, a disabled or a deceased account beneficiary a tax IRC 223(f)(4)(B) and (C) do not impose, or drop a tax 223(f)(4)(A) does.
TWO ARMS, TWO AMOUNTS, AND ONE INTAKE CANNOT SERVE BOTH. IRC 408(e)(2)(B) measures the section 4975 case as ALL the account's assets on the FIRST DAY of the year and the instructions put it on Form 8889 line 14a; IRC 408(e)(4) measures the pledge as "the portion so used" and the instructions put it on Schedule 1 line 8f, bypassing Form 8889 Part II entirely. Two measures, two dates, two printed lines, therefore two facts: /filers/*/writableHsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1Fmv and form8889 /writableHsaPledgedAssetsFairMarketValue.
FORM 8889 PART II IS UNTOUCHED BY THE PLEDGE, which is worth stating once because it is the structural surprise of this arm: the pledged amount never enters line 16, so no printed Form 8889 line moves, and the 20% additional tax it bears prints on Schedule 2 line 17z rather than 17c. The banner above /hsaPledgeSchedule2Line17zAdditional20PctTax carries that reading in full, with the 17z instruction that admits it.
On the box-4 arm: hsa-death-code6-nonspouse-beneficiary-computes and hsa-death-code4-nonspouse-computes against hsa-death-code4-estate-still-refused and review-r2-code4-estate-on-decedents-final-return.
Amount of distributions rolled over into other HSAs

Fact.Name: January 1 fair market value of all assets in the HSA (section 4975 deemed distribution)
Fact.Description:
The amount of the IRC 223(e)(2) / section 4975 deemed distribution, per filer, the code-5 (prohibited transaction) case. Read through ../hsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1Fmv, never directly.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION (the application builds the screen from this Description and never opens an IRS document).
THE QUESTION: "What was the total value of everything in this HSA on January 1, 2025?"
HELP TEXT: "Because a prohibited transaction happened, the law treats the account as if it stopped being an HSA on the first day of the year and paid out everything in it that day. Enter what ALL of the account's assets were worth on January 1, 2025 - not the amount shown in box 1 of any Form 1099-SA, which is only what was actually withdrawn. Your trustee's year-end or year-start statement, or Form 5498-SA, will show it. If you have more than one HSA, enter the value of the account the prohibited transaction happened in - and if it happened in more than one, add those accounts together. Do not include an HSA that was not involved, and do not also enter a Form 1099-SA from an account you are reporting here: the January-1 value already covers everything that was in it." (Paraphrasing the 2025 Instructions for Form 8889, "Deemed Distributions From HSAs": "Your account ceases to be an HSA as of January 1, 2025, and you must include the fair market value of all assets in the account as of January 1, 2025, on line 14a"; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 3, the heading at line 187. The statute behind it is IRC 223(e)(2) applying IRC 408(e)(2), whose subparagraph (B) is the "fair market value (on such first day) of all assets in the account (on such first day)"; 26 U.S.C. 408, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section408&num=0&edition=2024.)
ASKED WHEN: /hsaDeemedDistributionSection4975Triggered is true - that is, EITHER the filer answered the return-level prohibited-transaction attestation form8889:/writableHsaProhibitedTransactionOccurred yes, OR this return carries a Form 1099-SA whose box 3 is code 5. Asked PER FILER, because Form 8889 is a per-individual form (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 4) and line 14a is a per-filer line; on a joint return where both spouses have HSAs, ask the spouse whose account it was, and ask it ONCE PER ACCOUNT rather than once per spouse (both spouses answering reports one event twice - see /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionCode's named residue (ii)). Never asked otherwise.
PER FILER, THOUGH THE STATUTE IS PER ACCOUNT, and the gap is the screen's to close. IRC 408(e)(2) operates on "the account", and i8889 says "any of your HSAs"; this writable is one Dollar per FILER, so a filer with two HSAs, one tainted, has no place to say which - and a filer with two tainted accounts is not told to add them. The help text above supplies both instructions. Modelling it per account would need an HSA ACCOUNT collection this module does not have (the /hsaDistributions collection is a collection of DOCUMENTS, and a section 4975 event produces no document), so the one-writable shape is deliberate and the residue is a screen-wording obligation, not a graph gap.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED. hsa:/flowKnockoutHsaDistributionCode blocks submission for a code-5 item whose owner has not answered this question and for a return-level section 4975 attestation with no filer's answer behind it. That is the data-completeness residue named on /filers/*/hsaDistributionNotNormalKnockout, and it is the correct permanent refusal: without this figure the return would tax box 1 of the Form 1099-SA - a number the statute does not use - instead of the whole account.
VALIDATION: Dollar, Limit type="Min" $0. No upper bound (an HSA balance has no statutory ceiling; the contribution limits cap what goes IN each year, not what an account can be worth). $0 is a valid answer and means a worthless account, not a missing answer - the graph tells the two apart with IsComplete on this Writable, not with a zero test.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: ../hsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1Fmv adds it to ../totalHsaDistributions (printed Form 8889 line 14a), from which it flows through line 14c and line 16 to Schedule 1 line 8f as income, and through Form 8889 lines 17a/17b to Schedule 2 line 17c as the 20% additional tax. The instructions are explicit that the deemed amount gets no qualified-expense offset - "Any deemed distribution will not be treated as used to pay qualified medical expenses. Generally, these distributions are subject to the additional 20% tax" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 3) - and the graph honours that without any special arithmetic, because line 15 (../hsaQualifiedMedExpenses) is itself an intake of expenses PAID USING distributions and a deemed distribution paid for nothing. The screen should say so, so a filer does not add the deemed amount to their medical expenses. The 20% is forgiven only through the attestation pair (../writableHsaCollectionExceptionAmount and ../writableHsaCollectionExceptionReason).

Fact.Name: This filer supplied the January 1 fair market value
Fact.Description:
The "source answered" predicate for ../writableHsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1Fmv, and the only thing the code-5 admission and the narrowed guards read. It is IsComplete over a BARE optional Writable, which is a real answered-test: the writable has no default and no complete-safe wrapper of its own, so this fact is false until the filer types a number and true the moment they do, INCLUDING a typed $0.
NOT IsComplete on a complete-safe fact. The sibling ../hsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1Fmv IS complete-safe (it defaults to $0) and asking IsComplete of THAT would be the always-true trap the module rules forbid; this fact deliberately reads the writable itself.

Fact.Name: This filer's section 4975 deemed distribution, read complete-safely
Fact.Description:
../writableHsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1Fmv read complete-safely, and the addend of ../totalHsaDistributions (printed Form 8889 line 14a) immediately below.
$0 UNLESS BOTH A TRIGGER AND AN ANSWER ARE PRESENT. The Case requires /hsaDeemedDistributionSection4975Triggered (a code-5 Form 1099-SA on this return, or the return-level section 4975 attestation) AND ../hasAnsweredHsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1Fmv. Requiring the TRIGGER as well as the answer is deliberate: a January-1 value is a deemed distribution only because a prohibited transaction occurred, so a value left behind by an edited interview would otherwise inflate line 14a - and therefore line 16, Schedule 1 line 8f and the 20% additional tax - with nothing refusing the return. That direction is taxpayer-ADVERSE, which is the direction this module refuses to fail in.
THE RESIDUE THAT GATE CREATES, NAMED. A filer who answers the amount and then answers the attestation NO (and holds no code-5 document) has their answer silently dropped to $0. That is the intended outcome - they are saying no deemed distribution happened - but it is the stale-answer shape /hsaDistributions/*/hasDistributionsWithoutHsaActivity guards against, so it is stated rather than left to be found. It cannot understate a return that files, because the same trigger being false is exactly what makes the code-5 and attestation refusals inert.
COMPLETE-SAFE $0 EVERYWHERE ELSE, which is load-bearing: this fact is an addend of a fact exported to MeF and read by the whole Part II chain, so it must never take line 14a Incomplete.

Fact.Name: This filer's January 1 fair market value will actually reach income
Fact.Description:
../hasAnsweredHsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1Fmv AND ../hasHsaCanHaveDistribution. This, not the bare answered-test, is what the narrowed guards read, and the second conjunct is the whole reason this fact exists.
WITHOUT IT THE NARROWING WOULD OPEN AN UNDERSTATEMENT HOLE, and it is the same shape /hsaDistributions/*/hasDistributionsWithoutHsaActivity closes. ../taxableHsaDistributionTotal (printed line 16) is a Switch with NO default whose every Case is gated on ../hasHsaCanHaveDistribution, so for a filer who cannot have HSA distributions the printed line is Incomplete and ../taxableHsaDistributionTotalOrZero falls to $0 - which means the January-1 value would sit on line 14a and NEVER reach line 16, Schedule 1 line 8f, or the 20% additional tax. Retiring the refusal for such a filer would let a return file with a deemed distribution and no income from it. That direction is taxpayer-favourable understatement, which this dictionary does not ship.
HOW A FILER LANDS IN THAT STATE: ../hasHsaCanHaveDistribution is ../mayHaveHsaContributions, which needs either a W-2 box 12 code W or an answered "had non-W-2 HSA activity" AND "non-employer HSA activity". A filer who attests a section 4975 prohibited transaction while answering the HSA-activity questions no is contradicting themselves; the return stays refused and the interview should send them back, which is exactly what a data-completeness residue is for.
THE SECOND CONJUNCT IS FENCED WITH IsComplete, and that fence is not decoration. ../hasHsaCanHaveDistribution is ../mayHaveHsaContributions, which is INCOMPLETE for a filer who has answered no HSA-activity question - the ordinary state of a spouse on an MFJ return. A bare All(answered, canHaveDistribution) is then Incomplete, and because this fact feeds /someFilerAnsweredHsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1Fmv and through it the BlockSubmissionOnTrue guard /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionCode, the guard STOPS RESOLVING and flow:/flowIsKnockedOut degrades Complete to Placeholder on exactly the return shape the return-level attestation exists to serve.
