Measured, not reasoned: without the fence, an MFJ return with the section 4975 attestation true and the ineligible SPOUSE answering $12,000 loses /filers/*/hsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1FmvIsUsable, /someFilerAnsweredHsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1Fmv and /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionCode from the snapshot entirely. With the fence an Incomplete eligibility yields FALSE, so the return-level arm keeps refusing, which is the safe direction and the one this fact's own paragraphs above say it is for. The module used the same All(IsComplete(x), x) idiom two facts earlier on /hsaDistributions/*/isAdmittedProhibitedTransactionDistribution; this is that idiom, not a new one.

Fact.Name: Some filer supplied a usable January 1 fair market value
Fact.Description:
Return-level projection of /filers/*/hsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1FmvIsUsable. It is what narrows the RETURN-LEVEL arm of /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionCode: the section 4975 attestation form8889:/hasNonNormalTopLevelHsaDistribution is answered on the return, not per filer, so the question "has the amount been supplied" can only be asked of the return there. The per-item collection arm asks the sharper per-owner question instead (/hsaDistributions/*/isAdmittedProhibitedTransactionDistribution).
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE, and the claim is EARNED rather than asserted. A Count over a collection-relative Dependency is Complete only if every member resolves, and /filers/*/hsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1FmvIsUsable does: its All fences the one Incomplete-capable conjunct (../hasHsaCanHaveDistribution) with IsComplete, so it is Complete on every filer on every return - FALSE for a filer who answered nothing, FALSE for a filer whose HSA eligibility is unanswered, TRUE only for a filer who both answered the amount and is eligible. So this Count is Complete on every return and this fact is complete-safe FALSE, which is the REFUSING direction for the guard that reads it.

Appears on Form 8889 line 14a.
THE SECTION 4975 DEEMED DISTRIBUTION IS AN ADDEND HERE (the code-5, prohibited-transaction case). The instructions put it on this exact line and name no other: "Your account ceases to be an HSA as of January 1, 2025, and you must include the fair market value of all assets in the account as of January 1, 2025, on line 14a" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 3). It is an ADD rather than a select because a filer can hold ordinary Forms 1099-SA and have had a prohibited transaction in the same year: line 14a is scoped to ALL of the filer's HSAs, and the graph holds no account identity, so a filer with one tainted account and one clean one is served correctly only by adding.
THE ADD DOUBLE-COUNTS ON A SINGLE-ACCOUNT RETURN, AND THAT IS A NAMED, ADJUDICATED RESIDUE rather than a defended claim. It is NOT true that "the 1099-SA reports what was actually withdrawn and the deemed amount is the rest of the account, so the two never describe the same dollar". IRC 408(e)(2)(B) measures ALL assets in the account on the FIRST DAY of the year, and anything withdrawn later in that year was among those assets on January 1; Form 1099-SA box 1 is "the total amount of the distribution" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099sa--2025.pdf, page 2), i.e. what was actually paid out, not the January-1 value. With one Form 1099-SA, code 5, box 1 $8,000 and a January-1 FMV of $12,000, line 14a is $20,000 and the $8,000 is inside both figures. IRC 408(e)(2)(A) also has the account ceasing to be an HSA as of January 1, so on the strictest reading there is no later HSA distribution from that account to report at all.
THE ARITHMETIC IS KEPT AND THE DIRECTION IS SAID PLAINLY. The IRS text is literally additive (line 14a "Enter the total distributions your HSAs made in 2025. These amounts should be shown on Form 1099-SA, box 1", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 8, beside the deemed section's "on line 14a" at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 3) and the graph cannot tell the one-account case from the two-account case, so no derivation can serve both. The failure direction on a single account is taxpayer-ADVERSE (over-inclusion), which is not a filing blocker, and the screen keeps the filer out of it: the screen must say "do not also enter a Form 1099-SA from the account that had the prohibited transaction — the January-1 value already covers everything that was in it". It is an open owner question, asked together with the 20% additional tax on the pledged amount (see /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionFMV).
IT IS ROUNDED SEPARATELY, deliberately. The printed line rounds once, but the collection sum is rounded on its own, and re-shaping that to round the combined figure would move cents-bearing figures for no tax reason. Round(x) + Round(0) is Round(x), so a return with no deemed distribution is unaffected.
Enum for if the filer had other health coverage that would make them ineligible for HSA contributions
Duration that filer had other health coverage that would make them ineligible for HSA contributions
Duration that filer had other health coverage that would make them ineligible for HSA contributions after accounting for edit conditions
Whether filer had other health coverage that would make them ineligible for HSA contributions for part of the year

Fact.Name: A part-year other-coverage answer the monthly coverage vector does not carry
Fact.Description: Whether this filer answered that disqualifying other health coverage lasted part of the year and the Line 3 Limitation Chart on this return cannot show those months. Either the monthly coverage vector does not supply line 3, so the legacy count and type cannot split the year; or it does and shows the filer an eligible individual on the first day of all twelve months, which contradicts the part-year answer. A vector that routes at least one month to the chart's enter-zero line carries the answer, and line 3 is the sum of the monthly limitations for the eligible months.

Fact.Name: Part-year disqualifying other coverage the Line 3 chart cannot show
Fact.Description: Refuses a return on which some filer reported disqualifying other health coverage for part of the year and the monthly coverage vector does not carry it: the vector does not supply line 3, or it shows that filer eligible on the first day of every month. A vector that routes the covered months to the chart's enter-zero line computes line 3 month by month and does not refuse.
Whether filer had other health coverage that would make them ineligible for HSA contributions for the whole year
Knockout due to not having HDHP coverage all year
The filer's HSA base contribution limit, regardless of age.

Maximum amount of HSA contributions for the tax year. Reported on line 3 of form 8889.
FORM 8889 PART I GATE. Read through ../hsaForm8889PartIRequired, not ../hasMadeContributionsToHsa alone: Part I is also owed to a filer who made no 2025 contributions but carries a prior-year excess into Form 5329 line 42, because Form 5329 line 43 measures the absorption against Form 8889 line 12.
Whether the filer had HDHP coverage for the whole year
Whether the filer has met the conditions for a special rule to where we need to calculate the optimal line 6 value for the filer.
Helper calculation for primary: The sum of lines 2 and 11 less line 7.
The calculated contribution limit for the primary filer. This should only be used when the filer has met the family contribution limit rule.
The calculated contribution limit for the secondary filer. This should only be used when the filer has met the family contribution limit rule.
The calculated contribution limit for the case where both filers have HSAs and are filing jointly and we must determine the correct contribution limit for each filer

Form 8889 Line 6: the contribution limit less the addition in line 7. When the monthly-vector equal-division rule applies, the default half share takes precedence over the legacy contribution-based allocation. Unresolved legacy coverage or contribution limits leave line 6 Incomplete rather than printing a placeholder amount.
FORM 8889 PART I GATE. Read through ../hsaForm8889PartIRequired, not ../hasMadeContributionsToHsa alone: Part I is also owed to a filer who made no 2025 contributions but carries a prior-year excess into Form 5329 line 42, because Form 5329 line 43 measures the absorption against Form 8889 line 12.
Whether the return is for MFJ filers with at least one having family coverage.

Fact.Name: The return's MSA answer resolves TRUE
Fact.Description:
Whether this return has answered the Archer/medical-savings-account question in the affirmative. COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE, which is the property every fact below leans on: on a return that never reached the question — every return committed to this repo today — this resolves false rather than Incomplete, so the Form 8853 line 2 intake is never demanded and the line 4 reduction is a hard 0.
IT IS THE GUARD'S OPERAND, NOT A NEW PREDICATE. /flowKnockoutHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType reduces to /hasHsaMedicalSavingsAccountTypeDerived alone (the two negated flow gates are vacuous whenever that operand is true — re-derived against the bodies at /flowToExcessContributionsPreviousYear and /skipToHsaExcessContributions, not taken from the contract's word), so this fact is exactly the population the guard has always refused, with an IsComplete fence in front of it.

Fact.Name: Writable: any 2025 Archer MSA distribution (Form 8853 Part II line 6a)
Fact.Description:
Whether the taxpayer or spouse received any distribution in 2025 from any Archer MSA, including a fair-market-value amount a beneficiary must report after the account holder's death. This is the Form 8853 Part II gate, and it is asked so the guard can tell a DORMANT legacy Archer MSA, which files with nothing to report, from one with distributions, which Form 8853 Section A Part II (lines 6a to 9b) computes.
WHY THE DEATH LEG IS INSIDE THIS ONE QUESTION rather than a second intake: the instructions route the beneficiary's FMV to the SAME line ("On lines 6a and 6c, enter the fair market value"), so a return that must report it is a return with a line 6a, and one question fences both.

Fact.Name: Writable: a Medicare Advantage MSA (Form 8853 Section B)
Fact.Description: Whether the taxpayer or spouse has a Medicare Advantage MSA - Form 8853 SECTION B, not Section C (Section C is Long-Term Care insurance contracts and is outside this guard entirely). The single shipping question /hasHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType asks only whether the filer has "a medical savings account" and CANNOT distinguish the two vehicles Form 8853 separates — Section A is the Archer MSA and Section B is the Medicare Advantage MSA, and the form's own Section A heading says "If you have only a Medicare Advantage MSA, skip Section A and complete Section B." A reduction of the HSA limitation is an ARCHER fact (IRC 223(b)(4)(A) names Archer MSAs), so a Medicare Advantage MSA is not an Archer contribution and reduces nothing on Form 8889. This writable is the population gate of Form 8853 Section B (/medicareAdvantageMsaOnThisReturn reads it), and such a return files once lines 10 to 13b resolve.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 line 2 — this filer's own Archer MSA contributions for 2025
Fact.Description:
The Archer MSA contributions this filer made for 2025, including those made in 2026 by the unextended due date of the return that were for 2025, EXCLUDING rollovers. Form 8853 line 2.
WHY PER FILER AND NOT PER RETURN: the Part I header settles it — "If you are filing jointly and both you and your spouse have high deductible health plans with self-only coverage, complete a separate Part I for each spouse." Line 2 is a Part I line, so it is one spouse's figure. The joint-return fold-in Form 8889 line 4 prescribes is applied downstream at /archerMsaBothFilersContributionsTotal, not by widening this question.
THE "Don't include rollovers" CONDITION IS NOT SILENCED: it is carried in this Description and in the authority quote, and it is an application screen-wording obligation rather than a computation — this dictionary has no Archer rollover intake to subtract, and inventing one would be an intake nobody answers. This is a named gap.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 1 — this filer's employer Archer MSA contributions, from W-2 box 12 code R
Fact.Description:
FORM 8853 LINE 1, per filer, cents preserved. Read off the W-2s rather than asked, because the instructions say where it comes from: "These contributions should be shown in box 12 of Form W-2 with code R." The per-filer split mirrors /filers/*/hsaContributionsW2sTotal, which does the same job for box 12 code W and Form 8889 line 9.
NO ROUND HERE, and that is a deliberate divergence from the code-W sibling. Form 8889 line 4 adds line 1 to line 2 before printing, so under i1040gi page 23 the cents must survive into that sum and the single Round belongs at ../hsaLine4ArcherMsaContributions.
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 for every return without a code-R entry: the addend formW2s:/formW2s/*/archerMsaContributionsUnrounded folds an unanswered box-12 code-R entry to 0.
THE SPLIT GATE IS filers:/isMarried, NOT filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ, and that is a DELIBERATE divergence from the code-W sibling ../hsaContributionsW2sTotal, which uses MFJ. The reason is arithmetic rather than stylistic: /archerMsaBothFilersContributionsTotal aggregates both filers on every MARRIED return, so if this fact fell through to the PRIMARY filer's W-2 sum for a secondary filer on an MFS return, that primary sum would be counted TWICE inside the aggregate. Reading each filer's own W-2s on every married return is the only split that makes the aggregate a sum of disjoint parts.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 2 — this filer's own Archer MSA contributions, fenced
Fact.Description:
FORM 8853 LINE 2, per filer. HARD 0 whenever the return has no MSA at all, and the RAW INTAKE otherwise — which means INCOMPLETE, not 0, on a return that answered the MSA question true and then left this amount blank.
THE INCOMPLETENESS IS THE POINT, and it is the taxpayer-adverse direction fenced rather than a convenience. Defaulting an unanswered line 2 to 0 would UNDER-state Form 8889 line 4 and so OVER-state line 5, handing the filer a larger HSA limitation than IRC 223(b)(4)(A) allows. This is the same stance /filers/*/hsaMonthlyMedicareVectorAnswered takes on its own vector, and for the same reason. Such a return is ALSO refused by /flowKnockoutHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType, because /archerMsaDormantLegacyAccountOnly requires this fact to be Complete — so the fence is doubled on purpose: the guard refuses the filing and the number refuses to exist.
A HARD 0 ON EVERY RETURN WITHOUT AN MSA: /archerMsaOnThisReturn is complete-safe false wherever the MSA question is answered false.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 lines 1 and 2 for this filer — the pair Form 8889 line 4 reads
Fact.Description: This filer's own Archer MSA contributions for 2025: employer (line 1) plus own (line 2), cents preserved. Form 8889 line 4 names exactly this pair — "from Form 8853, lines 1 and 2" — so the sum is the form's own composition, not a derived aggregate.

Fact.Name: Family HDHP coverage at any time in 2025, for the Form 8889 line 4 spouse fold-in
Fact.Description:
Whether this filer had family coverage under an HDHP at any time during 2025 — the condition Form 8889 line 4 puts on including the SPOUSE's Archer MSA contributions.
TWO REGIMES, READ THE ONE THAT GOVERNS. Where the twelve-month vector supplies line 3 (/hsaLine3VectorGoverns), the any-month test already exists as ../hsaLine3HadFamilyCoverageAnyMonth and is used verbatim. Otherwise the legacy chain's ../isCoveredByFamilyHdhp is the module's own answer to the same question. Choosing per regime rather than picking one is what keeps this fact from disagreeing with the line 3 it is about to reduce.
INCOMPLETE IS TOLERATED HERE and handled by the caller: a filer with no HSA coverage answers at all leaves ../isCoveredByFamilyHdhp Incomplete, and /archerMsaSpouseAmountIncludedOnLine4 fences every read of this fact with IsComplete before testing it.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 4 includes the spouse's Archer MSA contributions
Fact.Description:
Whether the printed line 4 condition is met: a joint return on which EITHER spouse had family coverage under an HDHP at any time during 2025. When it is, each spouse's line 4 carries BOTH spouses' Form 8853 lines 1 and 2 — the form says so, and IRC 223(b)(5)(B)(i) agrees, reducing the shared married limitation by "the aggregate amount paid to Archer MSAs of such spouses".
MARRIED, NOT MFJ. IRC 223(b)(5) carries no filing-status condition - "In the case of individuals who are married to each other, if either spouse has family coverage" - and its (B)(i) reduction runs on "the aggregate amount paid to Archer MSAs of such spouses". ../writableArcherMsaOwnContributions is PER FILER, so on an MFS return the secondary filer's copy is a real number in the tree, and gating on MFJ would drop it, in the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction (a larger HSA limit). This module reads the same sentence's (B)(ii) division through filers:/isMarried at ../hsaLine3EqualDivisionApplies, so both halves of one statutory sentence read filers:/isMarried.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: every read of a per-filer coverage answer is fenced with IsComplete first, so a half-answered interview yields false (the filer's own amount alone) rather than Incompleteness spreading to line 4.

Fact.Name: Both spouses' Form 8853 lines 1 and 2, for the line 4 fold-in
Fact.Description: The aggregate of both filers' own Archer MSA contribution totals, cents preserved. Read only when /archerMsaSpouseAmountIncludedOnLine4 holds. On a return with no secondary filer figure in the tree this falls back to the primary filer's own total, so the fact is always defined and the fold-in decision stays with the gate rather than being smuggled in here.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 LINE 4 — the IRC 223(b)(4)(A) Archer MSA reduction
Fact.Description:
FORM 8889 LINE 4, per filer, whole dollars. This is the contract /archerMsaForm8853Contributions obligation (1): the one number Form 8889 needs from Form 8853.
THE ROUND HAPPENS HERE AND ONLY HERE. Lines 1 and 2 are cents-bearing addends and line 4 is a printed whole-dollar line, which is exactly the i1040gi page 23 rule — "include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total".
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 ON EVERY RETURN WITHOUT AN MSA, so Form 8889 line 5 is line 3 passed through for every return without one.
WHAT IT IS NOT: it is not the Archer MSA DEDUCTION. Form 8853 line 5 ("Enter the smallest of line 2, 3, or 4") is a different number on a different form, computed at /filers/*/archerMsaForm8853Line5Deduction.

Fact.Name: No Form 8853 Section A Part II activity on this return
Fact.Description: Whether the return has answered, in the negative, that anyone received an Archer MSA distribution in 2025. REQUIRES THE ANSWER: an unanswered intake resolves this false, which keeps the guard refusing. Taxpayer-adverse direction, deliberately — Form 8853 Part II is not built, so a return with distributions must not file.

Fact.Name: No Form 8853 Section B vehicle on this return
Fact.Description:
Whether the return has answered, in the negative, that anyone has a Medicare Advantage MSA. The Archer predicates read /archerMsaSectionBResolvedOrAbsent, an Any over this fact and /medicareAdvantageMsaSectionBFullyComputed, so a return that answers YES and completes Form 8853 Section B lines 10 to 13b files too. This fact keeps its exact meaning - the return has ANSWERED NO - because "no Section B" and "a Section B that resolves" are two different states and the Archer chain needs to be able to tell them apart. It REQUIRES THE ANSWER, for the same taxpayer-adverse reason as /archerMsaNoSectionAPartIiDistributions.
THE SECTION LETTER. Read on disk: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8853.pdf, page 1 is "Section B. Medicare Advantage MSA Distributions" and https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8853.pdf, page 2 is "Section C. Long-Term Care (LTC) Insurance Contracts". The Medicare Advantage MSA is SECTION B. Section C is LTC and is NOT in this guard's scope at all: an LTC policyholder is not thereby an MSA holder, /hasHsaMedicalSavingsAccountTypeDerived never resolves true for them on that ground, and this guard has never reached them.

Fact.Name: This filer's Form 8853 lines 1 and 2 are both known to be zero
Fact.Description:
Whether this filer's Archer MSA took NO contribution of either kind for 2025 — employer (line 1) or own (line 2) — and both figures are KNOWN, not merely absent. The IsComplete conjuncts come first (the unanswered-collection trap: an unanswered line 2 makes this false rather than leaving it Incomplete, and false is the refusing direction).
THIS IS THE "WHO MUST FILE" TEST, INVERTED. The Form 8853 filing trigger is contributions: "You must file Form 8853 if any of the following applies. • You (or your employer) made contributions for 2025 to your Archer MSA. • You are filing a joint return and your spouse (or their employer) made contributions for 2025 to your spouse's Archer MSA." A filer for whom both figures are zero does not trip that trigger, which is why the dormant cell this fact feeds can file WITHOUT the Form 8853 attachment this repo does not build.
NEGATIVES ARE IMPOSSIBLE ON BOTH INPUTS (the W-2 box 12 code R writable and ../writableArcherMsaOwnContributions both carry a Min 0 Limit), so Not(GreaterThan 0) is exactly "is zero" and no separate floor test is owed.

Fact.Name: The return's only MSA fact is a dormant legacy Archer MSA
Fact.Description:
THE NARROWING PREDICATE. Whether this return's Archer MSA took no contributions, made no distributions, and is not a Medicare Advantage MSA — in which case there is nothing for Form 8853 to report, no reduction for Form 8889 line 4 to carry, and no reason left to refuse the return.
WHY THIS IS THE CELL, AND WHY IT IS NOT A CONSOLATION PRIZE. Publication 969 records that the Archer MSA population is CLOSED: "After 2007, you can't be treated as an eligible individual for Archer MSA purposes unless: 1. You were an active participant for any tax year ending before 2008, or 2. You became an active participant for a tax year ending after 2007 by reason of coverage under a high deductible health plan (HDHP) of an Archer MSA participating employer." A closed population that cannot take new entrants drifts toward DORMANCY, so the legacy holder with an untouched account is the modal Archer return in TY2025 — and it is the one cell that needs no part of Form 8853 at all.
WHAT THE WIDER CELLS NEED, stated rather than left to be found. A return with employer contributions (line 1 > 0) or own contributions (line 2 > 0) MUST FILE Form 8853, and the excess-employer-contribution test needs Form 8853 line 3 and line 4 — "Excess employer contributions are the excess, if any, of your employer's contributions over the smaller of (a) your limitation on line 3 or (b) your compensation from the employer(s) who maintained your HDHP (line 4)". Those cells file through /archerMsaSectionAPartIFullyComputed or /archerMsaForm8853FullyComputed (see /flowKnockoutHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType), not through this predicate.
THE SECONDARY FILER IS CONSULTED ON EVERY MARRIED RETURN, MFS INCLUDED. The gate is filers:/isMarried, matching ../hsaLine3EqualDivisionApplies, which reads the same statutory sentence that way. An MFJ-only gate would let an MFS return whose SPOUSE had answered a nonzero Form 8853 line 2 resolve DORMANT and file with a line 4 of $0 - the taxpayer-favourable direction, and exactly the cell IRC 223(b)(5)(B)(i) aggregates over "such spouses".
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE for every return without an MSA, so this fact adds nothing to any guard evaluation there.

Fact.Name: Treated as having family coverage for each month, AFTER the Line 3 rule 2 deeming
Fact.Description:
The condition on the FIRST bullet of the Form 8889 Line 6 instruction, read with the Line 3 narrative rule 2. ../hsaLine3TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth asks the CHART's question — are all twelve post-collapse months `family` — and that is not the whole of the bullet's question, because rule 2 says that where the last-month rule applies "you are treated as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year". A filer whose December was a family month is therefore treated as having family coverage for EACH month however few months they actually held it, and the first bullet's equal division of line 5 is their branch, not the second bullet's four-step refigure.
WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE FACT AND NOT A WIDENING OF ../hsaLine3TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth. The chart must NOT apply rule 2's deeming: rule 4 makes line 3 the GREATER of the worksheet limitation, which is computed from the months actually held, and the last-month-rule amount, so the same twelve months are asked two different questions and the worksheet needs the literal one. Repointing the line-3 fact would also move rows pinned on the two Publication 969 worksheet-verified fixtures (hsa-monthly-vector-p969-example-1-december-only and -example-2-selfonly-to-family, whose ../hsaLine3EqualDivisionHalfShare is pinned at 8,550.00 for a married-filing-separately filer with December family coverage). This is the same separation, for the same reason, that put ../hsaLine6EqualDivisionHalfShare beside ../hsaLine3EqualDivisionHalfShare.
THE SECOND DISJUNCT ADDS A NARROW POPULATION AND NOTHING WIDER. Within the married population this fact serves, a family month's chart amount is 8,550 and a self-only month's is 4,300 — the age-55 additional amount is diverted to line 7 by the Line 3 Note for a married filer who had family coverage at any time — so the worksheet limitation, an average of twelve such months, reaches the last-month-rule amount of 8,550 only when every month is family, which is the first disjunct. A December-family filer outside the first disjunct therefore always has ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleIncreasedLimitation true; where that filer was not married every month, ../hsaLine6DeemedFamilyYearGoverns sends them into the four steps with the deemed month set.
ONE DIVERGENCE, NAMED. IRC 223(b)(8)(A)(ii) deems December's plan only "during each of the months such individual is treated as an eligible individual solely by reason of clause (i)" — i.e. only for the months the filer was not actually eligible — while the printed rule 2 deems it "for the entire year" with no such carve-out. A filer who held SELF-ONLY coverage in months they were actually eligible and family coverage in December is inside the form's sentence and outside the statute's. THIS DICTIONARY FOLLOWS THE FORM, and it does so consistently: ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleAmount already puts December's chart amount on all twelve months with no "solely by reason of" test, so reading rule 2 the other way here would make the Line 6 branch disagree with the line 3 the same rule produced. The divergence is taxpayer-favourable in the same direction rule 4's greater-of already is.

Fact.Name: Had family coverage at ANY time during 2025, AFTER the Line 3 rule 2 deeming
Fact.Description:
The Form 8889 Line 6 instruction's own population precondition — "Spouses who have separate HSAs and had family coverage under an HDHP at any time during 2025, use the following rules to figure the amount on line 6" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 7, LEFT column) — read through the Line 3 narrative rule 2 deeming, exactly as ../hsaLine6TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth reads the FIRST bullet's condition through it. Where the last-month rule SUPPLIED this filer's line 3, the twelve months the Line 6 rules ask about are December's plan repeated twelve times; otherwise they are the months the chart actually records, and this fact is ../hsaLine3HadFamilyCoverageAnyMonth unchanged.
WHY IT EXISTS: interpretation: owner ruling, see TAX-INTERPRETATIONS-FOR-EXPERT-REVIEW.md AD-01 - RULE FOR THE FORM. The question is whether rule 2's unqualified "entire year" deeming or IRC 223(b)(8)(A)(ii)'s "solely by reason of clause (i)" carve-out governs the Line 6 month set. The ruling's two supporting spans: (1) Form 8889's own Line 1 instruction treats deemed coverage as coverage for the form's own computations: "If you were covered, or considered covered, by a self-only HDHP and a family HDHP at different times during the year, check the box for the plan that was in effect for a longer period" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 4, LEFT column; the RIGHT column of those same physical lines carries the Line 3 narrative items 5 and 6). "Considered covered" is the form's own name for the deeming, and it is the form that then computes on it. (2) IRC 223(b)(8)(A)(ii) itself deems the individual "as having been enrolled ... in the same high deductible health plan in which the individual was" enrolled in the last month (26 U.S.C. 223, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section223&num=0&edition=2024, page 970 LEFT column; the RIGHT column of those physical lines carries IRC 223(c)(1)(B)). The deemed enrolment is an enrolment in DECEMBER'S plan — so a filer whose December was self-only is considered covered by a self-only plan for the months the deeming reaches, and "had family coverage at any time" is FALSE of them.
WHAT THIS SERVES, AND THE NUMBER. A married filer who held family coverage in some real month, whose DECEMBER was SELF-ONLY, and whose line 3 came from the last-month rule would otherwise face Form 8889 Line 6 Step 1's "the total of the worksheet amounts only for the months you were treated as having family coverage" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 7, LEFT column), a set that is empty under the deeming while the worksheet's is not. With this fact the filer is outside the Line 6 special rules altogether and takes the printed default, "Enter the amount from line 5" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8889.pdf, page 1). On the worked fixture hsa-line6-lastmonth-december-self-only-still-refused (the name is historical; the fixture files) that is $4,300.00 each. MEASURED, not asserted: the four steps run on the worksheet month set give $714.58 each, which is the reading the ruling rejects.
THE TRIGGER IS ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleIncreasedLimitation AND NOT ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleApplies, which is the one place this fact must diverge from ../hsaLine6TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth beside it, and the reason is rule 4's greater-of. A filer with family coverage in most months and a self-only December satisfies the last-month rule but LOSES the greater-of, so their line 3 IS the worksheet limitation and the four steps decompose exactly the number it is. The weaker trigger would hand that filer an undivided line 5 instead. Witnessed at cents by hsa-line6-lastmonth-worksheet-beats-the-deemed-year-four-steps-run: worksheet $7,483.33 against a last-month-rule amount of $4,300.00, line 6 $3,920.83 through the four steps, where the weaker trigger pays $7,483.33 undivided.
THE COST OF THE FORM READING, PRICED RATHER THAN ELIDED, because the ruling does not erase the arithmetic. A couple who actually held a family HDHP in a real month and whose December was self-only carry $4,300.00 each, $8,600.00 for the couple, where the statutory reading would give them ONE $8,550.00 limitation to divide, $4,275.00 each — $50.00 on the worked case; the statutory reading carries its own open sub-question (a flat $8,550.00 divided by two against a month-keyed $4,654.17 worksheet), so $50.00 is the smaller of the two candidate divergences, not a bound. The statute's carve-out words are "solely by reason of clause (i)" — the limitation the statutory reading rests on. Publication 969 prints the statute's version, "You are treated as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month if you didn't otherwise have coverage" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p969.pdf, page 5, RIGHT column). The ruling is for the FORM, and it is the same choice this module makes twice elsewhere — ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleAmount puts December's chart amount on all twelve months with no "solely by reason of" test, and ../hsaLine6TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth reads rule 2's unqualified sentence — so the Line 6 branch and the line 3 the same rule produced agree.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE OFF-POPULATION, and both operands are why: ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleIncreasedLimitation is a GreaterThan over two hard-0 amounts on a return that never answered the monthly vector, and the else arm's ../hsaLine3HadFamilyCoverageAnyMonth is an Any over twelve complete-safe enums. Pinned on hsa-line6-single-filer-return-level-facts-off-population and hsa-monthly-vector-unanswered-complete-safe.
THE ONE CELL THIS FACT DOES NOT SERVE is deeming-INDEPENDENT: a married filer whose DECEMBER WAS a family month, whose line 3 came from the last-month rule, and who was NOT married in every month. Rule 2 deems them family for all twelve months, so they are outside the first bullet's equal division - /hsaMarriedEveryMonth keeps them out of it, because IRC 223(b)(5) shares a limitation only between people married to each other - and ../hsaLine6DeemedFamilyYearGoverns sends them into the four steps with the deemed month set. Pinned by hsa-line6-lastmonth-december-family-mid-year-marriage-still-refused (the name is historical; the fixture files).

Fact.Name: The Line 6 steps run over a DEEMED twelve-family-month year, not the months actually held
Fact.Description:
Whether this filer's Form 8889 Line 6 figure has to be built out of the twelve months the Line 3 narrative rule 2 DEEMS them to have held, rather than out of the months the Limitation Chart records. It is true for exactly one shape, the Line 6 cell of /flowKnockoutHsaCoverage: a MARRIED filer whose line 3 came from the last-month rule (../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleIncreasedLimitation), whose DECEMBER was a family month (carried by ../hsaLine6HadFamilyCoverageAnyMonth, which under that trigger IS the December test — see the fact itself), and who was NOT married to the other spouse on the first day of every month (/hsaMarriedEveryMonth false).
WHY THOSE FIVE CONJUNCTS AND NOTHING WIDER. Rule 2 deems this filer December's coverage "for the entire year", so under the owner ruling (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS-FOR-EXPERT-REVIEW.md AD-01, RULE FOR THE FORM, carried at ../hsaLine6HadFamilyCoverageAnyMonth) every month of their year is a family month at December's chart amount and their line 3 IS twelve of those divided by 12. That makes them "treated as having family coverage for each month" — the Line 6 FIRST bullet's own condition, carried by ../hsaLine6TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth — and yet IRC 223(b)(5) divides a limitation only "in the case of individuals who are married to each other", so the months before the marriage were never shared with anybody and halving the whole of line 5 would understate this filer by exactly the unshared half. /hsaMarriedEveryMonth is what keeps them out of the first bullet, and this fact is what sends them into the second bullet's four steps WITH THE DEEMED MONTH SET rather than the chart's. Where the couple was married every month the first bullet is right and this fact is false.
THE READING, AND IT IS THE ONE THE CONTRACT ASKS FOR: "a month-keyed division of a DEEMED year — the deemed months inside the marriage divided under 223(b)(5)(B), the rest left whole; the shape ../hsaLine6SharedFamilyMonthsChartTotal already applies to real months". That is what this fact and its two siblings do: the Step 1 month set is December's chart amount counted once per month of the marriage, the Step 4 remainder is the same amount counted once per month outside it, and the two halves still sum to the filer's own line 3 — which is the property the four steps need and the reason this filer is decomposable.
COMPLETE-SAFE, and every operand is why. IsComplete(filers:/isMarried) is the first conjunct because filers:/isMarried CAN be unanswered — an empty return answers no filing status — and a bare read of it would be neither true nor false; ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleIncreasedLimitation is a GreaterThan over two hard-0 amounts on a return that never answered the monthly vector; ../hsaLine6HadFamilyCoverageAnyMonth is complete-safe false off-population by its own record; and /hsaMarriedEveryMonth is an All over twelve rows that each fall back to filers:/isMarried. NO IsComplete WRAPS THIS FACT ITSELF anywhere, because it is complete-safe false and an IsComplete on a complete-safe fact is always true.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 Line 6 — the FIRST bullet is this filer's branch
Fact.Description:
The SHIPPING gate on the IRC 223(b)(5)(B) equal division: this is ../hsaLine3EqualDivisionApplies with its coverage conjunct replaced by the rule-2-aware ../hsaLine6TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth. The other three conjuncts are carried over unchanged and for their original reasons — the division is only ever between "individuals who are married to each other", and /hsaMarriedEveryMonth is that condition month-keyed, so a couple married mid-year with family coverage all twelve months still takes the four steps rather than a halved whole-year line 5.
../hsaLine3EqualDivisionApplies IS NOT RETIRED AND IS NOT WRONG. It remains the literal reading of the printed first bullet against the chart's twelve-month vector, it still gates the pinned draft ../hsaLine3EqualDivisionHalfShare, and it is asserted by committed node tests at that meaning. What moved to this path is the BRANCH DECISION: ../hsaContributionLimitLessAddition, ../hsaLine6EqualDivisionHalfShare and ../causesHsaLine3NonUniformFamilyMonths all read this fact now, so the equal-division arm and the four-step arm stay exact complements of each other.

Fact.Name: Your agreed share of the family HSA contribution limit (Form 8889 line 6)
Fact.Description: When you and your spouse each have an HSA and family coverage, the family contribution limit is divided equally between you unless you both agree on a different division (such as allocating nothing to one spouse). Enter your share under that agreement. Leave it unanswered for the equal division. On a joint return both spouses' shares together may not exceed the shared limit.

Fact.Name: This filer's part of the divided family limitation
Fact.Description: The part of the shared family limitation this filer takes on line 6: the first bullet's share of line 5 when that bullet applies, the second bullet's Step 3 amount when the family months are not the whole year, and zero when no division applies.

Fact.Name: The shared family limitation this filer's division is taken from
Fact.Description: Line 5 when the first bullet of the Line 6 instructions applies, the Step 1 refigured line 5 when the second bullet applies, and zero when no division applies.

Fact.Name: The spouses' agreed division of the family HSA limit adds up to more than the limit
Fact.Description: Refuses a joint return on which either spouse states an agreed share of the family HSA contribution limit and the two spouses' line 6 shares together exceed the shared limitation (the smaller of the two spouses' division bases). The limitation is divided between the spouses, so the parts cannot add up to more than the whole. The filer corrects it by giving each spouse's agreed share so that the two add up to no more than the limit.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 LINE 6 — this filer's share of LINE 5 under the IRC 223(b)(5)(B) division
Fact.Description:
This filer's agreed share of line 5 when the spouses agree on a different division (../writableHsaAgreedFamilyLimitShare, capped at line 5); otherwise half of this filer's line 5 — line 3 reduced by the Archer MSA contributions on line 4 — which is what the printed Line 6 instruction divides: "If you are treated as having family coverage for each month, divide the amount on line 5 equally between you and your spouse, unless you both agree on a different allocation." IRC 223(b)(5)(B) has the same order: the limitation "(i) shall be reduced by the aggregate amount paid to Archer MSAs of such spouses for the taxable year, and (ii) after such reduction, shall be divided equally between them."
WHY THIS EXISTS BESIDE ../hsaLine3EqualDivisionHalfShare rather than replacing it. That fact is the draft's division of LINE 3, is asserted directly by seven committed node tests, and on a non-vector return line 5 is the LEGACY line 3 — a different number — so repointing it would have moved pinned rows unrelated to the Archer reduction. Its own Description carries the dated note. This fact is read ONLY by ../hsaContributionLimitLessAddition, and only on the arm that already requires /hsaLine3VectorGoverns and ../hsaLine3EqualDivisionApplies.
VALUE-IDENTICAL TO ../hsaLine3EqualDivisionHalfShare ON EVERY RETURN WITHOUT AN ARCHER MSA, since line 4 is then a hard 0 and line 5 is line 3 verbatim. The unconditional else-arm returns line 5 unhalved so the fact is total; the gate that decides whether the division applies stays at the consumer, exactly where it was.

FORM 8889 LINE 5: line 3 less line 4, floored at zero. "Subtract line 4 from line 3. If zero or less, enter -0-" is printed on the form face, so the floor is the form's own and not this repo's.
LINE 4 IS THE ARCHER MSA REDUCTION (../hsaLine4ArcherMsaContributions, the /archerMsaForm8853Contributions contract's obligation (1)). It is complete-safe 0 whenever /archerMsaOnThisReturn is false, so for every return without an MSA line 5 resolves line 3 exactly: GreaterOf(0, x) is x for a nonnegative x.
THE GATE HAS NO DEFAULT Case ON PURPOSE, so this fact stays Incomplete for a filer who is not owed Form 8889 Part I; adding a True-arm 0 would flip those filers Incomplete to Complete 0 for no tax reason — the same reasoning ../taxableHsaDistributionTotal records for its own un-defaulted Switch.
NO ROUND HERE. Line 3 arrives already rounded on the legacy arm and cents-bearing on the vector arm, line 4 is rounded at its own printed line, and the consumers (../hsaContributionLimitLessAddition and /hsaPrimaryFilerAllocatedContributionLimit) round once at line 6.
FORM 8889 PART I GATE. Read through ../hsaForm8889PartIRequired, not ../hasMadeContributionsToHsa alone: Part I is also owed to a filer who made no 2025 contributions but carries a prior-year excess into Form 5329 line 42, because Form 5329 line 43 measures the absorption against Form 8889 line 12.

Sets the value for line 16 of form 8889: line 14c minus line 15, floored at zero. The floor is printed on the form itself — "Taxable HSA distributions. Subtract line 15 from line 14c. If zero or less, enter -0-." The minuend is this filer's printed line 14c (../hsaCalculatedDistributionAmount) and the subtrahend is this filer's printed line 15 (../hsaQualifiedMedExpenses), so the tree mirrors the printed subtraction rather than re-deriving it from the per-item amounts: line 15 aggregates every item's qualified expenses before the floor applies, and flooring item by item would tax a filer whose second 1099-SA over-spent on medical care against a first that did not.
THE LINE IS COMPUTED, AND IT IS WHAT THE UNQUALIFIED-DISTRIBUTION REFUSAL NARROWS ONTO. /hsaCollectionRouteTaxableDistributions carries it to Schedule 1 line 8f, and /flowKnockoutHsaUnqualifiedDistributions refuses only a return whose positive line 16 lacks the 20%-tax exception attestation (see /hsaDistributions/*/causesUnqualifiedDistributionsKnockout).
THE OUTER GATE HAS NO DEFAULT Case ON PURPOSE. This fact stays Incomplete for a filer who cannot have HSA distributions at all (the non-HSA spouse of an MFJ pair); adding a True-arm 0 would flip those filers Incomplete to Complete 0 for no tax reason. That is NOT a silent understatement: with the gate false, ../taxableHsaDistributionTotalOrZero falls to 0, and a filer who cannot have an HSA distribution has no Form 8889 line 16 and no line 8f term, so both this fact and the alias are correct for them. A filer holding a Form 1099-SA must not BE in that state and file; that is a data-consistency question, answered by the data-consistency guard /hsaDistributions/*/hasDistributionsWithoutHsaActivity, which refuses the return rather than leaving it quietly short. Computing a line 16 here instead was considered and rejected — the coverage and contribution section is skipped for such a filer, so ../hsaCalculatedDistributionAmount (line 14c) would be built out of answers nobody gave.
BOTH INPUTS ARE GUARDED, and the else-arm is 0 rather than a partial subtraction. ../hsaCalculatedDistributionAmount is deliberately left undefined when a filer has no distributions at all, and ../hsaQualifiedMedExpenses sums the raw per-item writable, so a mid-interview item with box 1 or the qualified-expenses answer still blank would take an unguarded read Incomplete where this fact resolves Complete 0. Falling back to 0 for the SUBTRAHEND alone would instead tax the whole of line 14c on a half-answered interview. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form8889/hsa-collection-line16-med-expenses-unanswered-complete-safe.
ONE ROUNDING ARTIFACT, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND. The knockout /flowKnockoutHsaUnqualifiedDistributions compares each item's UNROUNDED modifiedDistribution against that item's UNROUNDED writableQualifiedMedExpenses, while this fact subtracts the printed aggregates — and the aggregates do not round the same number of times: line 14a rounds the gross sum, line 14b rounds the rollover sum and the withdrawn-excess sum SEPARATELY, and line 15 rounds once. So with cents in the inputs this fact can resolve $1 on a filer no item knocks out (Sigma gross 10.50, Sigma rollovers 0.40, Sigma withdrawn excess 0.40 gives 14a 11 minus 14b 0 = 14c 11 against a line 15 of 10, while every item has modifiedDistribution equal to its qualified expenses). The bound is one dollar per filer and it needs cent-level inputs to arise. /hsaCollectionRouteTaxableDistributions carries this fact to Schedule 1 line 8f, so the $1 appears as $1 of income and the two lines agree. The residue filer is also NOT swept into the refusal — /hsaDistributions/*/causesUnqualifiedDistributionsKnockout keeps its per-item first conjunct precisely so that a filer whose line 16 is positive while no item exceeds its own expenses stays allowed, and their line 17b is 20% of $1 rounded to $0.

../taxableHsaDistributionTotal read complete-safely: this filer's printed Form 8889 line 16 when that fact resolves, and 0 when it does not. The only input to the return-level /hsaCollectionRouteTaxableDistributions sum below.
THE WRAPPER IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT STYLISTIC, and simplifying it to a bare CollectionSum over ../taxableHsaDistributionTotal would take the whole return Incomplete. That fact has NO default Case on purpose (its own Description records why): it stays Incomplete for a filer who cannot have HSA distributions at all, which is the non-HSA spouse of an MFJ pair and BOTH filers on every return with no HSA. Its return-level sum feeds income /schedule1TotalOtherIncome, so an Incomplete there propagates to /otherIncome, /totalIncome and taxCalculations /totalTaxIsIncomplete (BlockSubmissionOnTrue) on essentially the whole corpus. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form8889/hsa-collection-line16-non-hsa-spouse-stays-incomplete, which asserts the per-filer fact Incomplete and this alias Complete 0 on the same return.
0 IS THE RIGHT ELSE-ARM rather than a Placeholder: a filer who cannot have an HSA distribution has no Form 8889 line 16, and a term of 0 in the Schedule 1 line 8f sum is exactly what "no Form 8889" means on that line. hsa.xml's older answer to the same problem is a filtered collection (/filersWithHsaContributions in /hsaTotalDeductibleAmount); the alias does the same job with one fewer collection.

Fact.Name: Taxable HSA distributions from the /hsaDistributions collection (Schedule 1 line 8f leg)
Fact.Description:
Both filers' printed Form 8889 line 16 on the /hsaDistributions collection route, summed for Schedule 1 Part I line 8f. Form 8889 line 16 says "Also, include this amount in the total on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), Part I, line 8f", and on MFJ each spouse files their own Form 8889, so the Schedule 1 line carries the sum of the two forms' line 16.
IT IS THE ONLY LEG. The /hsaDistributions collection is the sole intake for Form 8889 Part II; there is no separate top-level line 14a route, so there is no second intake to add beside this one and no double-intake question to police.
IT IS COMPLETE EVERYWHERE because its addend is the complete-safe alias above.
THE OUTER IsComplete(/filers) GUARD IS formW2Gs /w2gWinnings' pattern, and it is load-bearing for the same reason: a CollectionSum over a collection that was never answered resolves PLACEHOLDER, not Complete, and this fact is an addend of income /schedule1TotalOtherIncome. Without the guard the empty-graph scenario scenarios/strategies/spike.json would flip /schedule1TotalOtherIncome from Complete 0 to Placeholder 0.

Fact.Name: Line-16 amount meeting a 20%-tax exception, collection route (input to Form 8889 line 17b)
Fact.Description:
The portion of THIS filer's Form 8889 line 16 (the /hsaDistributions collection route) that was distributed after the account beneficiary dies, becomes disabled, or turns age 65, and is therefore exempt from the additional 20% tax. Taxpayer-attested. Complete-safe at every reader: unanswered means 0 here, so the whole of line 16 bears the 20% tax.
THE BOX-3 CODE DOES NOT CARRY THE DISABILITY OR DEATH EXCEPTION. The instructions list three exceptions, "distributions made after the account beneficiary: Dies, Becomes disabled or Turns age 65" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 9). IRC 223(f)(4)(B) disapplies the additional tax to a payment or distribution made after the account beneficiary becomes disabled within the meaning of section 72(m)(7) or dies, and it conditions on NOTHING about the box 3 code: 26 U.S.C. 223, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section223&num=0&edition=2024 (page 973 LEFT column of a two-column extraction; "(B) Exception for disability or death" at line 392), continuing in that page's RIGHT column at 26 U.S.C. 223, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section223&num=0&edition=2024. So a filer whose distribution is coded 1 and who became disabled, or whose account beneficiary died, holds the exception on this route — and the only way they can say so is by attesting it here, beside ../writableHsaCollectionExceptionReason.
ALL THREE GROUNDS ARE THEREFORE ATTESTED RATHER THAN DERIVED, and age 65 is no different in kind. The one age derivation, ../hsaAdditionalTaxExceptionAmountDerived, reaches only a filer whose filers:../age is 66 or more — whose 65th birthday fell before the tax year opened, so that every distribution in the year is necessarily after it (223(f)(4)(C); 26 U.S.C. 223, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section223&num=0&edition=2024, page 973 RIGHT column, "which the account beneficiary attains the" at line 328). Every other filer attests, which is what this intake is for.
AND TURNING 65 IS NOT DERIVABLE FOR THE MID-YEAR TURNER, WHOM THAT AGE READ CANNOT REACH. The exception is scoped to distributions made AFTER the beneficiary turns 65, a date-of-distribution test, and /hsaDistributions carries no distribution date. A filer who turns 65 during the year has distributions on both sides of the birthday, so a DOB-derived amount would be wrong in both directions: it would except pre-birthday distributions for a filer who turned 65 in December, and except nothing for a filer who turned 65 in January. The attested amount is the only honest input.
PER FILER, NOT PER RETURN. Form 8889 is filed per spouse, this route's line 16 is per filer, and on MFJ both spouses can have collection-route distributions with different exception facts — so the per-filer shape is the right one, and it is the only 20%-tax exception intake for Form 8889 line 16 on the return.
IT MUST BE ANSWERED WHEREVER LINE 16 IS POSITIVE, including with a 0 meaning "no exception applies": /filers/*/causesUnattestedTaxableHsaDistributionKnockout refuses the MISSING PAIR, not a particular answer — the answer is this amount AND ../writableHsaCollectionExceptionReason beside it, and either half missing refuses. Every committed case the guard actually asks therefore carries BOTH an explicit amount here and an explicit reason: three attest an amount with the reason age65, and three attest $0 with the reason "none". Three further cases carry an explicit $0 amount and no reason because their line 16 resolves 0 and ../flowShouldAskHsaCollectionExceptionAmount is false, so they are outside the asked population; one case answers neither, on purpose.
ONE SENTENCE OF THE SCREEN IS LOAD-BEARING ON A DOLLAR, and it must be shown. The opening paragraph's "distributed after the account beneficiary dies" is the IRC 223(f)(4)(B) death ground on the filer's OWN account and it is attestable. It is NOT the IRC 223(f)(8)(B) inclusion a nonspouse beneficiary takes into income when they inherit someone else's HSA - that one the graph derives for itself from the Form 1099-SA (box 3 code 4 or 6, box 4, and the pre-death expenses intake /hsaDistributions/*/writableDecedentPredeathQualifiedMedExpenses), and ../hsaCollectionExceptionAmountOrZero ADDS the derived and the attested amounts. Adding two amounts that overlap would except the same dollars twice, so the screen must keep them disjoint.
THE SENTENCE THE APPLICATION MUST PUT ON THIS SCREEN, verbatim: "Do NOT include the date-of-death value of an HSA you inherited from someone other than your spouse - that exception is already applied for you." It goes in the help text of this question, and it is the convention ../flowShouldAskHsaCollectionExceptionAmount already assumes when it stops asking a filer whose whole line 16 is the derived death inclusion.

The vocabulary of the 20%-additional-tax exception question, wherever it is asked: which of IRC 223(f)(4)'s exceptions the filer says an amount rests on, plus the "none" answer a filer with no exception gives. TWO INTAKES SHARE IT, because the grounds are the statute's and not the route's: /filers/*/writableHsaCollectionExceptionReason on the /hsaDistributions collection route, beside the attested ../writableHsaCollectionExceptionAmount, and /writableHsaPledgeAdditionalTaxExceptionReason on the return-level IRC 223(e)(2) / 408(e)(4) pledge deemed distribution, where the exception is all-or-nothing and no amount is asked.
THE THREE NAMED REASONS ARE THE INSTRUCTIONS' OWN LIST, not a vocabulary of our own: "The additional 20% tax does not apply to distributions made after the account beneficiary: Dies, Becomes disabled or Turns age 65". deathOfBeneficiary and disability are IRC 223(f)(4)(B); age65 is 223(f)(4)(C).
"none" IS A REAL ANSWER AND NOT AN ABSENT ONE. The refusal /filers/*/causesUnattestedTaxableHsaDistributionKnockout fires on the MISSING answer, so a filer whose whole line 16 bears the tax has to be able to SAY so — exactly as the sibling amount intake takes an explicit $0 rather than reading unanswered as zero.
WHY THIS CARRIES AN Export, which most EnumOptions facts in this dictionary do not, and it is the same reason /hsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonthOptions above gives. The options-set edge is an optionsPath ATTRIBUTE on the Enum element, not a Dependency, so scripts/lint_wiring.py's manifest-derived edge model cannot see either consumer above and reports the fact UNWIRED. The two sanctioned answers are a wiring_skip_list.tsv row or an Export; this takes the Export, on that sibling's and /line4cElectionOptions's precedent, because the Export states a true fact about the surface rather than asking a reader to trust a skip row.

Fact.Name: Which 20%-tax exception the attested amount rests on, collection route (Form 8889 line 17a)
Fact.Description:
WHICH of the IRC 223(f)(4) exceptions THIS filer says their ../writableHsaCollectionExceptionAmount rests on, or "none" when no exception applies to any of the distributions included on their Form 8889 line 16. Taxpayer-attested, beside the amount rather than instead of it.
IT CHANGES NO DOLLAR ON THE RETURN, ON PURPOSE, and saying so here is cheaper than a reader deriving it from the absence of a consumer. Line 17a stays the ../hsaCollectionExceptionAmountOrZero checkbox and line 17b stays 20% of (line 16 - line 17a): the printed form asks WHETHER an exception applies and for HOW MUCH, and prints no reason cell at all. What the reason buys is the AUDIT TRAIL behind the amount — the filer names the statutory ground, and ../causesUnattestedTaxableHsaDistributionKnockout refuses until they have.
THE AGE-65 ARM IS STILL DERIVED, NOT TAKEN FROM HERE. A filer who reached 65 before the tax year opened is excepted by ../hsaAdditionalTaxExceptionAmountDerived without being asked anything, and ../flowShouldAskHsaCollectionExceptionAmount does not ask them — so an age65 answer here is the MID-YEAR turner's, the one arm the date-of-birth cannot settle (../writableHsaCollectionExceptionAmount's own Description carries that measurement). 223(f)(4)(C) is not elective, so an unanswered reason never costs a derivable filer their exception.
NO CROSS-CHECK AGAINST THE AMOUNT, AND THAT IS A NAMED GAP RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. "none" beside a positive amount, or age65 beside a filer this graph reads as under 66, are both accepted as answered. The refusal asks for completeness, not consistency, and a consistency refusal would be a NEW refusal on answers the filer has given. The mid-year-65 turner is exactly why age65-beside-under-66 must stay legal.

Fact.Name: This filer had already attained the Medicare eligibility age when the tax year opened
Fact.Description:
Whether every distribution this filer could have taken during the tax year is a distribution "after the date on which the account beneficiary attains the age specified in section 1811 of the Social Security Act" — i.e. after 65 — which is the condition IRC 223(f)(4)(C) excepts from the 20% additional tax.
THE TEST IS 66 AT THE CLOSE OF THE YEAR, AND THE EXTRA YEAR IS THE POINT rather than an off-by-one. filers:/filers/*/age is the ordinary anniversary-rule age on 31 December, so age 66 there means the 65th birthday fell in the PRIOR calendar year or earlier — and therefore strictly before 1 January of this tax year, so no distribution in this year can precede it. A filer who is merely 65 at the close of the year turned 65 DURING it, and a distribution taken before their birthday is not excepted; this dictionary holds no distribution DATE, so that filer is not derivable and keeps the attestation question. filers:/filers/*/age65OrOlder is the WRONG fact here for exactly that reason: it is the end-of-year test, with the day-before-birthday exception on top.
WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT COVER, so the residue is named rather than silenced: 223(f)(4)(B)'s disability and death exceptions. This dictionary holds no disability fact and no date of death for the account beneficiary, and the box-3 distribution codes that would signal them are themselves still refused (/flowKnockoutHsaDistributionCode). Those filers keep the attestation.

Fact.Name: The 20%-additional-tax exception amount this graph can derive without asking
Fact.Description:
The portion of this filer's Form 8889 line 16 that escapes the 20% additional tax under IRC 223(f)(4) WITHOUT an attestation. On the age arm the exception is total: 223(f)(4)(C) disapplies subparagraph (A) to any distribution after the beneficiary attains 65, so for a filer who reached 65 before the tax year opened the whole of line 16 is excepted and the derived amount IS line 16.
IT IS AN EXCEPTION TO THE ADDITIONAL TAX, NOT TO THE INCOME INCLUSION, and conflating the two would be the expensive error here. 223(f)(2) still includes the unqualified portion in gross income, so line 16 and Schedule 1 line 8f are UNCHANGED by this fact; only the printed lines 17a/17b and Schedule 2 line 17c move.
THE DERIVABLE DEATH CASE, the second Case below: the IRC 223(f)(8)(B) inclusion an admitted nonspouse-beneficiary or estate death item puts on line 16 (../hsaDeathBeneficiaryInclusionTotal). i8889 exempts it in as many words - "The distribution is not subject to the additional 20% tax" - so no attestation is wanted, and the Case returns it, clamped at line 16. It is $0 for every filer with no such item.
0 ON EVERY OTHER FILER, which is a statement about what is DERIVABLE and not a statement that no exception applies. A filer who turned 65 during the year, or who is disabled, or whose ordinary code-1 distribution followed a death (the IRC 223(f)(4)(B) grounds), may well have an exception this graph cannot see — which is why ../flowShouldAskHsaCollectionExceptionAmount asks them wherever this derivation leaves a positive uncovered remainder, and why ../hsaCollectionExceptionAmountOrZero ADDS this and the attested amount and caps the sum at line 16 rather than taking a maximum: a maximum over a PARTIAL derivation would discard the filer's genuine 223(f)(4)(B) attestation on a different Form 1099-SA on the same return. The screen spec on ../writableHsaCollectionExceptionAmount keeps the two amounts disjoint so that nothing is excepted twice; the measurement is recorded on the wrapper.
Sign: NON-NEGATIVE, and bounded above by line 16 because that is what it reads.

../writableHsaCollectionExceptionAmount read complete-safely and combined with the derived exception: the derived amount alone while the attestation is unanswered, and derived + attested, capped at line 16, once it is answered. The wrapper is the completeness firewall the two line-17 facts below need — a bare unanswered Writable read would take the printed line 17a checkbox, line 17b, Schedule 2 line 17c and /totalTaxIsIncomplete Incomplete on every return that has any collection-route HSA distribution.
0 IS ALSO THE TAX-SAFE DIRECTION for the attested half: no attested exception means the whole of line 16 outside any derived exception bears the additional 20% tax. It is not, however, the CORRECT direction for a filer who is over 65 and simply was not asked, which is why /flowKnockoutHsaUnqualifiedDistributions refuses a return whose line 16 is positive and whose attestation is unanswered.
THE COMBINATION IS AN ADD-AND-CAP, NOT A MAXIMUM. A maximum is safe only while every derived arm returns the WHOLE of line 16, as the age-65 arm does. The IRC 223(f)(8)(B) death inclusion is PARTIAL - it can be a fraction of line 16 - and a maximum over a partial derivation silently throws away a taxpayer's genuine 223(f)(4)(B) attestation on the OTHER Form 1099-SA beside it.
THE TWO AMOUNTS ARE DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION, which is what makes the Add sound rather than a double count: ../writableHsaCollectionExceptionAmount's screen spec tells the filer in as many words NOT to include the date-of-death value of an HSA inherited from someone other than their spouse, because the graph derives that part itself. The two are a PAIR and neither is correct without the other.
THE CAP AT LINE 16 keeps this fact's own invariant - the exception is scoped to "any amount included on line 16", so it cannot exceed line 16 - and it also keeps the age arm non-elective, because derived + attested is never less than derived and the age arm's derived amount IS line 16. Two fixtures pin over-attestation against the cap: hsa-collection-line17b-exception-exceeds-line16 (a $5,000 attestation against a $3,000 line 16: this fact 3,000.00, printed line 17b $0.00) and hsa-collection-line17a-checkbox-no-line16-distributions (a $6,000 attestation against a line 16 of $0: this fact 0.00, the printed line 17a checkbox false because ../hsaCollectionRouteExceptionAppliesCheckbox takes its own min against line 16, and printed line 17b $0.00).

Whether this filer owes an answer to the 20%-tax exception question on the /hsaDistributions collection route: true exactly when their Form 8889 line 16 is positive, because the exception is scoped to "the distributions included on line 16" and a filer with no such distributions has nothing to except. The module's own flowShouldAsk idiom (../flowShouldAskForHsaHdhpCoverageType and its siblings): the attestation existing is not enough if nothing says when it must be asked. /flowKnockoutHsaUnqualifiedDistributions reads this fact and refuses the return when the answer is owed and missing.

Form 8889 line 17a for this filer's collection-route Form 8889, a CHECKBOX: "If any of the distributions included on line 16 meet any of the Exceptions to the Additional 20% Tax (see instructions), check here." True exactly when min(line 16, ../hsaCollectionExceptionAmountOrZero) is greater than 0.
THE min IS THE PRINTED SCOPING RULE: the test is scoped to "the distributions INCLUDED ON LINE 16", so a line 16 of 0 leaves the box unchecked no matter what the filer attested. It is not the same test as "line 17b is 0" — a PARTIAL exception checks this box AND leaves a nonzero line 17b. ../hsaCollectionExceptionAmountOrZero caps ITSELF at line 16, so the min is redundant on paper; it is KEPT, because it is this printed cell's own statement of the scoping rule and must not depend on a sibling keeping its cap.
NO DEFAULT CASE, ON PURPOSE. This is a printed, mef-exported line of a Form 8889, so it resolves exactly where that form's line 16 does and stays Incomplete for a filer who cannot have HSA distributions at all — the posture ../taxableHsaDistributionTotal takes. The sibling line 17b below is deliberately NOT gated this way, because it is an addend of a return-level sum rather than a printed export.

Form 8889 line 17b for this filer's collection-route Form 8889: 20% of the portion of line 16 that meets none of the exceptions, i.e. 20% x max(0, line 16 minus the attested exception amount). The instruction is printed: "Enter on line 17b only 20% (0.20) of any amount included on line 16 that does not meet any of the exceptions."
COMPLETE-SAFE RATHER THAN GATED, unlike the line 17a checkbox above. This fact is not exported to MeF; its job is to be an addend of /hsaCollectionRouteAdditionalTax20PctTotal, and an addend must resolve wherever the sum is taken. It therefore reads ../taxableHsaDistributionTotalOrZero and is Complete 0 for a filer who cannot have HSA distributions, where the printed line 16 and line 17a are Incomplete. Nothing prints this 0, so the asymmetry costs no wrong form.
THE ROUNDING IS THE ENGINE'S HALF-UP TO WHOLE DOLLARS, applied once at the end - pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form8889/hsa-collection-distribution-code-normal-computes, which carries the 600.60-rounds-to-601 case.

Fact.Name: Additional 20% tax on collection-route HSA distributions (Schedule 2 line 17c leg)
Fact.Description:
Both filers' collection-route Form 8889 line 17b, summed for Schedule 2 Part II line 17c ("Additional tax on HSA distributions. Attach Form 8889") to line 18 to line 21 to Form 1040 line 23. On MFJ each spouse files their own Form 8889, so the Schedule 2 line carries the sum of the two forms' line 17b.
THE ONLY LEG OF THAT PRINTED LINE, for the same reason as its income-side twin /hsaCollectionRouteTaxableDistributions above: the /hsaDistributions collection is the sole intake for Form 8889 Part II. taxCalculations /line21OfSchedule2 and form2210's Schedule 2 line-17c term read this fact alone.
THE OUTER IsComplete(/filers) GUARD is the same formW2Gs /w2gWinnings pattern the income leg uses, and for the same measured reason: a CollectionSum over a never-answered collection resolves Placeholder, and this fact is an addend of taxCalculations /line21OfSchedule2.

Fact.Name: Which IRC 223(f)(4) exception the pledge deemed distribution meets (writable)
Fact.Description:
Whether the IRC 223(f)(4)(A) 20% additional tax reaches the pledged amount, and on which statutory ground it does not. Taxpayer-attested and return-level, beside the pledge amount form8889 /writableHsaPledgedAssetsFairMarketValue.
ALL OR NOTHING, WHICH IS WHY IT IS A REASON AND NOT AN AMOUNT. The line-16 route takes an exception AMOUNT because line 16 aggregates many distributions and an exception can cover some of them. A pledge is ONE deemed distribution at ONE moment: IRC 223(f)(4)(B) disapplies the tax "if the payment or distribution is made after the account beneficiary becomes disabled within the meaning of section 72(m)(7) or dies" and 223(f)(4)(C) disapplies it "to any payment or distribution after the date on which the account beneficiary attains the age specified in section 1811 of the Social Security Act", so either the pledge is after that date or it is not and no split is possible. The answer excepts the whole amount or none of it.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION (the application builds the screen from this Description and never opens an IRS document).
THE QUESTION: "When you pledged the HSA as security for the loan, had the account owner already turned 65, become disabled, or died?"
THE OPTIONS AND THE LABELS TO PRINT BESIDE THEM: age65 is "Yes, they had already turned 65"; disability is "Yes, they were disabled"; deathOfBeneficiary is "Yes, they had died"; none is "No, none of these applied".
HELP TEXT: "Pledging an HSA as security for a loan counts as taking that money out of the account, so it is taxed as income. On top of the income tax there is an extra 20% tax, unless the account owner had already turned 65, was disabled, or had died at the time of the pledge. Answer for the person whose HSA was pledged, not for whoever signed the loan." (Paraphrasing the 2025 Instructions for Form 8889, "Exceptions to the Additional 20% Tax": "The additional 20% tax does not apply to distributions made after the account beneficiary: Dies, Becomes disabled or Turns age 65"; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 9. The statute is IRC 223(f)(4)(B), 26 U.S.C. 223, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section223&num=0&edition=2024 continuing at 26 U.S.C. 223, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section223&num=0&edition=2024(f)(4)(C), 26 U.S.C. 223, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section223&num=0&edition=2024.)
ASKED WHEN: form8889 /hasTopLevelHsaPledgedAsSecurity is true, immediately after the pledge amount question. Asked ONCE FOR THE RETURN and not per filer, because the attestation it follows is return-level for the reason the form8889 module header gives. Never asked otherwise.
PRE-SELECT age65 WHERE THE RETURN ALREADY SHOWS IT: on a return with a single filer whose filers /filers/*/age is 66 or more, that filer had already attained 65 before the tax year opened, so age65 is the correct answer and the screen should offer it pre-selected while still letting the filer change it. The graph does not derive it because this question is return-level and a joint return does not say whose HSA was pledged.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED. hsa /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionFMV has its pledge arm for exactly this case and for a pledge amount left unanswered. Both guesses are wrong in a direction that matters: reading unanswered as "none" charges a 65-year-old a tax the statute does not impose, and reading it as an exception drops a tax the statute does impose.
VALIDATION: Enum over /hsaCollectionExceptionReasonOptions, the same four options the line-16 route's reason intake uses. "none" is a real answer and the one most filers give; it is not the same state as leaving the question blank.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /hsaPledgeAdditionalTaxExceptionAttested and, through it, /hsaPledgeSchedule2Line17zAdditional20PctTax, which is Schedule 2 (Form 1040) Part II line 17z and an addend of line 18, line 21 and Form 1040 line 23. It moves no income: IRC 223(f)(2) includes the pledged amount in gross income whatever the answer, so Schedule 1 line 8f is unchanged by it.
NO CROSS-CHECK AGAINST THE AGE THIS GRAPH HOLDS, a named gap rather than an oversight and for the reason the line-16 route's reason intake gives: a filer who turned 65 during the year is excepted for a pledge made after the birthday and not for one made before it, this dictionary holds no pledge date, and a consistency refusal would be a NEW refusal.

Fact.Name: The pledge 20%-tax exception reason was supplied
Fact.Description: The "source answered" predicate for /writableHsaPledgeAdditionalTaxExceptionReason, and the second thing the narrowed guard /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionFMV reads. IsComplete over a BARE optional Writable with no default and no complete-safe wrapper of its own, so it is false until the filer picks an option and true the moment they do, the "none" answer included. It is NOT IsComplete over a complete-safe fact, which would be the always-true trap.

Fact.Name: An IRC 223(f)(4) exception was attested for the pledge deemed distribution
Fact.Description:
The filer named one of IRC 223(f)(4)'s statutory grounds for the pledged amount, rather than "none". Complete-safe FALSE when the question is unanswered, which is every return in the committed corpus, so nothing that reads this fact can go Incomplete by contagion.
FALSE IS NOT "NO EXCEPTION APPLIES" HERE, and the difference is carried by a different fact. This one is false both for the filer who answered "none" and for the filer who has not answered at all; what tells them apart is /hasAnsweredHsaPledgeAdditionalTaxExceptionReason, and the unanswered filer is REFUSED by /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionFMV before this fact decides anything. So the 20% tax reads both facts and never charges a tax on the strength of a blank.

Fact.Name: Additional 20% tax on the pledged HSA amount (Schedule 2 line 17z leg)
Fact.Description:
IRC 223(f)(4)(A)'s 20 percent additional tax on the IRC 223(e)(2) / 408(e)(4) pledge deemed distribution, and the Schedule 2 (Form 1040) Part II line 17z leg that carries it to line 18, to line 21 and to Form 1040 line 23. The banner above this fact carries the statutory chain, the i8889 sentence that charges the tax on both deemed-distribution bullets alike, and the 17z instruction that admits a tax no itemized line carries.
THE BASE IS THE AMOUNT INCLUDED IN GROSS INCOME, WHICH IS ONE FACT AND NOT TWO. 223(f)(4)(A) measures the tax on "the amount which is so includible", so this reads form8889 /schedule1Line8fPledgedHsaFmvIncome, the Schedule 1 line 8f leg itself, rather than re-deriving the amount from the intake behind it. That leg is already gated on the attestation and on the answer and is already a complete-safe $0 off its population, so the tax inherits both properties.
NOTHING IS CHARGED ON A BLANK. The computing arm requires the pledge attestation, an answered pledge amount AND an answered exception reason; anything less falls to the $0 arm, and /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionFMV refuses that return anyway. An attested exception on any of IRC 223(f)(4)(B)'s or (C)'s three grounds takes the tax to $0 while leaving the income alone, which is what those subparagraphs say: they disapply subparagraph (A), not 223(f)(2).
THE ROUNDING IS THE ENGINE'S HALF-UP TO WHOLE DOLLARS applied once at the end, the same shape as the line-16 route's /filers/*/hsaCollectionRouteAdditionalTax20Pct.
COMPLETE-SAFE $0 AND $0 ON EVERY COMMITTED SCENARIO, which is load-bearing because the consumers are shipping totals: no committed scenario answers the pledge attestation, so schedule2 /line18OfSchedule2, taxCalculations /line21OfSchedule2 and Form 1040 line 23 are byte-identical.
CONSUMERS: schedule2 /line18OfSchedule2 (the printed line 18 sum) and schedule2 /schedule2Line17zAnyOtherTaxesPrinted (the printed 17z box). Both are required and neither double counts, for the reason the Schedule 1 line 8f leg records: the total adds the legs individually and never reads the printed-box fact, so an amount named in only one of the two makes the filed schedule fail to foot.
Reported on line 16 of form 8889.
Primary filer total HSA distributions excess contributions amount
Secondary filer total HSA distributions excess contributions amount
Amount of HSA excess contributions withdrawn in time
Reported on line 14b of form 8889.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's IRC 223(f)(8)(B) nonspouse-beneficiary death inclusion
Fact.Description: The primary filer's admitted death-beneficiary items, summed. Rounded here for the same reason the sibling line-15 and rollover sums are: it is compared against, and subtracted from, already-rounded printed lines.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's IRC 223(f)(8)(B) nonspouse-beneficiary death inclusion
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's twin of the fact above. Form 8889 is a per-individual form ("If married filing jointly and both you and your spouse have HSAs, complete a separate Form 8889 for each of you", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 4), so the exception follows the filer who inherited the account and not the return.

Fact.Name: This filer's IRC 223(f)(8)(B) death inclusion, the part of line 16 the 20% tax cannot reach
Fact.Description: This filer's admitted IRC 223(f)(8)(B) death inclusions (nonspouse beneficiary and estate), summed, read COMPLETE-SAFELY. The two filtered collections above are Switches with no default arm, so they are Incomplete for a filer who cannot have HSA distributions at all; this fact fences every read with IsComplete and falls to $0, because its only consumer (../hsaAdditionalTaxExceptionAmountDerived) is itself read by the printed line 17a checkbox, line 17b and Schedule 2 line 17c on essentially the whole corpus. An unfenced read there would take /totalTaxIsIncomplete Incomplete on every return with no HSA, which is the measured failure mode /filers/*/taxableHsaDistributionTotalOrZero's Description records for its own wrapper. It sums whatever the per-item /hsaDistributions/*/deathBeneficiaryInclusionAmount carries - the nonspouse-beneficiary arm and the estate arm alike.
Primary filer total HSA qualified medical expenses.
Secondary filer total HSA qualified medical expenses.
Reported on line 15 of form 8889.
Determines the net amount of HSA distributions.
