Fact.Name: This filer reported an HSA funding distribution the return does not model
Fact.Description:
Whether this filer has told the HSA section they made a qualified HSA funding distribution that this return cannot report end to end. It is the per-filer term of /flowKnockoutMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistribution.
WHY THE KNOCKOUT IS NARROW. The transfer itself is handled: form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/line4cHfdExclusion takes the HFD off Form 1040 line 4b and ../hsaFundingDistributionsTotal reports it on Form 8889 line 10, so the two printed places an HFD appears both carry it. Refusing on the yes/no answer alone would make that whole Exception unreachable, because the HSA coverage-and-contributions section cannot be completed without answering the yes/no question and answering it truthfully would fire the refusal.
WHAT REFUSES. (1) THE RETURN DOES NOT CARRY THE TRANSFER: the filer said yes here and no Form 1099-R of theirs elects an HFD, so line 10 would be $0 while the filer says otherwise. A data-contradiction with a filer-side remedy. (2) THE TESTING-PERIOD QUESTION IS UNANSWERED WHERE IT MATTERS: line 10 is above $0, the filer states they were NOT an eligible individual all year, and ../writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth is unanswered. The return then knows a testing period exists and cannot tell whether it was breached, or in which tax year, so it can neither compute Part III line 19 nor rule it out. A data-completeness refusal on a MISSING INPUT - which is the only honest ground for refusing a case the dictionary can otherwise compute. (3) A PRIOR-YEAR HFD WHOSE TESTING PERIOD FAILS IN THIS YEAR, with its amount unanswered. Such a transfer is Part III line 19 too, and the question below ("did you make one") is asked of the present tax year and cannot see a 2024 transfer. THE FIRST CASE is the completeness half of that arm: it refuses exactly the slice the return cannot decide (the prior-year gate answered yes, the amount unanswered - see ../writableHsaPriorYearFundingDistributionFailedThisYear) and does not touch the present-year Case where that gate is answered no or left unanswered.
WHAT COMPUTES: a filer who states they were NOT an eligible individual for the whole tax year AND answers the testing-period question. Name a month of THIS tax year and /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome carries their line 10 onto Form 8889 Part III line 19, /hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncomeAndAdditionalTax sums both spouses onto Schedule 1 line 8f and /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureAdditionalTax takes each spouse's 10% onto Schedule 2 line 17d. Answer "none", or name a 2026 month, and line 19 is $0 - the transfer's testing period was not breached inside this tax year, and a breach in a later year belongs to that year's return (IRC 408(d)(9)(D)(i)(I)).
WHY ARM (2) IS NEEDED. Without the eligibility conjunct an unanswerable case would be resolved by charging it: partOfYear coverage alone would be read as a testing-period failure in this tax year, which is neither necessary (the period starts at the month of the transfer, so earlier ineligible months are outside it) nor sufficient (a failure after December is a 2026 inclusion). Arm (2) refuses exactly the undecidable slice, and no wider.
THE VERDICT IS PRESERVED EVERYWHERE AND THE COMPLETENESS IS NOT. The present-year Case tests the yes/no fact itself rather than an IsComplete of it, so where ../hasMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistributionDerived cannot be decided this fact falls through past it - to the default Placeholder false at the bottom, the same "no knockout fires" rendering /flowIsKnockedOut carries - rather than resolving Incomplete, which would omit it from a snapshot. The inner Any is what keeps the ANSWERED-yes population Complete even when the eligibility chain is not.

Knockout due to a qualified HSA funding distribution this return cannot report.
The transfer computes end to end - off Form 1040 line 4b through form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/line4cHfdExclusion and onto Form 8889 line 10 through /filers/*/hsaFundingDistributionsTotal - so what refuses is the residue named on /filers/*/hasUnmodeledHsaFundingDistribution: a filer who reports an HFD the return does not carry; a filer whose line 10 is above $0, who states they were not an eligible individual all year, and who has not answered /filers/*/writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth; and a prior-year HFD failed this year whose amount is unanswered. EVERY ARM IS A MISSING-INPUT OR CONTRADICTION REFUSAL. Form 8889 Part III line 19 itself COMPUTES: it is the answered case that leaves this guard, not the scope.
Its type, BlockSubmissionOnTrue, Export and flow:/flowIsKnockedOut membership are those of a refusal with a live contract, on /knockoutIraSepSimple's precedent for the same shape.
WHERE THE QUESTION IS UNANSWERED this fact resolves Placeholder false - the "no knockout fires" rendering /flowIsKnockedOut already carries - rather than Incomplete, so it appears in every snapshot and moves no verdict.
Whether TP made HSA contribution during testing period of TP - 1

Fact.Name: TP has additional conctributions during testing period TY-1
Fact.Description: TP confirmed addtional contributions during testing period TY-1

Whether TP have additional income due to use of last month rule during testing period of TP - 1. This is the SCREEN GATE for the line 18 group below, not the refusal trigger by itself: a yes answer opens the per-filer prior-year intake pair (/filers/*/writableHsaLastMonthRuleExcessContributions and /filers/*/writableHsaTestingPeriodExceptionReason), and /flowKnockoutHsaTestingPeriodAdditionalIncomeYes refuses only while that group is unanswered for a filer in the testing-period flow.

The answer set for /filers/*/writableHsaTestingPeriodExceptionReason: "none" plus the two statutory grounds - death, and disability within the meaning of IRC 72(m)(7) - on which BOTH testing-period inclusions and their 10% additional taxes are disapplied: IRC 223(b)(8)(B)(ii) for the line 18 last-month-rule leg and IRC 408(d)(9)(D)(ii) for the line 19 funding-distribution leg, in identical words ("shall not apply if the individual ceased to be an eligible individual by reason of the death of the individual or the individual becoming disabled (within the meaning of section 72(m)(7))"). ONE enum, BOTH legs, because the fact attested is a fact about the individual, not about either leg.
72(m)(7) IS ITS OWN TEST and none of the three shipping disability vocabularies contains it - /filers/*/isDisabled is IRC 21(b)(1)(C), elderlyAndDisabled's is IRC 22(e)(3), and the 223(f)(4)(B) distribution arm is the attestation - which is why this is a new intake rather than a read of a live answer (the line 19 fact, /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome, records the same finding). "none" is an option rather than a companion Boolean on /hsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonthOptions' own precedent: one fact, one answer, no contradiction. It serves /flowKnockoutHsaTestingPeriodAdditionalIncomeYes.

Fact.Name: Why this filer ceased to be an eligible individual during an HSA testing period, if death or 72(m)(7) disability
Fact.Description: This filer's attested ground, if any, for the IRC 223(b)(8)(B)(ii) / 408(d)(9)(D)(ii) exception: whether they ceased to be an eligible individual during the testing period by reason of death or of becoming disabled within the meaning of IRC 72(m)(7). Answered "death" or "disability", BOTH Part III legs and their 10% additional taxes go to $0 for this filer - line 18 through /filers/*/hsaLine18LastMonthRuleIncome and line 19 through /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome, via ../hsaTestingPeriodExceptionAttested. Answered "none" or left UNANSWERED, both legs charge in full: the exception is an affirmative claim, so the unanswered case keeps the shipped taxpayer-adverse-but-disclosed behavior of the line 19 leg rather than widening a computing path with a new refusal. (The line 18 leg is different: there the intake GROUP gates /flowKnockoutHsaTestingPeriodAdditionalIncomeYes, because requiring the group answered refuses only the undecidable slice of a population that would otherwise have no line 18 at all.) Asked by the application beside ../writableHsaLastMonthRuleExcessContributions on the testing-period screens (grouped writables).

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 18 intake - this filer's prior-year contributions in excess of the limitation redetermined without the last-month rule
Fact.Description: This filer's attested Form 8889 Part III line 18 amount: the excess of what they contributed for the PRIOR year over the prior-year limitation redetermined without the last-month rule - IRC 223(b)(8)(B)(i)(I)'s "aggregate amount of all contributions to the health savings account of the individual which could not have been made but for subparagraph (A)". ATTESTED, NOT DERIVED, and the Line 18 instructions put the determination on the taxpayer in as many words: "You can use the Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet (in these instructions) for the year the contribution was made to determine the contribution you could have made if the last-month rule did not apply. Enter on line 18 the excess of the amount contributed over the redetermined amount." The two inputs of a derivation (the prior year's contributed amount and the prior year's redetermined limitation) are nowhere in this TY2025 graph - the records contract names both - so this intake is the contract's own first honest shape, the same taxpayer-attestation posture as the 20%-exception amount. $0 is a real answer (used the last-month rule, stayed within the redetermined limitation). THE WRITABLE WINS where it is answered: line 18 computes from it even where the screening yes/no was answered no, on /filers/*/writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth's writable-wins precedent. Asked by the application beside ../writableHsaTestingPeriodExceptionReason (grouped writables).

Fact.Name: This filer attested the 223(b)(8)(B)(ii) / 408(d)(9)(D)(ii) death-or-disability exception
Fact.Description: Whether this filer's ../writableHsaTestingPeriodExceptionReason is answered with a statutory ground (death or 72(m)(7) disability) rather than "none". The single switch both Part III legs read: attested, /filers/*/hsaLine18LastMonthRuleIncome and /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome are both $0 and the 10% tax follows them down. Complete-safe FALSE while the reason is unanswered, so both legs keep charging and nothing goes Incomplete by contagion.

Fact.Name: This filer is in the testing-period flow and the line 18 intake group is unanswered
Fact.Description: Whether this filer is in the testing-period check flow (../hasToShowTestingPeriodCheck) and the line 18 prior-year intake group is not yet served: neither an attested exception (../hsaTestingPeriodExceptionAttested, which needs no amount - the statutory ground zeroes the leg by itself) nor BOTH group answers (../writableHsaLastMonthRuleExcessContributions and ../writableHsaTestingPeriodExceptionReason). The Count of these across /filers is what /flowKnockoutHsaTestingPeriodAdditionalIncomeYes refuses on: yes-answered AND any in-flow filer still missing the group. COMPLETE BY CONSTRUCTION for every filer - the flow gate is wrapped in its own IsComplete (a filer whose hasToShowTestingPeriodCheck cannot resolve is not refusable on a question nobody could have asked), and every other term is an IsComplete or a complete-safe helper - so the return-level Count always resolves and the knockout cannot go Incomplete by contagion.

Fact.Name: Whether this filer had a prior-year (2024) IRA-to-HSA qualified HSA funding distribution whose testing period was first breached in a 2025 month
Fact.Description:
THE GATE FOR ARM (4) of /flowKnockoutMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistribution (interpretation: owner ruling). This Description and ../writableHsaPriorYearFundingDistributionFailedAmount's together are the FULL screen specification for the application to build directly, without re-opening an IRS document.
THE QUESTION. "In 2024, did you make an IRA-to-HSA qualified HSA funding distribution (a one-time trustee-to-trustee transfer) and then, at some point during that transfer's 12-month testing period, stop being an eligible individual in a month of 2025?"
HELP TEXT (paraphrasing IRC 408(d)(9)(D) and the 2025 Instructions for Form 8889's line-10 testing-period paragraph; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 8): "A qualified HSA funding distribution is a once-in-a-lifetime, tax-free transfer from an IRA into an HSA. Making one starts a testing period running from the month of the transfer through the last day of the 12th month after it (26 U.S.C. 408, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section408&num=0&edition=2024). If you stopped being an HSA-eligible individual at any point during that period, the transfer becomes taxable income in the tax year in which you FIRST failed to be eligible, unless you ceased to be eligible because of death or disability. Answer yes here only if that first failed month fell in 2025. If you made the transfer in 2025, answer the earlier questions on this screen instead; if the failure fell in 2026, report it on your 2026 return."
ASKED-WHEN: per filer, in the existing TY-1 testing-period section (../hasToShowTestingPeriodCheck), beside ../writableHsaLastMonthRuleExcessContributions and ../writableHsaTestingPeriodExceptionReason - one more grouped writable on the same screen family, gated on the same flow entry a prior-year-only filer already reaches.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: NOT REPORTED. An unanswered gate is not itself refusable - a filer who has never been shown the screen is not blocked by it, and ../hasUnmodeledHsaFundingDistribution's default Case holds for this filer. ANSWERED YES WITH THE AMOUNT UNANSWERED IS REFUSED: the FIRST Case on ../hasUnmodeledHsaFundingDistribution, ahead of the present-year Case, is When(All(IsComplete(this), this)) Then Not(IsComplete(../writableHsaPriorYearFundingDistributionFailedAmount)) - the same data-completeness posture as the neighboring line-18 intake. IT MUST BE FIRST: a prior-year-only filer reaches this section through ../flowSkipToHsaTestingPeriodContributionCheck, which means ../hasMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistributionDerived (the one-Case Switch, no default, that the present-year Case tests) is INCOMPLETE for exactly that filer, so a Case placed second could never run for the population this gate exists to serve.
VALIDATION: Boolean. No Limit, no Dependency - a leaf (lint_writable_dependency precedent, same as ../writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth).
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: answered yes, WITH ../writableHsaPriorYearFundingDistributionFailedAmount also answered, adds that amount onto ../hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome (Form 8889 line 19) alongside the present-year leg. Answered no, or left unanswered, nothing changes anywhere. ONE ANSWER PER FILER, THE FORM'S OWN QUANTIFIER: Form 8889 line 19 is "the total of any qualified HSA funding distribution" (i8889 lines 515-517, one per-filer sum), so the window rule is carried by the ATTESTATION wording above rather than by a per-transfer intake - the same fold line 18 already makes for the last-month rule.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 19 intake - this filer's total 2024 qualified HSA funding distributions whose testing period was first breached in 2025
Fact.Description:
THE AMOUNT HALF of the arm-(4) gate above, ../writableHsaPriorYearFundingDistributionFailedThisYear. ATTESTED, on ../writableHsaLastMonthRuleExcessContributions's precedent: the neighboring line-18 intake is attested rather than derived for the identical reason - the inputs a derivation would need (the 2024 transfer amount and its testing-period breach date) are nowhere in this TY2025 graph, and the taxpayer already holds the number the form asks for directly.
THE QUESTION, the line 19 instruction's own words (2025 Instructions for Form 8889, Line 19, "Enter the total of any qualified HSA funding distribution (see line 10)"; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 9): "Enter the total of those 2024 transfers."
ASKED-WHEN: immediately after ../writableHsaPriorYearFundingDistributionFailedThisYear is answered yes, same screen (grouped writables), same section as the line-18 intake.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED where the gate is yes - see the gate's own Description for the Case wired on ../hasUnmodeledHsaFundingDistribution. Not reached at all where the gate is no or unanswered.
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0 - kept for the same reason ../writableHsaLastMonthRuleExcessContributions keeps it: a non-negative amount is the only constraint the form states, even though a real $0 answer here is not a meaningful case (the gate being yes already asserts a real transfer).
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: added onto ../hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome (Form 8889 line 19) alongside the present-year leg, WHERE ANSWERED - the writable wins, on ../writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth's precedent, so this leg computes even for a prior-year-only filer whose ../hasMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistributionDerived is Incomplete rather than false. The death-or-disability exception (../hsaTestingPeriodExceptionAttested) zeroes THIS leg too, same as the present-year leg and the line-18 leg - one shared attestation, three legs. ONE ANSWER PER FILER, NOT PER TRANSFER: the same taxpayer-adverse approximation ../writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth's Description already discloses on the present-year leg (Pub 969 gives each transfer its own testing period; this intake sums them into one per-filer total, exactly as the printed line does) - stated here rather than left silent.

Fact.Name: Knockout: last-month-rule testing-period income answered yes but the line 18 intake group is unanswered
Fact.Description:
TP answered yes to additional income from use of the last-month rule AND some filer in the testing-period flow has not yet answered the line 18 intake group.
The attested prior-year intake exists (/filers/*/writableHsaLastMonthRuleExcessContributions, with /filers/*/writableHsaTestingPeriodExceptionReason carrying the 223(b)(8)(B)(ii) death-or-disability ground beside it), so a yes-answered return whose in-flow filers have all answered the group COMPUTES line 18 and files, and this guard is the data-completeness refusal of the unanswered group (Count of /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodPriorYearIntakeMissing above zero).
WHY THE YES/NO STAYS as the screen gate rather than being replaced: wholesale replacement would strand every historic yes-answer and turn the unanswered-amount population into a silent $0 line 18 - the exact adverse-or-favourable guess this module refuses to make elsewhere. The yes opens the group and the group's absence refuses. CONSEQUENCE, stated because the contract's second finding depends on it: the SCREENING-REACHABILITY defect (a filer who used the last-month rule, contributed OUTSIDE the testing window, and answers the /someFilersMadeTestingPeriodContribution screen no is never asked any of this) remains - it dissolves only under full replacement of the screening pair, which is SERVICE-visible surgery not performed here. It stays recorded on the contract.

Fact.Name: Options for the first month of an HSA testing period in which the filer was not an eligible individual
Fact.Description:
The answer set for /filers/*/writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth: "none" plus every calendar month a TY2025 qualified HSA funding distribution's testing period can reach.
WHY THE SET SPANS TWO YEARS AND STOPS THERE. IRC 408(d)(9)(D)(iii) makes the testing period "the period beginning with the month in which the qualified HSA funding distribution is contributed and ending on the last day of the 12th month following that month". The transfer this fact is asked about is reported on THIS return's Form 8889 line 10, so it was contributed in a 2025 month; the earliest testing period is therefore Jan-2025 through Jan-2026 and the latest is Dec-2025 through Dec-2026. No month outside 2025-2026 can be the first ineligible month of a TY2025 transfer, and every month inside them can.
WHY THE YEAR IS PART OF THE ANSWER RATHER THAN A SEPARATE QUESTION. The year is the whole of what decides which RETURN carries the income: IRC 408(d)(9)(D)(i)(I) puts the inclusion in "the taxable year in which occurs the first month in the testing period for which such individual is not an eligible individual". A bare month name (the shipping /monthOptions) cannot say whether "June" is June 2025 or June 2026, and those two answers produce opposite TY2025 returns. Reusing /monthOptions here would re-introduce exactly the ambiguity this options list exists to remove.
WHY "none" IS AN OPTION RATHER THAN A SECOND BOOLEAN. A filer who remained an eligible individual through every month of the testing period so far has an answer, and it is not the absence of one. Splitting it into a companion yes/no would let the two facts contradict each other - "I maintained eligibility" alongside a named failure month - and nothing could adjudicate that. One fact, one answer, no contradiction. UNANSWERED still means unanswered, and /filers/*/hasUnmodeledHsaFundingDistribution refuses on it.
WHY THIS CARRIES AN Export, which most EnumOptions facts in this dictionary do not. The options-set edge is an optionsPath ATTRIBUTE on the Enum element, not a Dependency, so scripts/lint_wiring.py's manifest-derived edge model cannot see the writable consuming it and reports the fact UNWIRED. The two sanctioned answers are a wiring_skip_list.tsv row or an Export; this takes the Export, on /line4cElectionOptions's precedent (form1099Rs), because the Export states a true fact about the surface rather than asking a reader to trust a skip row.

Fact.Name: The first month of this filer's HSA funding distribution testing period in which they were not an eligible individual
Fact.Description:
WHAT IT ASKS. "Your IRA-to-HSA transfer opened a testing period that runs from the month of the transfer through the last day of the 12th month after it. What was the FIRST month in that window in which you were not an eligible individual? Answer 'none' if you were an eligible individual in every month of it."
WHY IT HAS TO EXIST. Charging line 19 off ../wasEligibleToMakeHsaContributionsAllYear alone - which is ../hsaHdhpCoverageStatus == partOfYear plus the other-coverage tests - would be wrong, because "HDHP coverage part of the year" is NEITHER NECESSARY NOR SUFFICIENT for a testing-period failure. It is wrong in both directions of realization, and both are the MODAL member of the population, not an edge:
NEVER FAILED. Coverage starts in March, the transfer is made in April, coverage runs through December. The testing period is Apr-2025 through Apr-2026 and nothing inside 2025 breaches it, so TY2025 line 19 is $0 - but the filer is partOfYear, so a coverage-based test would charge the whole line 10 plus 10%. To make a funding distribution at all you need an HSA, which needs HDHP coverage, so "coverage begins mid-year, transfer after it begins" is the ORDINARY shape of a partOfYear filer with a line 10, not an unusual one.
FAILED IN THE WRONG YEAR. A December-2025 transfer whose eligibility breaks in June 2026 fails a testing period that runs to December 2026. IRC 408(d)(9)(D)(i)(I) puts the inclusion in the taxable year containing the FIRST ineligible month of the testing period, so that is a 2026 return, not this one; Publication 969's Example 1 has this exact shape on the neighbouring last-month-rule leg and the IRS puts it on the 2026 return. A coverage-based test would charge it in TY2025.
WHAT UNANSWERED MEANS - REFUSED, NARROWLY, NOT DEFAULTED. Where the filer has a line 10 above $0 and is not eligible all year and this question is unanswered, the return cannot decide the case and does not guess: ../hasUnmodeledHsaFundingDistribution fires on exactly that conjunction and /flowKnockoutMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistribution blocks submission. That is the "refuse only when the input is missing" posture: an ANSWERED failure computes, and nothing computes without asking. Nothing else in the tree goes Incomplete on an unanswered value: /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome resolves a complete $0.
THE WRITABLE WINS ON CONTRADICTION, on /writableHsaEitherSpouseHadFamilyCoverage's precedent. A filer who names a 2025 failure month while their coverage answer says allYear gets line 19 charged: the statute keys on the testing-period month, and this fact is the only place that month is stated. ../wasEligibleToMakeHsaContributionsAllYear is not read by line 19 at all; it survives only in the refusal conjunction, deciding WHEN the question must be asked.
ONE ANSWER PER FILER, NOT PER TRANSFER - an approximation, stated rather than left silent because it is taxpayer-ADVERSE. Publication 969 says "Each qualified HSA funding distribution allowed has its own testing period" and works an example of two transfers in one year with two different windows. This intake asks one question per filer and line 19 charges that filer's WHOLE line 10 when the named month falls in 2025, so a filer with two transfers - one whose window was breached in 2025 and one made after eligibility was regained, whose window was not - is charged on both. Charging the per-transfer amount would need an intake that carries amount AND month per transfer; it is not built here.
NO Limit, NO Dependency, DELIBERATELY. This is a leaf (lint_writable_dependency): every consistency relationship it participates in is expressed as a derived sink - ../hsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonthIsThisTaxYear - and, where the answer is missing, as the refusal above.

Fact.Name: This filer's first testing-period month of ineligibility falls in tax year 2025
Fact.Description:
Whether ../writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth names a month of THIS tax year. This is the whole of the test IRC 408(d)(9)(D)(i)(I) applies to decide whether the funding distribution belongs on THIS return: the inclusion lands in the taxable year containing the first testing-period month of ineligibility, so a 2026 month is a 2026 return's line 19 and produces $0 here, exactly as "none" does.
FALSE, AND COMPLETE, WHERE THE QUESTION IS UNANSWERED. The IsComplete arm is tested FIRST so an unanswered intake yields a resolving false rather than an Incomplete that would carry incompleteness through line 19, Schedule 1 line 9 and Schedule 2 line 21 into /totalTax. That false is not a claim that the filer never failed - it is the $0 half of a return that is simultaneously REFUSED by /flowKnockoutMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistribution, which is where the missing answer is actually reported to the filer. Reading this fact as an assertion about the taxpayer without reading the refusal alongside it would be a mistake.
A SINK, in the lint_writable_dependency sense: it reads the writable, the writable reads nothing, and every downstream edge points into the existing DAG.

Fact.Name: Whether this filer had a prior-year HSA funding distribution failure this year, complete-safe
Fact.Description: Passes the prior-year testing-period yes/no answer through when it is answered and supplies false when it is unanswered, so the line 19 amount branch cannot select on an incomplete gate. The original writable remains the intake; this is only a complete-safe routing alias.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 19 - this filer's qualified HSA funding distribution, included in income on a testing-period failure
Fact.Description:
This filer's own Form 8889 Part III line 19: the qualified HSA funding distribution reported on their line 10, included in income when the transfer's testing period was first breached in a month of THIS tax year, PLUS any attested 2024 transfer whose testing period was first breached in a 2025 month. $0 where neither leg applies.
WHAT DECIDES IT IS THE TESTING-PERIOD MONTH, NOT THE COVERAGE ANSWER. Charging the whole line 10 plus 10% whenever ../wasEligibleToMakeHsaContributionsAllYear is answered false - which is ../hsaHdhpCoverageStatus == partOfYear plus the other-coverage tests - would be UNSOUND, and unsound in the taxpayer-adverse direction. IRC 408(d)(9)(D)(iii) starts the testing period AT THE MONTH OF THE TRANSFER, so ineligible months BEFORE the transfer are outside the window entirely - a filer whose coverage begins in March, who transfers in April and stays covered through December is partOfYear and has breached nothing. And IRC 408(d)(9)(D)(i)(I) puts the inclusion in the taxable year containing the FIRST ineligible month of the testing period, so a December-2025 transfer that breaks in June 2026 is a 2026 return's line 19 and $0 here. Neither case is exotic: an HSA needs HDHP coverage, so "coverage starts mid-year, transfer follows" is the ordinary shape of a partOfYear filer with a line 10.
SO THE PRESENT-YEAR LEG READS ONE THING: ../hsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonthIsThisTaxYear, which is the year test applied to ../writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth, the intake. Answer "none" and this is $0. Name a 2026 month and this is $0. Name a 2025 month and the whole line 10 is included, whatever the coverage answer says - THE WRITABLE WINS ON CONTRADICTION, on /writableHsaEitherSpouseHadFamilyCoverage's precedent, because the statute keys on the testing-period month and the writable is the only place that month is stated.
$0, AND COMPLETE, WHERE THE INTAKE IS UNANSWERED - but not silently. The year test resolves a complete false on an unanswered intake rather than an Incomplete that would take incompleteness through Schedule 1 line 9 and Schedule 2 line 21 into /totalTax; the missing answer is reported to the filer instead by ../hasUnmodeledHsaFundingDistribution, which refuses on exactly Not(eligible all year) AND line 10 > $0 AND this question unanswered. That is the "refuse only when the input is missing" posture rather than a guess.
LINE 18 COMPUTES SEPARATELY: the last-month-rule half of Part III is the ATTESTED ../writableHsaLastMonthRuleExcessContributions on ../hsaLine18LastMonthRuleIncome, and /flowKnockoutHsaTestingPeriodAdditionalIncomeYes refuses only the yes-answered filer whose intake group is unanswered. This fact is the line 19 leg alone; ../form8889Line20TestingPeriodIncome adds the two.
THE DEATH-OR-DISABILITY CARVE-OUT IS APPLIED. IRC 408(d)(9)(D)(ii) disapplies the income inclusion AND the 10% additional tax where the individual ceased to be an eligible individual by reason of death, or of becoming disabled within the meaning of section 72(m)(7); the first Switch case reads ../hsaTestingPeriodExceptionAttested. UNANSWERED, the exception is simply not claimed and this fact charges in full: an affirmative claim, not a completeness refusal.
A PRIOR-YEAR TRANSFER whose testing period fails in THIS year is ALSO ON THIS LINE, as the SECOND leg: ../writableHsaPriorYearFundingDistributionFailedAmount, WHERE ../writableHsaPriorYearFundingDistributionFailedThisYear is answered yes AND the amount is answered. THE TWO LEGS ARE INDEPENDENT AND ADDITIVE, not a Switch choosing one - a filer could in principle answer yes on both the present-year question (a 2025 transfer that itself breaks before year end) and the prior-year question (a 2024 transfer whose window breaks in 2025), and Form 8889 line 19 is one total either way ("the total of any qualified HSA funding distribution", i8889 lines 515-517). Unanswered or no on the prior-year gate, the second leg is $0. THE WRITABLE WINS ON CONTRADICTION here too, on ../writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth's own precedent: this second leg computes even for a filer whose ../hasMadeQualifiedHsaFundingDistributionDerived is Incomplete (the prior-year-only filer who never reached the present-year yes/no at all), because it reads the prior-year writables directly rather than through that chain. UNANSWERED SAFETY: the gate is complete-safe by construction (IsComplete-gated in the Then below), so an unanswered prior-year gate never widens an Incomplete into this fact; an ANSWERED yes with the amount unanswered does not fall through to a guessed $0 either - it is caught upstream by ../hasUnmodeledHsaFundingDistribution's FIRST Case, which blocks submission before this fact's own $0 default would otherwise be reached. ONE ANSWER PER FILER, NOT PER TRANSFER, on the same taxpayer-adverse approximation as the present-year leg - stated on the prior-year writable's own Description, not repeated here.
ONE PART III PER SPOUSE, per the form's own header sentence, and the two are summed into ONE Schedule 1 line 8f entry and ONE Schedule 2 line 17d entry by /hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncomeAndAdditionalTax and /hsaTestingPeriodFailureAdditionalTax.
THE QUANTIFIER THE RETURN-LEVEL INTAKES CANNOT REACH: /someFilersHaveTestingPeriodAdditionalIncome and /someFilersMadeTestingPeriodContribution are return-level Booleans, so they cannot say WHICH spouse failed. This fact does not read them; it is per filer from the start, off that filer's own line 10 and their own testing-period answer, which is what the per-spouse Part III requires - and it is why the testing-period intake is per filer too rather than one more return-level question.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 21 - this filer's own 10% additional tax on their own Part III
Fact.Description:
This filer's Form 8889 line 21, "Multiply line 20 by 10% (0.10)", rounded on THEIR OWN FORM. The multiplicand is ../form8889Line20TestingPeriodIncome - the printed line 20, "Add lines 18 and 19". Line 18 computes from the attested last-month-rule intake, so multiplying the line 19 leg alone would drop the 223(b)(8)(B)(i)(II) 10% on the line 18 half. The pinned fixture hsa-testing-period-line18-plus-line19-sum-taxed is the discriminator: line 18 = 2,000 and line 19 = 3,000 give $500 here, where a line-19-only multiplicand gives $300. Both legs share the death-or-disability zeroing upstream (each leg is $0 when ../hsaTestingPeriodExceptionAttested), so no separate exception term is needed here.
WHY THE ROUNDING IS PER SPOUSE RATHER THAN ONCE ON THE COUPLE'S TOTAL. The Part III header sentence says that on a joint return where both spouses have separate HSAs, a SEPARATE Part III is completed for each spouse, and line 21 is a line ON that form: each spouse's 10% is computed and printed on their own Form 8889, and line 17d of the one Schedule 2 is "the total" of the two printed figures. The 1040 instructions' rounding rule is stated of amounts entered on "your return and schedules" and requires that if you round at all you "must round all amounts", which is what makes each printed line 21 a whole dollar before the two are added. Rounding once on the couple's summed line 20 is a different number: two spouses at line 20 = $55.00 each give $5.50 and $5.50, which print as $6 and $6 for a total of $12, where 10% of the summed $110.00 is $11.00. The pinned fixture hsa-testing-period-line21-per-spouse-rounding-differs is exactly that case. This is the one place in this leg where the repo's usual round-at-the-printed-destination convention does NOT collapse to a single Round, because there are TWO printed destinations feeding one total.
THE i8889 INSTRUCTIONS SAY NOTHING ABOUT ROUNDING - checked, and recorded here because the absence is the reason the general 1040 rule governs. The authority for the per-form placement is the form's own per-spouse header plus the general rule, not a Form 8889 sentence.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: its only input is complete-safe $0.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 Part III line 20 for this filer, "Add lines 18 and 19"
Fact.Description:
This filer's printed Form 8889 Part III line 20: Add(../hsaLine18LastMonthRuleIncome, ../hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome). PER FILER BECAUSE PART III IS PER FILER - the Part III header says "If you are filing jointly and both you and your spouse each have separate HSAs, complete a separate Part III for each spouse" - and the return level /hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncomeAndAdditionalTax sums this leaf across /filers for the single Schedule 1 line 8f entry the joint return files.
IT IS LINE 18'S CONSUMER: line 18 computes from the attested ../writableHsaLastMonthRuleExcessContributions, and this Add carries it beside line 19 to the return-level sum. COMPLETE SAFE: both addends resolve a complete $0 on a filer who never answered the testing period questions, so this Add resolves for every filer and the return level CollectionSum stays complete.
CENTS ARE KEPT, like the sum above it: the printed rounding happens once, on income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 20 - testing-period failure income (Schedule 1 line 8f leg)
Fact.Description:
Both filers' Form 8889 Part III line 20, summed for Schedule 1 (Form 1040) Part I line 8f ("Income from Form 8889"). Line 20 is "Add lines 18 and 19": line 18 is /filers/*/hsaLine18LastMonthRuleIncome (the attested last-month-rule inclusion) and line 19 is /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome, so this sum is the two spouses' separate Part IIIs added into the one printed entry the joint return files. It sums /filers/*/form8889Line20TestingPeriodIncome, which is that filer's Add(line 18, line 19).
CENTS ARE KEPT HERE AND ROUNDED AT THE DESTINATION. There is no Round on this sum: the printed rounding happens once, on income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome, which already wraps its Add in a Round. A 2,500.50 line 19 therefore arrives here as 2,500.50 and lands on the Schedule 1 total as 2,501 (HALF-UP), which is the same shape the excess-contribution earnings leg uses.
THE OUTER IsComplete(/filers) GUARD is the /hsaCollectionRouteAdditionalTax20PctTotal pattern, for its measured reason: a CollectionSum over a never-answered collection resolves Placeholder, and this fact is an addend of a printed total.
THE 10% TAX IS A SEPARATE PAIR OF FACTS - /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureAdditionalTax per spouse and /hsaTestingPeriodFailureAdditionalTax for their total - because it lands on a different schedule AND because it rounds on each spouse's own form, which is why it is not simply 10% of this sum. The name of this fact carries both halves because it is the path its records contract declared.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 21 - the 10% additional tax on testing-period failure income (Schedule 2 line 17d leg)
Fact.Description:
Both filers' Form 8889 Part III line 21, "Multiply line 20 by 10% (0.10)", summed for Schedule 2 (Form 1040) Part II line 17d ("Additional tax on an HSA because you didn't remain an eligible individual"), which reaches line 18 and then line 21 and Form 1040 line 23. A SEPARATE PRINTED LINE from 17c, which carries the 20% tax on unqualified distributions through /hsaCollectionRouteAdditionalTax20PctTotal: routing this leg to 17c would double-book that line.
THE ROUNDING HAPPENS PER SPOUSE AND THIS FACT ONLY ADDS. Each spouse's Form 8889 line 21 is a line on THEIR OWN form, so /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureAdditionalTax takes 10% of that spouse's unrounded line 20 and rounds it HALF-UP there; Schedule 2 line 17d is "the total" of the printed figures, and this fact is that total. Summing both spouses' unrounded line 20s and rounding once would give a DIFFERENT NUMBER whenever both spouses fail and both halves carry cents: $55.00 each gives $6 + $6 = $12 printed, against $11.00 for one Round of the $110.00 sum. The fixture hsa-testing-period-line21-per-spouse-rounding-differs pins that difference; the single-filer cents boundary (10% of 2,500.50 is 250.05, which rounds to 250) cannot distinguish the two placements.
THE MULTIPLICAND IS THE UNROUNDED LINE 20, not the rounded Schedule 1 figure: the printed instruction multiplies line 20, and Schedule 1's rounding is a different form's.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: every addend is complete-safe $0, so this is $0 and Complete on every return that answers nothing. THE OUTER IsComplete(/filers) GUARD is the /hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncomeAndAdditionalTax pattern for its measured reason - a CollectionSum over a never-answered collection resolves Placeholder, and this fact is an addend of a printed total.
THE DEATH-OR-DISABILITY CARVE-OUT that this tax shares with its income legs is APPLIED UPSTREAM: each leg is $0 where the filer attested the 223(b)(8)(B)(ii) / 408(d)(9)(D)(ii) ground on /filers/*/writableHsaTestingPeriodExceptionReason, so the 10% follows the zeroed line 20 down with no term here; the reading is on /filers/*/hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncome and the options fact, and is not repeated here.

Fact.Name: Monthly HDHP coverage type (Form 8889 Line 3 Limitation Chart)
Fact.Description: The three answers the Line 3 Limitation Chart can produce for a single month: `none` when the chart routes the month to its enter-zero line, `selfOnly` and `family` for the two coverage types the chart's last question distinguishes. `none` is WIDE on purpose: it is the chart's enter-zero answer, so it covers every IRC 223(c)(1) reason the filer was not an eligible individual on the first day of that month, both the (A)(i) no-HDHP prong and the (A)(ii) disqualifying-other-coverage prong. It is NOT the Medicare arm, which IRC 223(b)(7) states separately and which this dictionary carries on its own vector.

Whether IRC 223(b)(7) zeroes the filer's monthly limitation for January. January is the base of the recursion: there is no earlier month for the statute to carry forward from.

Whether IRC 223(b)(7) zeroes the filer's monthly limitation for February. The Any over the PRECEDING month is the statute's "and for each month thereafter": once January is true it stays true through December, so a filer who answers only their onset month leaves every later month unanswered and still gets the right answer.

Fact.Name: IRC 223(b)(5)(A) collapses both spouses onto family coverage for January
Fact.Description: Whether January is a month in which either spouse held family HDHP coverage on the first day, so that both spouses are treated as having only that family coverage for the month. The test is IRC 223(b)(5)(A)'s own condition, "individuals who are married to each other", and not the narrower MFJ filing choice: the marital conjunct reads /hsaMarriedOnFirstDayMonth01, with the year-end filers:/isMarried as its complete-safe fallback. The caution that the married rules apply only if BOTH spouses are eligible individuals is satisfied structurally rather than by a conjunct: a spouse whose month type is `family` is by construction an eligible individual for that month, and the reading filer's own eligibility is tested by the first arm of ../hsaLine3EffectiveCoverageTypeMonth01. ON AN MFS RETURN the spouse's monthly vector comes from the return-level intake /writableHsaMfsSpouseCoverageTypeMonth01..12, the third leg of this fact's Any, so the collapse fires from the spouse's side on a separate return once those rows are answered; /flowKnockoutMFSLine6Check refuses only until they are.

Fact.Name: Family coverage in at least one month, after the married collapse
Fact.Description: Whether any of the twelve post-collapse months is `family`. This is the "had family coverage at any time during the year" test the Line 3 Note uses to divert the age-55 additional contribution amount to line 7 for a married filer.

Fact.Name: Treated as having family coverage for each month
Fact.Description: Whether all twelve post-collapse months are `family`. This is the condition on the FIRST bullet of the Form 8889 Line 6 instruction, It is the CHART's question and is not the shipping branch decision (../hsaLine6TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth is); the four-step refigure the second bullet prescribes for a couple treated as having family coverage in only some months ships at /filers/*/hsaLine6NonUniformFamilyMonthsAmount.

Fact.Name: The $1,000 age-55 additional amount rides on line 3 rather than line 7
Fact.Description: Whether the IRC 223(b)(3) additional contribution amount is included in each of this filer's chart amounts. The chart includes it for every eligible month of a filer who is 55 or older at the end of 2025, and the Line 3 Note removes it again for a filer who is married AND had family coverage at any time during the year, because that filer figures it on line 7 instead. This reproduces, on the monthly vector, the reading the module already carries on ../hsaProrationAnnualLimit (see that fact's Description for the rule-6 "for the entire year" tension and why the chart's own text governs); that reading is carried here unchanged rather than re-argued. DIVERGENCE, named: an unanswered date of birth leaves age unknown, and this fact then resolves a complete FALSE, which is the taxpayer-adverse direction and is the same posture ../hsaProrationAnnualLimit takes.

Fact.Name: The chart's self-only-coverage amount for one month

The chart enters the FULL annual amount on each eligible month line and divides the twelve-month total by 12 at the end, so this is an annual figure appearing on a monthly row, not a twelfth of one.

Fact.Name: Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet, Total for all months
Fact.Description: The sum of the twelve month lines. Publication 969's printed examples put $8,550 and $60,100 on this row.

Fact.Name: Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet, Limitation (divide the total by 12)
Fact.Description: The worksheet's last line: the twelve-month total divided by 12. CENTS ARE KEPT AND MUST BE. The worksheet prints no rounding instruction and Publication 969's two examples publish $712.50 and $5,008.33, so no Round wraps this Divide; the engine's Dollar is a scale-2 BigDecimal, which is exactly the precision the printed figures carry. This is NOT Form 8889 line 3 by itself — rule 4 makes line 3 the GREATER of this figure and the last-month-rule amount, which is ../hsaLine3ContributionLimitation.

Fact.Name: Eligible on December 1, so IRC 223(b)(8)(A) treats the filer as eligible all year
Fact.Description: Whether the filer was an eligible individual on the first day of the last month of the tax year and was not enrolled in Medicare for that month. Derived from December's own vector row rather than attested: it is the same predicate the older attestation ../writableHsaLastMonthRuleEligible asks for, now decidable from the monthly intake. THE MEDICARE CONJUNCT IS NOT REDUNDANT AND IS NOT WIDER THAN IT LOOKS: ../hsaMedicareLimitationZeroMonth12 latches over the preceding month, so a December that is not a Medicare month implies no Medicare month anywhere in the year, which is why the twelve-month treatment this rule grants never has to be reconciled with an earlier zeroed month.

Fact.Name: The limitation IRC 223(b)(8)(A) produces, i.e. December's coverage type for all twelve months
Fact.Description: Under the last-month rule the filer is treated as an eligible individual in every month, with the same HDHP coverage they had on the first day of December. Every one of the twelve chart rows would then carry December's amount, so the total is twelve times it and the divide-by-12 returns December's amount unchanged — which is why this fact reads ../hsaLine3ChartAmountMonth12 directly instead of rebuilding the table. $0 when the rule does not apply, where it is inert as the floor of the GreaterOf below.

Fact.Name: IRC 223(b)(6) zeroes the vector route's Form 8889 line 3
Fact.Description: Whether this filer can be claimed as another taxpayer's dependent, which zeroes the vector route's contribution limitation the way the legacy chain's own ../wasEligibleToMakeHsaContributionsAllYear already zeroes ../hsaBaseContributionLimit via its `Not(filers:/filers/*/canBeClaimed)` conjunct — the twelve-month vector chart reads no dependent status at all, so a claimable dependent whose vector governs took the FULL limitation instead of $0. NOT the identical unanswered posture: the legacy conjunct is a BARE `Not(canBeClaimed)`, which leaves an unanswered `canBeClaimed` Incomplete and propagates that Incompleteness rather than defaulting a direction; this fact is instead complete-safe FALSE on an unanswered filers:/filers/*/canBeClaimed (unanswered is treated as not claimable), matching ../hsaDeductionDeniedAsDependent's shape so an unanswered return still completes. filers:/filers/*/canBeClaimed is required intake on every return this dictionary builds, so the two postures never actually diverge on a completing return.

Fact.Name: IRC 223(c)(1)(A)(ii) zeroes the vector route's Form 8889 line 3 for whole-year disqualifying other coverage
Fact.Description: Whether this filer answered disqualifying other coverage for the WHOLE year (../hadOtherCoverageIneligibleForHsaDerived equal to `wholeYear`), which makes the filer not an eligible individual in ANY month under IRC 223(c)(1)(A)(ii) and zeroes the vector route's contribution limitation, matching IRC 223(b)(1), which gives the whole-year disqualified $0. Deliberately reads ../hadOtherCoverageIneligibleForHsaDerived directly (a `../`-relative dependency, bound to THIS filer) rather than the existing /filers/*/causesOtherCoverageWholeYearKnockOut (an absolute-wildcard dependency that broadcasts over every filer in the return) — the wildcard form throws a resolution-time vector-length mismatch when read from inside a per-filer Switch `When` next to a plain per-filer boolean, the same MaybeVector.vectorize2 trap formW2s/schedule3's own broadcast-vs-per-filer commentary documents; this fact avoids it by staying strictly per-filer throughout. Complete-safe FALSE on an unanswered ../hadOtherCoverageIneligibleForHsaDerived, matching ../hsaLine3DependentZeroesLimitation's shape (unanswered is treated as not whole-year-disqualified).

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 3 — the IRC 223(b) contribution limitation
Fact.Description: FORM 8889 LINE 3, per the Line 3 narrative rule 4: the GREATER of the Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet's last line and the maximum based on the coverage held on the first day of the last month of the tax year, unless ../hsaLine3DependentZeroesLimitation applies (IRC 223(b)(6)) or ../hsaLine3OtherCoverageWholeYearZeroesLimitation applies (IRC 223(c)(1)(A)(ii)) — a `../`-relative per-filer twin of /filers/*/causesOtherCoverageWholeYearKnockOut, read here instead of that fact because the absolute-wildcard form crashes when read from inside this per-filer Switch — either of which zeroes it outright before either operand is read. The greater-of is not an optimisation; the instructions print it, and the TIP beside it says a filer with family coverage on December 1 need not use the worksheet at all and simply enters $8,550. Both of Publication 969's worked examples land here: each contributes $8,550 for 2025 even though their worksheet lines read $712.50 and $5,008.33, because the last-month rule wins the greater-of. This per-filer fact is Form 8889 line 3, which is per spouse; /hsaLine3MonthlyContributionLimitation is return-level. ../hsaInitialContributionLimit's vector Case reads this fact directly.

Fact.Name: The filer's line 3 depends on the last-month rule
Fact.Description: Whether the last-month-rule amount strictly exceeds the worksheet limitation, i.e. whether any part of this filer's line 3 exists only because of IRC 223(b)(8)(A). That is precisely the predicate 223(b)(8)(B) opens a testing period on, and the difference between the two operands is what Form 8889 line 18 recaptures. EXPOSED, NOT WIRED, and the linkage is stated honestly: the testing-period facts in this module today (/filers/*/writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth and its neighbours) implement the IRC 408(d)(9) FUNDING-DISTRIBUTION testing period and consume no last-month-rule fact at all; the only last-month-rule input the module has ever had is the attestation ../writableHsaLastMonthRuleEligible, read by ../hsaProratedContributionLimit alone. Line 18 remains unbuilt for the reason its own record gives — it needs the PRIOR year's contribution amount and the PRIOR year's redetermined limitation, neither of which has an intake. This fact and ../hsaLine3WorksheetLimitation are the two operands that record asks for, supplied for the current year, with no body of any existing fact changed.

Fact.Name: IRC 223(b)(5)(B)'s equal division is the branch this filer takes
Fact.Description: Whether the couple is treated as having family coverage for EVERY month, which is the condition on the first bullet of the Form 8889 Line 6 instruction It is the Line 3 chart's gate rather than the shipping branch decision, which is ../hsaLine6EqualDivisionApplies.

Fact.Name: IRC 223(b)(5)(B) — this spouse's half of the shared family limitation
Fact.Description:
Half of this filer's line 3 where the equal division applies, otherwise line 3 unchanged. WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. IRC 223(b)(5)(B) divides the paragraph (1) LIMITATION equally between the spouses — and Form 8889 applies that division at LINE 6, to line 5, which is line 3 reduced by the Archer MSA contributions on line 4. Line 3 itself is never divided: rule 1 puts the FULL family amount on both spouses' line 3.
THE ARCHER REDUCTION IS APPLIED AT THE CONSUMER, NOT HERE. This fact is the statute's division computed on line 3 alone, and it equals line 6 only where line 4 is zero. Repointing its Dividend at line 5 would move seven committed node tests that assert this fact directly as the vector's line 3 half, and on a return where the vector does NOT govern (every MFS return) line 5 is the LEGACY line 3, a different number. So ../hsaContributionLimitLessAddition's vector-equal-division arm reads ../hsaLine6EqualDivisionHalfShare, which is half of LINE 5 and follows the printed Line 6 instruction literally, "divide the amount on line 5 equally between you and your spouse"; the legacy sibling /hsaPrimaryFilerAllocatedContributionLimit reads line 5 too, so the two Form 8889 line 6 arms agree on the Archer reduction.
THIS FACT HAS NO CONSUMER AND CARRIES <Export downstreamFacts="true" />, exactly as its sibling ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleIncreasedLimitation does for the same reason ("EXPOSED, NOT WIRED"): scripts/lints/lint_wiring.py reds on a derived fact that nothing consumes and nothing exports, and a skip-list row would hide a fact that is genuinely meant to be readable.
TWO FURTHER POINTS, NAMED: (b) "unless they agree on a different division" — the statute and the Line 6 instruction both allow any allocation the spouses agree on, and this dictionary has no writable for it, so the equal split is imposed rather than offered; (c) the four-step refigure the second bullet of the Line 6 instruction prescribes when the couple is treated as having family coverage in only SOME months is computed by the Line 6 facts (../hsaLine6Step1MonthSetChartTotal and its siblings), not by this fact. NOTE the additional contribution amount is NOT divided: 223(b)(5)(B) says the limitation is divided "without regard to any additional contribution amount under paragraph (3)", which is why Publication 969 caps a 55-or-older couple at $10,550 — $4,275 each plus $1,000 each.

Fact.Name: Every month of the Medicare vector carries the answer the chart needs
Fact.Description: Whether the twelve per-month Medicare rows of the Line 3 Limitation Chart carry an answer for this filer. TRUE WITHOUT TWELVE ANSWERS IN EXACTLY ONE CASE: a filer whose year-level ../enrolledInMedicareDerived is `noneOfYear` has already answered the chart's Medicare question "No" for every month, so demanding twelve repetitions of it would refuse a return over an answer the filer has given. In every other case — Medicare for part of the year, Medicare for the whole year, or no year-level answer at all — all twelve rows are required, because ../hsaMedicareLimitationZeroMonthNN reads an unanswered row as "not a Medicare month" and a limitation computed off that default would be too LARGE. This fact is the taxpayer-adverse direction fenced, not a convenience.

Fact.Name: The monthly coverage vector, not the legacy count and type, supplies Form 8889 line 3
Fact.Description:
Whether every filer on this return has supplied the twelve-month coverage vector (and, where it is owed, the twelve-month Medicare vector), so that Form 8889 line 3 may be read off ../hsaLine3ContributionLimitation rather than off the legacy ../writableHsaMonthsOfCoverage + ../typeOfHdhp shortcut.
WHY IT IS RETURN-LEVEL AND WHY A MARRIED RETURN NEEDS BOTH SPOUSES. IRC 223(b)(5)(A) collapses BOTH spouses onto family coverage for any month in which EITHER of them held family coverage, so a filer's own line 3 depends on the other spouse's months. If one spouse's vector were allowed to govern while the other's was missing, the missing spouse's twelve rows would read `none` by default and the collapse could not fire from their side: one spouse would take the undivided family limit while the other took the legacy chain, and the couple's two line 3s could exceed the single shared limitation. So the vector governs a married return only when BOTH vectors are answered — including the spouse who holds no HSA, whose COVERAGE is what 223(b)(5)(A) reads.
FALSE IS THE COMPLETE-SAFE ANSWER, not a refusal: an unanswered vector leaves the filer on the legacy chain. the application may prefill the vector from the legacy count and type; that prefill is what makes this gate true for the unchanged-all-year majority.

Fact.Name: Treated as having family coverage in SOME months but not every month
Fact.Description: Whether this filer is one of a married couple who, after the IRC 223(b)(5)(A) collapse, held family coverage in at least one month but not in every month. That is exactly the population the SECOND bullet of the Form 8889 Line 6 instruction sends through a four-step refigure — refigure line 5 using only the family months, divide THAT equally, subtract the spouse's share, add back any other limits — and that refigure ships at /filers/*/hsaLine6NonUniformFamilyMonthsAmount.

Fact.Name: Every month treated as eligible with family coverage, under the Line 3 rule 2 deeming (Line 7 worksheet)
Fact.Description:
Whether the Line 3 narrative rule 2 deeming makes EVERY month satisfy the Line 7 worksheet's two items, so the twelve per-month facts below (../hsaLine7EligibleMonth01 through 12) each read this as their second disjunct. Rule 2 reads: where the last-month rule applies, "you are treated as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year" — so a filer whose December was a family month is treated as having family coverage, and as being an eligible individual, in EVERY month, however few months they actually held it. That is item (1) of the Line 7 instruction, answered the same way for all twelve months at once; item (2), not enrolled in Medicare for the month, is guaranteed for every month whenever ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleApplies is true, because that fact already requires December to be a non-Medicare month and Medicare enrollment latches forward from the month it starts (../hsaMedicareLimitationZeroMonth12's own predicate), so no earlier month can be a Medicare month either.
WHY A SEPARATE FACT AND NOT A WIDENING OF ../hsaLine3EffectiveCoverageTypeMonthNN. The Line 3 Limitation Chart itself must NOT apply rule 2's deeming to its per-month rows: rule 4 makes line 3 the GREATER of the worksheet limitation (computed from the months actually held) and the last-month-rule amount, so the two readings of the same twelve months have to stay distinct facts. This is the same separation ../hsaLine6TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth already keeps from ../hsaLine3TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth, for the identical reason, applied here to the Line 7 worksheet's per-month test instead of Line 6's whole-year test.
NOT THE (C)(i) SUBSTITUTED CHAIN. ../hsaHfdCapCatchUpAmount's own deemed-year arm (../hsaHfdCapDeemedYearGoverns) is a SEPARATE fact on the IRC 408(d)(9)(C)(i) qualified-HSA- funding-distribution basis, keyed on the TRANSFER month's coverage type rather than December's literal one; this fact changes nothing on that chain and reads only real-basis facts.
THE DIVERGENCE THIS EXTENDS, NAMED AS ../hsaLine6TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth ALREADY NAMES IT FOR LINE 6. IRC 223(b)(8)(A)(ii) deems December's plan only "during each of the months such individual is treated as an eligible individual SOLELY BY REASON OF clause (i)" - i.e. only for months the filer was not ALREADY, independently, an eligible individual - while the printed rule 2 deems it "for the entire year" with no such carve-out. A filer who was eligible on their own in every month, with SELF-ONLY coverage in some of them and FAMILY coverage in December, is inside the FORM'S sentence and outside the STATUTE'S: clause (ii) would leave their self-only months self-only (they needed no deeming to be eligible for those months), while rule 2 deems every month family regardless. THIS FACT FOLLOWS THE FORM, for the same reason and with the same consequence ../hsaLine6TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth already documents: a filer eligible all year on their own, with December family coverage among a mixed year, is DEEMED family every month for the Line 7 worksheet, not just for the months that needed the deeming. With twelve literal eligible months and six literal family months including December, ../hsaLine7EligibleMonth01 through 12 all resolve true and the worksheet prints $1,000.00, not the $500.00 a "solely by reason of" reading would give.

Fact.Name: Additional Contribution Amount Worksheet, January counts as a month eligible
Fact.Description:
Whether January is one of the "months eligible" the Additional Contribution Amount Worksheet counts. The Line 7 instruction states the two items in full and this fact is both of them: item (1) "You or your spouse had family coverage under an HDHP and were, or were considered to be, an eligible individual on the first day of the month" is ../hsaLine3EffectiveCoverageTypeMonth01 being `family` — that fact is `none` whenever the filer was not an eligible individual on the first day, and it is `family` whenever EITHER spouse held family coverage, which is the IRC 223(b)(5)(A) collapse and is exactly what "you or your spouse" means; item (2) "You were not enrolled in Medicare for the month" is Not(../hsaMedicareLimitationZeroMonth01). NOTE THE TWO ITEMS ARE NOT THE SAME TEST AS THE LINE 3 CHART'S TWO QUESTIONS even though they read the same facts: the chart pays a self-only month, this worksheet does not, because line 7 exists only for the married family-coverage case that line 3 excludes.
ALSO TRUE where the last-month rule governs (../hsaLine7DeemedEligibleEveryMonth): Line 3 narrative rule 2 deems a filer whose last-month rule applies as having December's HDHP coverage for the entire year, so a December family month makes every month a family month for THIS per-month test too - the same deeming ../hsaLine6TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth already applies to the Line 6 first bullet. Item (2)'s Medicare test needs no separate re-test here: ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleApplies already requires December to be a non-Medicare month, and Medicare enrollment latches forward from the month it starts, so a December that clears item (2) means every earlier month does too.

Item (2)'s Medicare test needs no separate re-test here: ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleApplies already requires December to be a non-Medicare month, and Medicare enrollment latches forward from the month it starts, so a December that clears item (2) means every earlier month does too.

Fact.Name: Additional Contribution Amount Worksheet, December counts as a month eligible
Fact.Description:
Whether December is one of the "months eligible" the Additional Contribution Amount Worksheet counts. The Line 7 instruction states the two items in full and this fact is both of them: item (1) "You or your spouse had family coverage under an HDHP and were, or were considered to be, an eligible individual on the first day of the month" is ../hsaLine3EffectiveCoverageTypeMonth12 being `family` — that fact is `none` whenever the filer was not an eligible individual on the first day, and it is `family` whenever EITHER spouse held family coverage, which is the IRC 223(b)(5)(A) collapse and is exactly what "you or your spouse" means; item (2) "You were not enrolled in Medicare for the month" is Not(../hsaMedicareLimitationZeroMonth12). Fact.Name: Additional Contribution Amount Worksheet, line 1 ($1,000 x number of months eligible)
Fact.Description: The worksheet's first line, "$1,000 × number of months eligible", expressed as the sum of the additional contribution amount over the eligible months rather than as a multiplication — the same shape the Line 3 Limitation Chart's own total already uses in this module, and arithmetically the same product. The $1,000 is the ledgered constants:/hsaOver55AdditionalCoverageLimit (authority/ty2025/parameters.tsv row 149, hsa-catchup-contribution-55plus), not a literal.

Fact.Name: Additional Contribution Amount Worksheet, line 2 (divide line 1 by 12) — Form 8889 line 7
Fact.Description:
The worksheet's second line, "Divide line 1 by 12. Enter here and on line 7". CENTS ARE KEPT AND THAT IS A READ RATHER THAN A CHOICE: the worksheet prints no rounding instruction, exactly as the Line 3 Limitation Chart's own divide-by-12 prints none, and this module already keeps the cents of that one because Publication 969 publishes $712.50 and $5,008.33 on it. The optional whole-dollar convention of the Form 1040 instructions is applied once, downstream, by the Round on ../hsaTotalContributionLimit (line 8), which is where this module has always elected it.
THE PRINTED FIGURE THIS REPRODUCES is the Line 7 TIP: "If items (1) and (2) apply to all months during 2025, enter $1,000 on line 7" — twelve eligible months give $1,000 × 12 / 12 = $1,000.00. Every partial-month figure is arithmetic from the same two printed lines and is published nowhere.

Fact.Name: Monthly Archer HDHP coverage type (Form 8853 Line 3 Limitation Chart)
Fact.Description:
The three answers the Form 8853 Line 3 Limitation Chart can produce for a single month of 2025: `none` when the chart routes the month to its enter-zero line, `selfOnly` and `family` for the two coverage types the chart's last question distinguishes.
`none` IS WIDE, exactly as the Form 8889 sibling /hsaMonthlyCoverageTypeOptions is wide, and for the same printed reason: the chart has THREE ways to reach its enter-zero line — enrolled in Medicare for the month, not an eligible individual on the first day of the month, or no HDHP at all — and prints one answer for all three. This enum is that one answer.
WHY IT IS A SEPARATE OPTIONS PATH FROM THE HSA ONE and not a reuse. The two charts are keyed on DIFFERENT PLANS: Form 8889's on the HSA's HDHP, Form 8853's on the Archer MSA's HDHP, whose printed deductible bands do not even overlap the HSA's ("Minimum annual deductible $2,850 / $5,700", "Maximum annual deductible $4,300 / $8,550"; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8853.pdf, page 2). A filer can hold both vehicles in the same month with different coverage types. Sharing one options path would also mean that a later change widening the HSA enum — its own Description contemplates a fourth option — would silently widen this one.

Fact.Name: Writable: Archer HDHP coverage type on the first day of January (Form 8853 line 3 chart)
Fact.Description:
January: the coverage type this filer's ARCHER MSA high deductible health plan provided on the FIRST DAY of the month, as the Form 8853 Line 3 Limitation Chart asks it, after the chart's two earlier questions have been applied — a month in which the filer was enrolled in Medicare, or was not an eligible individual on the first day, is `none`.
Optional and complete-safe: unanswered is read as the chart's enter-zero line by ../archerMsaChartAmountMonth01, which is the taxpayer-ADVERSE direction (a smaller line 3, so a smaller deduction and, on a return with contributions, an excess that refuses the filing).
The chart's own Tip is the warrant for prefilling the unchanged-all-year majority: "If eligibility and coverage for both you and your spouse didn't change from one month to the next, enter the same number you entered for the previous month."

Fact.Name: Writable: the annual deductible of this filer's SELF-ONLY Archer HDHP
Fact.Description:
The annual deductible of the high deductible health plan behind this filer's Archer MSA, for the months the Line 3 Limitation Chart answers `selfOnly`. The chart takes 65% of it.
THE PRINTED BAND IS CARRIED AS PARAMETER-LEDGER ROWS AND LIMITS. The chart prints "Enter annual deductible" / "(must be at least $2,850 but" / "not more than $4,300)." Those two indexed figures carry ledger rows in authority/ty2025/parameters.tsv (archer-hdhp-self-only-annual-deductible-min and -max), and this writable carries the matching Min and Max Limits; scripts/lint_param_ledger.py checks them. ONE HONEST QUALIFICATION: Limit-element enforcement is a GATE_JVM step rather than a resolution-time behaviour, so NO node-test witnesses the band — the dictionary STATES the bound, and the application's screen validation stays the layer that actually stops a filer typing an out-of-band number.
NAMED GAP — ONE DEDUCTIBLE PER COVERAGE TYPE, NOT ONE PER MONTH. The chart's dollar cell sits inside the per-month loop, so a plan whose deductible changed mid-year is not expressible. One answer per coverage type covers the plan-year-stable case, which is every case the closed Archer population can still present without a mid-year plan change.

Fact.Name: Writable: the annual deductible of this filer's FAMILY Archer HDHP
Fact.Description:
The annual deductible of the high deductible health plan behind this filer's Archer MSA, for the months the Line 3 Limitation Chart answers `family`. The chart takes 75% of it — or 37.5% on a married-filing-separately return.
THE SAME BAND TREATMENT the self-only sibling carries applies here with the family band ("must be at least $5,700 but" / "not more than $8,550"): ledger rows archer-hdhp-family-annual-deductible-min and -max and the matching Min/Max Limits, with the sibling's qualification about Limit-element enforcement being a GATE_JVM step. The one-deductible-per-coverage-type gap STANDS here too: one answer per coverage type rather than one per month.
NAMED GAP — THE MFS DIVISION ELECTION IS NOT OFFERED. The chart's family cell says "If married filing" / "separately, see Married filing" / "separately.", and that instruction offers a CHOICE: "enter only 37.5% (0.375) (one-half of 75%) of the annual deductible for each month on the worksheet; or, if you and your spouse agree to divide the 75% of the annual deductible in a different manner, enter your share." This dictionary takes the first branch unconditionally. The election needs a per-spouse share both returns agree on, which no single return can validate, and it is the taxpayer-ADVERSE half only for the spouse who would have taken more than half.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 line 4 — compensation from the employer maintaining the HDHP
Fact.Description:
Form 8853 LINE 4: "Compensation (see instructions) from the employer maintaining the high deductible health plan. (If self-employed, enter your earned income from the trade or business under which the high deductible health plan was established.)"
WHY IT IS ASKED RATHER THAN DERIVED FROM THE W-2s, which is the first thing a reader will challenge. The printed definition is not "box 1 of every W-2": it is compensation "from the employer maintaining the high deductible health plan" — one employer out of possibly several — and it "also includes net earnings from self-employment, but only for a trade or business in which your personal services are a material income-producing factor", net of expenses and of the deductible part of self-employment tax, while EXCLUDING pensions, annuities and deferred compensation. Nothing in this dictionary knows which employer maintained the Archer HDHP, and summing every W-2 would over-state the cap in the taxpayer-favourable direction on exactly the multi-employer return where the cap bites.
FENCED, NOT DEFAULTED: ../archerMsaForm8853Line4Compensation is a hard 0 for a filer with no Archer contributions of either kind and the raw answer otherwise, so a filer who HAS contributions and leaves this blank leaves line 4, line 5 and the excess tests Incomplete and the return refused. That is the D1 direction the sibling line 2 intake already takes.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 Line 3 worksheet — the January line
Fact.Description:
The dollar the Line 3 Limitation Chart puts on the January line of its worksheet: 65% of the self-only annual deductible, 75% of the family annual deductible (37.5% on a married-filing-separately return), or -0- when the chart routes the month to its enter-zero line.
THE MARRIED-FAMILY REGIME OVERRIDES BOTH RATES AND BOTH DEDUCTIBLES, and it is checked BEFORE this filer's own answer. IRC 220(b)(3): "In the case of individuals who are married to each other, if either spouse has family coverage - (A) both spouses shall be treated as having only such family coverage (and if such spouses each have family coverage under different plans, as having the family coverage with the lowest annual deductible), and (B) the limitation under paragraph (1) ... shall be divided equally between them unless they agree on a different division." The instructions say it as two of the three How-To-Complete-Part-I combining rules and Publication 969 says it in one sentence: "you are treated as having family coverage with the lower annual deductible of the two health plans. The contribution limit is split equally between the two of you unless you agree on a different division." So on a MARRIED return where EITHER spouse has Archer family coverage, every eligible month of BOTH spouses is 37.5% - half of 75% - of ONE governing deductible, and self-only plans are disregarded ("Disregard any plans with self-only coverage").
THE PRINTED CHART SHOWS THE HALVING ONLY UNDER "Married filing separately", AND THAT IS NOT A NARROWER RULE - it is the one case where the couple's two halves are on two different returns, so it is the one case the chart has to spell out. On a JOINT return the same division happens inside the instructions' case (2)(a)/(b), which put the couple on ONE plan; only case (2)(c), gated on BOTH spouses having SELF-ONLY coverage, gives them separate Part Is. Reading the 75% cell without (2)(a)/(b) lets a joint couple with two family plans deduct up to TWICE the shared limitation, which is what this Case exists to prevent and what archer-msa-both-spouses-family-over-the-shared-limitation-refused pins.
UNANSWERED IS -0-, WHICH IS BOTH COMPLETE-SAFE AND ADVERSE. The IsComplete test comes FIRST (the unanswered-collection trap), so a return that never reached the Archer interview — every return committed to this repo today — resolves a hard 0 here rather than Incomplete, and a return that DID reach it and skipped a month gets the chart's own enter-zero answer rather than a guess. Cents are preserved; the single Round is at /archerMsaForm8853Line5DeductionTotal, the figure Schedule 1 line 23 receives.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 Line 3 worksheet — "Total for all months"
Fact.Description: The sum of the twelve worksheet lines, cents preserved. The worksheet prints this as its own line ("Total for all months") before dividing by 12.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet — "Limitation. Divide the total by 12."
Fact.Description:
The worksheet result, per filer: "Limitation from the Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet in the instructions", with a married couple's family limitation divided equally. /archerMsaForm8853Line3Limitation (the printed line 3) is this figure unless the spouses state an agreed division. The worksheet's last two lines are "Total for all months" and "Limitation. Divide the total by 12.", and this fact is that division.
CENTS SURVIVE THE DIVISION, deliberately. Twelve months of 65% of $4,000 is $31,200 and divides evenly, but $2,850 does not: 0.65 x 2850 x 12 / 12 = 1852.50. The worksheet's own printed cell is a dollars-and-cents cell ("$"), and the single Round in this chain is at /archerMsaForm8853Line5DeductionTotal, the figure that reaches Schedule 1 — which is the i1040gi page 23 rule ("include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total").
HARD 0 ON EVERY RETURN THAT NEVER REACHED THE ARCHER INTERVIEW, because all twelve worksheet lines are hard 0 there. Nothing in this repo moves.
PER FILER, because Part I is: "If you are filing jointly and both you and your spouse have high deductible health plans with self-only coverage, complete a separate Part I for each spouse." The instructions' two combining rules for a couple with more than one Archer MSA are a named gap, not a silence.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 3 — the limitation from the Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet
Fact.Description: FORM 8853 LINE 3, per filer: "Limitation from the Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet in the instructions". It is the worksheet result (../archerMsaLine3WorksheetLimitation), which divides a married couple's family limitation equally, UNLESS the spouses agree on a different division: on a married return where either spouse's Archer HDHP provides family coverage (/archerMsaEitherSpouseFamilyCoverageArcherHdhp) and this filer states an agreed share (../writableArcherMsaAgreedFamilyLimitShare), line 3 is that share, floored at $0 and capped at the whole family limitation for this filer's months (twice the equal half, the 75% of the annual deductible before division). On a joint return the two shares together may not exceed the couple's limitation (/knockoutArcherMsaAgreedFamilyLimitDivisionExceedsTheLimit). Cents are kept; the single Round is at /archerMsaForm8853Line5DeductionTotal. PER FILER, because Part I is.

Fact.Name: Your agreed share of the family Archer MSA limitation (Form 8853 line 3)
Fact.Description: When you are married and either spouse's Archer MSA high deductible health plan provides family coverage, the Archer MSA limitation is divided equally between you unless you both agree on a different division. Enter your share of the limitation for the year under that agreement, the amount that goes on Form 8853 line 3. Leave it unanswered for the equal division. Your share cannot be more than the whole limitation for your months (75% of the annual deductible); on a joint return both spouses' shares together may not exceed the couple's limitation.

Fact.Name: The spouses' agreed division of the family Archer MSA limitation adds up to more than the limitation
Fact.Description: Refuses a joint return on which either spouse states an agreed share of the family Archer MSA limitation and the two spouses' Form 8853 line 3 amounts together exceed the couple's limitation (the sum of the two equally divided worksheet limitations). The limitation is divided between the spouses, so the parts cannot add up to more than the whole. The filer corrects it by giving each spouse's agreed share so that the two add up to no more than the limitation.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 4 — compensation from the employer maintaining the HDHP, fenced
Fact.Description:
FORM 8853 LINE 4, per filer. HARD 0 for a filer whose Archer MSA took no contribution of either kind — for whom lines 3, 4 and 5 are all zero and no cap can bite — and the RAW INTAKE otherwise, which means INCOMPLETE, not 0, for a filer who HAS contributions and left the answer blank.
THE FENCE IS ../archerMsaFilerHasNoContributions AND NOT /archerMsaOnThisReturn, and the difference is the dormant legacy account (/archerMsaDormantLegacyAccountOnly). That return answers the MSA question YES and answers nothing else; fencing on the MSA answer would leave its line 4 Incomplete, which would spread into line 5 and into the Schedule 1 total, and would break a cell that files. Fencing on "no contributions" gives it a hard 0, which is also its correct line 4.
