INCOMPLETE IS THE ADVERSE DIRECTION AND THAT IS THE POINT: it refuses the filing (the narrowing predicate /archerMsaSectionAPartIFullyComputed requires this fact Complete) rather than handing the filer an uncapped deduction.

Fact.Name: This filer's ARCHER HDHP provided family coverage in at least one month of 2025
Fact.Description:
Whether any of the twelve Line 3 Limitation Chart answers is `family`. This is the ARCHER plan's coverage, which is a different question from ../archerMsaFamilyCoverageAnyTime — that fact answers the FORM 8889 line 4 fold-in condition off the HSA coverage chain, and a filer can hold an Archer HDHP with family coverage and an HSA HDHP with self-only coverage in the same month.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: every read is fenced with IsComplete first, so an unanswered vector is false rather than Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Either spouse's Archer HDHP provided family coverage in some month of 2025
Fact.Description:
The condition the employer-contribution rule puts on its CROSS-SPOUSE arm: "If you and your spouse are covered under an HDHP with family coverage and an employer made contributions to either of your Archer MSAs, neither you nor your spouse is allowed to make deductible contributions to an Archer MSA."
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE, and false is the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction here (it leaves the other spouse's deduction alive), which is accepted because the cell where it could bite — a couple with family Archer coverage who answered one spouse's vector and not the other's — has an Incomplete line 3 on the unanswered side and is refused for that reason.
MARRIED, NOT MFJ, matching /archerMsaSpouseAmountIncludedOnLine4 and /archerMsaDormantLegacyAccountOnly: the printed rule says "you and your spouse", with no filing-status condition.

Fact.Name: The ONE family annual deductible a married couple's Line 3 chart runs on
Fact.Description:
Read only when /archerMsaEitherSpouseFamilyCoverageArcherHdhp holds. When both spouses have Archer family coverage it is the LOWER of the two annual deductibles; when only one does, it is that spouse's, whichever spouse that is.
THE RULE IS PRINTED THREE TIMES AND STATUTORY ONCE. IRC 220(b)(3)(A): both spouses are treated as having only the family coverage, "and if such spouses each have family coverage under different plans, as having the family coverage with the lowest annual deductible". The instructions: "If both spouses have HDHPs with family coverage, you both are treated as having only the family coverage plan with the lowest annual deductible." Publication 969's Archer chapter: "you are treated as having family coverage with the lower annual deductible of the two health plans."
WHY IT IS RETURN-LEVEL AND NOT PER FILER: because it is ONE plan. The whole point of (b)(3)(A) is that the couple stops having two limitations and starts having one, and a per-filer fact would let the two halves disagree about which deductible they are halves of.
THE THIRD CASE IS THE SECONDARY FILER'S OWN FIGURE, not a zero. This fact is only ever read behind the regime gate, so the fallthrough is reached exactly when the regime holds and the PRIMARY has no family Archer coverage - which means the SECONDARY is the one who does. If that spouse left the deductible blank the fact is Incomplete, every family month is Incomplete, line 3 is Incomplete and the return is refused. Refusing is the right answer there; a 0 would silently zero the couple's limitation.

Fact.Name: Some filer on this return has Form 8853 line 1 employer Archer contributions
Fact.Description:
Whether either filer's Form 8853 line 1 (W-2 box 12 code R) is greater than zero. COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE — the IsComplete fence comes first on the secondary filer, and line 1 is itself complete-safe 0 for every W-2 that does not answer box 12 code R.
TWO CONSUMERS, and they want the same predicate for different reasons: the cross-spouse arm of the employer-contribution deduction bar, and the knockout for a code-R W-2 (/flowKnockoutArcherMsaEmployerContributionWithoutMsaAnswer) on a return whose Archer question is not answered yes.

Fact.Name: An employer Archer contribution bars this filer's Form 8853 line 5 deduction
Fact.Description:
The printed bar, in its two arms. ARM 1, the filer's own: "If an employer made contributions to your Archer MSA, you aren't entitled to a deduction." ARM 2, the cross-spouse one: "If you and your spouse are covered under an HDHP with family coverage and an employer made contributions to either of your Archer MSAs, neither you nor your spouse is allowed to make deductible contributions to an Archer MSA."
THE THIRD SENTENCE OF THE SAME PARAGRAPH IS WHY ARM 2 IS GATED ON FAMILY COVERAGE AND NOT ON MARRIAGE: "If you and your spouse both have an HDHP with self-only coverage and only one of you received employer contributions to an Archer MSA, the other spouse is allowed to make deductible contributions to an Archer MSA." A self-only couple is therefore NOT barred by the other spouse's employer contribution, and reading arm 2 without that sentence would refuse a deduction the instructions expressly allow.
WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not skip lines 3 and 4. The instructions' How To Complete Part I case (1) says to "Skip lines 3 and 4" and "Enter -0- on line 5", but that is a PRESENTATION instruction for a paper form; the excess-EMPLOYER-contribution test needs both figures ("the excess, if any, of your employer's contributions over the smaller of (a) your limitation on line 3 or (b) your compensation from the employer(s) who maintained your HDHP (line 4)"), so this dictionary computes lines 3 and 4 on a barred return and zeroes only line 5. A filer whose deduction is barred must still answer the vector and the compensation, and is refused until they do.

Fact.Name: IRC 220(b)(6) - the Archer MSA deduction is denied to this filer (Form 8853 line 5)
Fact.Description:
Whether IRC 220(b)(6) denies this filer the Archer MSA deduction, because another taxpayer may claim them as a dependent.
IT IS THE ARCHER TWIN OF A SHIPPING FACT AND IS DELIBERATELY A SEPARATE ONE. /filers/*/hsaDeductionDeniedAsDependent encodes IRC 223(b)(6) for the HSA and the two statutes are word-for-word identical apart from the section they sit in — but they deny different deductions on different forms, and a later change narrowing one must not silently narrow the other. Its reading of filers:/filers/*/canBeClaimed as the section-151 trigger and its IRC 151(d)(5)(B) answer to the zero-exemption objection are inherited by citation rather than re-derived. The HSA twin's printed-chain question is decided for the HSA only, by the owner ruling in TAX-INTERPRETATIONS-FOR-EXPERT-REVIEW.md AD-02; this Archer fact keeps the IRC 220 reading below.
IT IS A DEDUCTION DENIAL AND NOTHING ELSE. It does not make the filer ineligible under 220(c)(1)(A), it does not change the 220(b)(1)-(2) monthly limitation, and it therefore leaves Form 8853 lines 1, 2, 3 and 4 exactly where they were: only line 5 reads it. The money does not disappear — a contribution that is "neither excludable from gross income under section 106(b) nor allowable as a deduction under section 220 for such year" is an excess contribution by IRC 4973(d)(1), so it lands on Form 5329 line 39 and is taxed at 6%, and the return FILES rather than being refused.
THE READING NOT TAKEN, recorded because it is the one a reader reaches for first: that a dependent is simply not an eligible individual, which would send every month of the Line 3 Limitation Chart to its enter-zero line and take lines 3, 5 AND the Form 5329 line 35 unused-limit absorption down with it. Three things are against it. IRC 220(c)(1)(A) defines the eligible individual by high deductible health plan coverage and the absence of other coverage, and says nothing about dependency. The denial sits in subsection (b), among the LIMITATIONS ON THE DEDUCTION, not in (c). And the printed instruction states it as a bar on deducting: "you can't deduct contributions if you are someone else's dependent". Taking the eligibility reading would also cancel the 6% excise on a filer IRC 4973(d)(1) plainly taxes, which is the taxpayer-favourable direction on money the statute does not forgive.
THE OTHER SENTENCE OF THE SAME PRINTED PAIR IS NOT BUILT HERE AND DOES NOT NEED TO BE. "You can't deduct any contributions you made after you became enrolled in Medicare" is IRC 220(b)(7), and the Line 3 Limitation Chart already asks it FIRST, per month — "Were you enrolled in Medicare for the month?" Yes routes that month to the chart's enter-zero line, so a Medicare month contributes nothing to line 3 and nothing more is owed. Naming it here rather than leaving it silent, because the two sentences are printed together.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE on an unanswered filers:/filers/*/canBeClaimed, so every return in this repo that never reached the dependency question keeps its Form 8853 line 5 byte-identical.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 5 — the Archer MSA deduction, per filer
Fact.Description:
FORM 8853 LINE 5: "Archer MSA deduction. Enter the smallest of line 2, 3, or 4 here. Also include this amount on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 23" — and -0- when a bar applies. Where no bar applies it also includes the prior-year excess this year's unused room absorbs: the i5329 Line 35 instruction adds to line 5 the smaller of Form 5329 line 35 or the excess, if any, of line 34 over line 36.
CENTS PRESERVED HERE, ROUNDED ONCE AT /archerMsaForm8853Line5DeductionTotal. That is not cosmetic: rounding here would make the excess test below compare a cents-bearing line 2 with a rounded line 5 and manufacture an excess of up to 99 cents on a return that has none.
THE SMALLEST OF THREE IS A NESTED PAIR because LesserOf is binary; the nesting is associative and carries no order dependence.
TWO BARS LEAD THE SWITCH: line 5 is -0- when an employer contribution bars the deduction, and when IRC 220(b)(6) denies it to a filer another taxpayer may claim (../archerMsaDeductionDeniedAsDependent). The two Cases are independent and both resolve to the same 0, so their order carries no meaning; the dependent Case is written first only because the statute is the narrower and older bar. Lines 1, 2, 3 and 4 are untouched by either bar, and the denied contribution becomes a Form 5329 line 39 excess under IRC 4973(d)(1) rather than disappearing.

Fact.Name: This filer made EXCESS Archer MSA contributions (Form 8853 line 2 over line 5)
Fact.Description:
Whether the filer's own contributions exceed what is deductible, which the instructions define as a subtraction: "To figure your excess contributions, subtract your deductible contributions (line 5) from your actual contributions (line 2)." The form face says the same thing as a Caution under line 5: "Caution: If line 2 is more than line 5, you may have to pay an additional tax. See instructions."
THIS IS A DETECTION, NOT A COMPUTATION. The 6% excise on a remaining excess is Form 5329 PART VI, lines 34 to 41 - on disk, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f5329.pdf, page 2 is "Part VI Additional Tax on Excess Contributions to Archer MSAs", and https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f5329.pdf, page 1, "Part III Additional Tax on Excess Contributions to Traditional IRAs", is the IRA excise - priced per filer at ../archerMsaForm5329Line41ExciseTax and summed to Schedule 2 line 8 at /archerMsaExcessContributionExciseTaxForm5329PartVi. This fact is what ../archerMsaPartIComputedAndClean reads, and eight committed fixtures assert it; the second narrowing predicate ../archerMsaPartIComputedExcessesPriced does NOT read it, because the amount behind it is priced.
IT DOES NOT NET OFF A TIMELY WITHDRAWAL. The instructions allow an excess to be treated as never contributed if it is withdrawn with its earnings by the due date, and this dictionary has no Archer withdrawal intake. The direction is ADVERSE (a filer who has already cured the excess is still treated as holding it) and it is a named gap, not a silence.

Fact.Name: This filer received EXCESS EMPLOYER Archer contributions (line 1 over the smaller of 3 and 4)
Fact.Description:
Whether the employer's Archer contributions exceed the smaller of the line 3 limitation and the line 4 compensation, which is the instructions' own definition: "Excess employer contributions are the excess, if any, of your employer's contributions over the smaller of (a) your limitation on line 3 or (b) your compensation from the employer(s) who maintained your HDHP (line 4)."
THE EMPLOYER-CONTRIBUTIONS CELL DIVIDES ON THIS TEST. The excess-employer test needs Form 8853 lines 3 and 4, and both exist: an employer contribution WITHIN the smaller of lines 3 and 4 files, and one OVER it is priced elsewhere - Other income on Schedule 1 line 8z (/archerMsaSchedule1Line8zEmployerExcessOtherIncome) and the Form 5329 Part VI excise (see /flowKnockoutHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType).
A DETECTION, NOT A COMPUTATION, for the same reason as the own-excess sibling: the amount is ../archerMsaEmployerExcessContributionAmount.

Fact.Name: This filer's Form 8853 Part I is fully computed and carries no excess of either kind
Fact.Description:
The per-filer half of the narrowing predicate: every printed Part I line resolves, and neither excess test fires.
THE THREE IsComplete CONJUNCTS COME FIRST (the unanswered-collection trap), and they are what make an unanswered vector or an unanswered compensation REFUSE rather than resolve. Line 3 is complete-safe by construction, so its conjunct is a belt-and-braces that costs nothing and keeps the predicate honest if a later change makes the vector demanding.
WHY BOTH EXCESS TESTS ARE HERE RATHER THAN ON THE GUARD: they are per-filer facts, and a joint return with one clean spouse and one over-contributing spouse must be refused on the strength of the second. The return-level fact folds both filers in.

Fact.Name: THE NARROWING PREDICATE: Form 8853 Section A Part I is complete for this whole return
Fact.Description:
Whether every part of Form 8853 Section A Part I is computed for every filer on the return, and nothing it does not cover is present: no Section A Part II distribution, no Section B Medicare Advantage MSA that does not resolve, no excess contribution of either kind.
WHAT THIS FREES, stated as a cell rather than as a slogan. An Archer MSA holder — with employer contributions, own contributions, both or neither — who answered the twelve-month vector, the plan deductible and the compensation, whose contributions are within the printed limits, who took no distributions and holds no Medicare Advantage MSA, FILES, with the Form 8853 line 5 deduction reaching Schedule 1 line 23.
THE EXPORT SURFACE EXISTS. An export surface in this repo is an Export element carrying mef=true on the printed lines, and Form 8853 lines 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 carry it, which is the same surface Form 8889 and Form 5329 have. "No Form 8853 export surface" is therefore not a reason to refuse this cell: Form 8889 is equally an attachment, has no more of an export surface than mef-tagged facts, and files.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE on every return without an Archer MSA, because /archerMsaOnThisReturn is, and it leads.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 Section A Part I is prepared on two STATEMENT forms, one per spouse
Fact.Description:
Whether this return's Form 8853 Section A Part I is the instructions' case (2)(c) shape: a separate statement Form 8853 for each spouse with "statement" written across the top, and a controlling Form 8853 carrying the sums of lines 1, 2 and 5.
THE RULE IS NOT RE-DERIVED HERE. Its finding, cited rather than re-argued: the Section A rule is PART I ONLY and it adds LINES 1, 2 AND 5 — not 6a, not 6b, not 6c, not 7, not 8, not 9b — and it fires in the one narrow case where both spouses hold self-only-coverage HDHPs.
THE THREE PRINTED CONDITIONS, each mapped to an operand. "If you are filing jointly" is filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ — MFJ and not merely married, because on a married-filing-separately return each spouse files their own controlling Form 8853 and there is no second Part I to attach. "both you and your spouse have high deductible health plans with self-only coverage" is the pair of line 3 limitations being positive with /archerMsaEitherSpouseFamilyCoverageArcherHdhp false: this dictionary asks coverage type per month rather than per plan, so "has a self-only HDHP" is read off the chart — a filer whose twelve-month vector produced a positive limitation had an Archer HDHP in some month, and with family coverage excluded return-wide that month's coverage can only have been self-only. /archerMsaOnThisReturn is the third operand and is not redundant with the other two: Part I is reached at all only by a return that says it holds an Archer MSA.
WHY IT IS A FACT AT ALL WHEN NO AMOUNT READS IT. It is the condition under which the two controlling-form totals below are the PRINTED sum of two statement forms rather than an arithmetic identity, and the distinction matters: on the family couple the same Add is warranted by IRC 220(b)(3)(B)'s equal division instead, and confusing the two warrants would let a joint couple deduct twice the shared limitation. Stating the condition keeps the two roads distinguishable to a reader and to the application, which must print "statement" on two forms only in this case.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE. The MFJ operand leads, so a single, HoH, QSS or MFS return is false without reading a filer path at all; and on an MFJ return with no Archer activity both line 3 limitations are the hard 0 they are by construction. The secondary-filer read is fenced by IsComplete first (the unanswered-collection trap).

Fact.Name: Form 8853 CONTROLLING FORM, LINE 1 — the return's employer Archer contributions
Fact.Description:
The amount printed on line 1 of the Form 8853 this return files: "Total employer contributions to your Archer MSA(s) for 2025".
TWO WARRANTS FOR ONE Add, and they are named separately because collapsing them is an error the line 5 total's own Description guards against. On the case (2)(c) couple the sum is PRINTED — "add lines 1, 2, and 5 from the two statement Forms 8853 and enter those totals on the respective lines of the controlling Form 8853". On every other MFJ return there is one Form 8853 and its line 1 is already both spouses' figure, because the Line 1 instruction says so in its own words: "Employer contributions include any amount an employer contributes to any Archer MSA for you or your spouse for 2025". Both roads end in the same Add; /archerMsaSeparatePartIForEachSpouse is what tells them apart.
MFJ, NOT MARRIED, for the reason /archerMsaForm8853Line5DeductionTotal already gives: on an MFS return each spouse files their own 1040 with their own controlling Form 8853, and summing on filers:/isMarried would print the spouse's employer contributions on it. That divergence from /archerMsaBothFilersContributionsTotal — which DOES aggregate on isMarried, because IRC 223(b)(5)(B)(i) reduces a SHARED married HSA limitation — is deliberate and is the first thing to check here.
THIS IS NOT /archerMsaBothFilersContributionsTotal. That fact is lines 1 AND 2 together, it exists for the Form 8889 line 4 fold-in, and it falls back to the primary filer's own total when the secondary's is missing. This one is line 1 alone, it is a printed Form 8853 line, and a missing operand contributes 0 rather than being papered over.
CENTS ARE KEPT AND THERE IS NO Round HERE. Lines 1 and 2 are cents-bearing on the statement forms, so their controlling-form totals are too; the single Round in the Form 8853 chain stays at /archerMsaForm8853Line5DeductionTotal, which is the only figure that leaves the form (Schedule 1 line 23). Rounding here would print a controlling form whose line 1 does not equal the sum of the two statement forms it was made from.
THE IsComplete FENCE IS LOSSLESS FOR THE SAME REASON THE LINE 5 TOTAL'S IS: line 1 is complete-safe 0 by construction on every filer (the code-R sum defaults to 0), so the fence can only fire on a filer path that does not exist, where 0 is the right contribution.
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 ON EVERY RETURN WITHOUT AN ARCHER MSA.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 CONTROLLING FORM, LINE 2 — the return's own Archer contributions
Fact.Description:
The amount printed on line 2 of the Form 8853 this return files: "Archer MSA contributions you made for 2025, including those made in 2026 by the unextended due date of your return that were for 2025. Don’t include rollovers."
THE SAME TWO WARRANTS AS THE LINE 1 SIBLING, and one difference worth stating. Line 1's own instruction already says "for you or your spouse", so its MFJ sum is printed twice over; line 2's says "contributions you made to your Archer MSA in 2025" in the singular, so on a joint return the couple's figure is a sum either by case (2)(c)'s printed rule or by the two spouses having one controlling form between them. Neither road reaches a different number.
THE "Don't include rollovers" CLAUSE IS NOT SILENCED HERE, it is carried upstream: the per-filer /filers/*/archerMsaForm8853Line2OwnContributions and its intake are where the exclusion is stated, and this total adds two figures that already honour it.
MFJ NOT MARRIED, CENTS KEPT, NO Round, IsComplete FIRST — all four for the reasons written on /archerMsaControllingForm8853Line1Total, with one qualification the sibling does not need. An unanswered line 2 on a return that answered the Archer question YES is INCOMPLETE by design (defaulting it to 0 would overstate Form 8889 line 5; see /filers/*/archerMsaForm8853Line2OwnContributions). So this total's fence CAN fire on a real return. It is still lossless where it matters: a return whose line 2 is Incomplete fails /archerMsaSectionAPartIFullyComputed and /archerMsaForm8853FullyComputed alike and does not file, so no controlling Form 8853 is ever printed from the fenced value.
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 ON EVERY RETURN WITHOUT AN ARCHER MSA, where line 2 is a hard 0 on both filers.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 LINE 23 — the Archer MSA deduction this return takes
Fact.Description:
The Archer MSA deduction that reaches Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 23, in whole dollars. Form 8853 line 5 says so on its face: "Also include this amount on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 23".
THE JOINT SUM HAS TWO DIFFERENT WARRANTS AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS PARAGRAPH NAMED ONLY ONE OF THEM, WRONGLY. It read: "THE JOINT SUM IS PRINTED, NOT INFERRED. When both spouses complete a Part I the instructions say to add lines 1, 2, and 5 from the two statement Forms 8853". That printed rule is How To Complete Part I case (2)(C) ONLY, and case (2)(c) is gated on BOTH SPOUSES HAVING SELF-ONLY COVERAGE - "c. If both spouses have HDHPs with self-only coverage, complete a separate Form 8853, Section A, Part I, for each spouse", continuing across the column break with "Next, add lines 1, 2, and 5 from the two statement Forms 8853". Citing it for the FAMILY case was a misread, and it was the misread that let a joint couple with two family plans deduct twice the shared limitation. SO: on the BOTH-SELF-ONLY couple the sum is printed, at case (2)(c). On the FAMILY couple the sum is the arithmetic of IRC 220(b)(3)(B)'s EQUAL DIVISION - one limitation, halved, each half capped by that spouse's own line 2 and line 4 - and the sum of the two halves can never exceed the one limitation. Both roads end in the same Add; only the family road needed the halving, which now happens upstream in the twelve chart facts.
MFJ, NOT MARRIED — A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM THE LINE 4 AGGREGATION, and it is the divergence a reviewer should check first. /archerMsaBothFilersContributionsTotal and /archerMsaDormantLegacyAccountOnly aggregate on filers:/isMarried, MFS included, because IRC 223(b)(5)(B)(i) reduces a SHARED married HSA limitation by "the aggregate amount paid to Archer MSAs of such spouses" — one limit, both spouses' contributions. A DEDUCTION is not shared: on an MFS return each spouse files their own 1040 and takes their own line 5, and the "controlling Form 8853" the instructions describe is the JOINT return's. Summing on isMarried would give an MFS filer their spouse's deduction as well as their own.
THE SINGLE Round IS HERE, per i1040gi page 23 ("include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total"), and it is the only Round in the Form 8853 chain.
THE IsComplete FENCE IS PROVABLY LOSSLESS, not merely safe. A filer whose line 5 is Incomplete contributes 0 here. Could that under-state a real deduction on a return that FILES? No: a return files only if /flowKnockoutHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType is false, which needs either /archerMsaDormantLegacyAccountOnly (whose filers have line 2 = 0, so a true deduction of 0) or /archerMsaSectionAPartIFullyComputed (which requires IsComplete on every filer's line 5). Both branches make the fenced-out amount provably zero. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Knockout: a W-2 box 12 code R against a return that does not claim an Archer MSA
Fact.Description:
Fires when some filer's W-2 reports an employer Archer MSA contribution (box 12 code R) and the return's Archer MSA question does NOT resolve yes — either answered no, or never reached at all.
THE DEFECT IS A CONTRADICTION between two answers on the same return. Box 12 code R is the employer's statement that it contributed to an Archer MSA "for you or your spouse"; a return carrying it MUST file Form 8853 ("You (or your employer) made contributions for 2025 to your Archer MSA"). A return that then says it has no medical savings account would file with a Form 8889 line 4 reduction taken off a form it did not attach, and with lines 3, 4 and 5 of that form never asked.
WHY IT COVERS THE NEVER-ASKED CASE TOO, and not only an explicit Archer-MSA answer of NO. /hasHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType is asked only inside the HSA section, so a filer with a code-R W-2 and no HSA activity is never asked at all — and their return has exactly the same defect, with exactly the same remedy. Refusing only the explicit-no half would leave the wider half filing, and the difference between them is an interview-reach accident rather than a fact about the return. Both halves are Not(/archerMsaOnThisReturn), which is one operand.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, which matters because this fact joins flow:/flowIsKnockedOut's Any, where an Incomplete member would make the whole aggregate Incomplete rather than false. Both operands are complete-safe: /archerMsaEitherFilerHasEmployerContributions fences the secondary filer with IsComplete and reads a line 1 that is itself complete-safe 0, and /archerMsaOnThisReturn is complete-safe false by its own construction.
THE FIX IS AN INTAKE, NOT A COMPUTATION: the application should ask — or prefill — the Archer MSA question whenever a W-2 carries box 12 code R, at which point the return either answers yes and completes Form 8853 Section A, or the code-R entry is corrected.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 line 6a — total Archer MSA distributions received in 2025
Fact.Description:
Form 8853 LINE 6a: "Total distributions you and your spouse received in 2025 from all Archer MSAs (see instructions)".
RETURN-LEVEL, NOT PER FILER, AND THE PRINTED LINE IS THE WHOLE REASON. Part I splits per spouse ("If you are filing jointly and both you and your spouse have high deductible health plans with self-only coverage, complete a separate Part I for each spouse"); Part II does the opposite and aggregates on its face — "you and your spouse ... from all Archer MSAs" — onto the one controlling Form 8853. Section B, by contrast, says "complete a separate Section B for each spouse". Three different aggregations on one form, each followed literally.
THE INSTRUCTIONS NAME THE SOURCE DOCUMENT: "These amounts should be shown in box 1 of Form 1099-SA." This dictionary has no Archer 1099-SA collection, so the figure is asked as one number rather than harvested; that is a SCREEN-WORDING obligation.
FENCED, NOT DEFAULTED: /archerMsaForm8853Line6aTotalDistributions is a hard 0 on a return with no Archer MSA and on a return that answered the distributions question NO, and this raw answer otherwise — so a return that answers YES and leaves this blank leaves line 6c, line 8, line 9b and Form 5329 line 36 Incomplete, and the guard keeps refusing it.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 6a — total Archer MSA distributions, fenced
Fact.Description:
The line 6a figure the rest of Part II reads. Hard 0 on every return without Archer distributions, the raw intake otherwise.
THE TWO HARD-0 ARMS ARE WHAT MAKE THIS FACT COMPLETE-SAFE, and the order matters. The FIRST arm is Not(/archerMsaOnThisReturn), which is complete-safe FALSE on every return in the repo that never reached the Archer interview — that is what holds every committed scenario at $0 on Schedule 1 line 8e. The SECOND is /archerMsaNoSectionAPartIiDistributions, the already-shipping answered-NO gate, which is an All(IsComplete, Not) and therefore never leaks an Incomplete.
THE THIRD ARM IS DELIBERATELY BARE. A return that says it took distributions and does not say how much has an Incomplete line 6a, an Incomplete line 8 and a refused filing. Defaulting to 0 would let it file with the distribution untaxed, which is the direction this dictionary never takes on a missing amount (the direction the line 2 sibling takes).

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 line 6b — rollovers and timely-withdrawn excess included in line 6a
Fact.Description:
Form 8853 LINE 6b: "Distributions included on line 6a that you rolled over to another Archer MSA or a health savings account. Also include any excess contributions (and the earnings on those excess contributions) included on line 6a that were withdrawn by the unextended due date of your return. See instructions".
ONE PRINTED LINE, TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, AND THIS INTAKE DOES NOT SPLIT THEM. The printed line mixes a rollover (never taxable, IRC 220(f)(5)) with a timely-withdrawn excess (which 4973(d)'s flush text treats "as an amount not contributed"). The two have DIFFERENT downstream consequences: both reduce line 6c, but only the second should reduce the Form 5329 line 39 excess. This dictionary asks the single printed number, so it cannot make the second reduction — a named gap, and the direction is taxpayer-ADVERSE (an excess already cured by a timely withdrawal is still taxed at 6%).
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 WHEN UNANSWERED, which is the ADVERSE direction here (a larger line 6c, a larger taxable line 8): most Part II filers have no rollover at all, and refusing the whole population to catch the few who do would be the wrong trade. The fence is on /archerMsaForm8853Line6bRolloversAndWithdrawnExcess.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 6b — rollovers and withdrawn excess, complete-safe 0
Fact.Description: The line 6b figure, 0 when nobody answered. See the writable for why 0 rather than Incomplete is the right default on this line and why it is the ADVERSE direction.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 6c — line 6a less line 6b
Fact.Description:
FORM 8853 LINE 6c: "Subtract line 6b from line 6a".
NO FLOOR, DELIBERATELY, AND THE FORM IS THE REASON. Line 8 carries the printed "If zero or less, enter -0-" and line 6c does not, so flooring here would silently move the printed floor one line up. A line 6b larger than line 6a is a self-contradictory answer (line 6b is defined as a subset of line 6a), and it produces a negative 6c that the line 8 floor absorbs — so the arithmetic never escapes, and the contradiction stays visible on the printed line where a reviewer can see it. NAMED, not silent: nothing in this dictionary refuses that contradiction.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 line 7 — unreimbursed qualified medical expenses
Fact.Description:
Form 8853 LINE 7: "Unreimbursed qualified medical expenses (see instructions)".
THE PRINTED DEFINITION IS NARROWER THAN "MEDICAL EXPENSES" AND THE SCREEN MUST SAY SO. The instructions scope line 7 to distributions "used for the qualified medical expenses ... of: 1. Yourself and your spouse; 2. All your dependents; and 3. Any person who would be your dependent except that: a. The person filed a joint return; b. The person had gross income of $5,200 or more; or c. You, or your spouse if filing jointly, are dependents of someone else." They then carve OUT withdrawals paying expenses of an individual who was not covered by an HDHP where a contribution was made for 2025, and they add a Caution that no Schedule A deduction may be taken for any amount included here. None of that is derivable from this dictionary; all of it is SCREEN WORDING.
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 WHEN UNANSWERED, which is the taxpayer-ADVERSE direction (the whole distribution becomes taxable). Fence on /archerMsaForm8853Line7UnreimbursedQualifiedMedicalExpenses.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 7 — unreimbursed qualified medical expenses, complete-safe 0
Fact.Description: The line 7 figure, 0 when nobody answered. See the writable for the printed definition the screen owes and for why 0 is the adverse-and-therefore-safe default.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 8 — taxable Archer MSA distributions (Schedule 1 line 8e)
Fact.Description:
FORM 8853 LINE 8: "Taxable Archer MSA distributions. Subtract line 7 from line 6c. If zero or less, enter -0-. Also include this amount in the total on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8e".
THE PRINTED FLOOR IS HERE AND ONLY HERE, which is the sibling rule the Form 8889 chain already follows: a floor belongs on the line that prints it. Cents are preserved; the single Round happens on the Schedule 1 line 9 total, which is where i1040gi puts it.
THE DESTINATION IS SHARED WITH SECTION B AND THAT IS PRINTED, NOT INFERRED: line 12 (Medicare Advantage MSA taxable distributions) reaches the SAME Schedule 1 line 8e, as /medicareAdvantageMsaSchedule1Line8eTaxableDistributions, an addend beside this one on income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome. The two never describe the same dollar - line 6a reads "all Archer MSAs" and line 10 reads "all Medicare Advantage MSAs" - so nothing here double-counts.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 line 9a — some line 8 distributions meet an exception to the 20% tax
Fact.Description:
Form 8853 LINE 9a: "If any of the distributions included on line 8 meet any of the Exceptions to the Additional 20% Tax (see instructions), check here".
THE THREE EXCEPTIONS ARE PRINTED AND ARE THE SCREEN'S WHOLE JOB: the additional 20% tax "doesn't apply to distributions made after the date that the account holder: Dies, Becomes disabled (see Disabled, earlier), or Turns age 65." All three are dated conditions on individual distributions, not on the return — the instructions' own Example 3 has one account holder with distributions on both sides of their 65th birthday — so the checkbox alone cannot price the tax, which is why line 9b needs its own amount and why this is a checkbox rather than a computation. This dictionary holds a date of birth and could in principle derive the age-65 half, and it deliberately does NOT: the age test is per DISTRIBUTION DATE, line 6a is a single annual total with no dates, and deriving "turned 65 during 2025 therefore excepted" would except the pre-birthday distributions the instructions expressly tax.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE WHEN UNANSWERED, which is the taxpayer-ADVERSE direction (the whole of line 8 is then subject to the 20% tax). Fence on /archerMsaForm8853Line9aExceptionChecked.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 9a — the exceptions checkbox, complete-safe false
Fact.Description: The line 9a checkbox, false when nobody answered. False is the ADVERSE reading: it sends the whole of line 8 into the 20% tax base.

Fact.Name: Writable: the part of Form 8853 line 8 that does NOT meet a 20%-tax exception
Fact.Description:
Asked only when line 9a is checked. The instructions define line 9b as "20% (0.20) of any amount included on line 8 that doesn't meet any of the exceptions" — so a checked line 9a splits line 8 into an excepted part and a taxed part, and this is the taxed part.
WHY IT IS ASKED RATHER THAN DERIVED, which is the same answer the Form 8889 sibling /filers/*/hsaAdditionalTaxExceptionAmountDerived gives for its own line: the split is per distribution and per date (the account holder's date of death, the date disability began, the 65th birthday), and line 6a is one annual total. There is nothing in the graph to split.
INCOMPLETE WHEN LINE 9a IS CHECKED AND THIS IS BLANK, deliberately. The alternatives are both wrong: 0 would except the entire distribution on the strength of a checkbox, and line 8 would make the checkbox meaningless. /archerMsaAmountSubjectToAdditional20PctTax carries that Incompleteness, so the return is refused rather than mispriced.

Fact.Name: The Form 8853 line 8 amount that carries the additional 20% tax
Fact.Description:
The multiplicand of line 9b: the whole of line 8 when no exception is claimed, and the claimed taxed part when line 9a is checked.
THE LesserOf IS A FENCE, NOT ARITHMETIC. The taxed part is by definition "an amount included on line 8", so it can never exceed line 8; capping it here means a wrong answer over-states nobody and cannot manufacture a tax on a distribution the return never reported. It does NOT rescue an under-stated answer, which is the direction only the screen can police.
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 ON EVERY RETURN WITHOUT AN ARCHER MSA, through line 8's own hard-0 arms; and INCOMPLETE exactly on the checked-but-unanswered cell.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 9b — the additional 20% tax (Schedule 2 line 17e)
Fact.Description:
FORM 8853 LINE 9b: "Additional 20% tax (see instructions). Enter 20% (0.20) of the distributions included on line 8 that are subject to the additional 20% tax. Also include this amount in the total on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 17e".
ROUNDED HERE, because line 9b is a printed line of the return and Schedule 2 line 17e carries it as printed. The Section A Part II figures are return-level, so unlike Form 5329 there is no per-spouse form to round separately.
LINE 17e, NOT 17c AND NOT 17f. 17c is the Form 8889 line 17b tax on unqualified HSA distributions and is already an addend of taxCalculations:/line21OfSchedule2; 17f is the additional FIFTY percent tax on a Medicare Advantage MSA (Form 8853 line 13b), which Section B carries at its own line. Routing to either would double-book a live printed line.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 LINE 8e — the Archer MSA leg
Fact.Description:
The Form 8853 line 8 amount as an addend of Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 9, fenced with IsComplete so an unanswered Part II contributes 0 rather than propagating Incompleteness into every return's total income.
THE FENCE IS PROVABLY LOSSLESS, not merely safe, and the argument is the same one the Schedule 1 line 23 fence makes. Line 8 is Incomplete only when line 6a is — i.e. the return said it took distributions and did not say how much — and such a return fails /archerMsaPartIiComputedAndClean, so /flowKnockoutHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType is true and the return does not file. No filing return can lose a dollar here.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 LINE 17e — the additional 20% Archer MSA distribution tax
Fact.Description: The Form 8853 line 9b amount as an addend of taxCalculations:/line21OfSchedule2, fenced with IsComplete for the same provably-lossless reason as the Schedule 1 line 8e sibling: line 9b is Incomplete only when line 6a or the line 9a taxed-part amount is, and both of those returns are refused by /flowKnockoutHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 5329 line 34 — this filer's prior-year excess Archer MSA contributions
Fact.Description:
Form 5329 LINE 34: "Enter the excess contributions from line 40 of your 2024 Form 5329. See instructions. If zero, go to line 39", and the instruction adds the condition the form face compresses: "Enter the amount from line 40 of your 2024 Form 5329 only if the amount on line 41 of your 2024 Form 5329 is more than zero."
NOTHING IN A TY2025 RETURN CARRIES A TY2024 FORM 5329, which is why this is asked rather than derived — the same reason the HSA sibling /filers/*/writableHsaPriorYearExcessContributionsForm5329Line48 gives for its own line 42.
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 WHEN UNANSWERED. That is the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction and it is accepted for one reason: the Archer population is closed and a carry-in is rare, while an Incomplete default would refuse every Archer return in the repo over a question almost none of them answer yes to. The cell where it could bite — a real 2024 carry-in the filer omitted — is a SCREEN-REACH question, not a fact this return carries, and it is routed rather than silenced.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 LINE 34 — prior-year excess Archer contributions, complete-safe 0
Fact.Description: The line 34 carry-in, 0 when nobody answered. See the writable for why 0 rather than Incomplete, and for the named screen-reach gap that default leaves.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 LINE 35 — the unused part of this filer's Archer contribution limit
Fact.Description:
FORM 5329 LINE 35: "If the contributions to your Archer MSAs for 2025 are less than the maximum allowable contribution, see instructions. Otherwise, enter -0-", and the instruction supplies both the difference and the limit: "If contributions to your Archer MSAs for 2025 were less than your contribution limit for Archer MSAs, enter the difference on line 35. Your contribution limit for Archer MSAs is the smaller of line 3 or line 4 of Form 8853".
THE FLOOR IS THE FORM'S OWN "Otherwise, enter -0-", so a filer who contributed at or above the limit enters nothing here and their carry-in is absorbed only by distributions.
IT IS 4973(d)(2)(B) IN PRINT: the statute reduces the prior year's excess by "the excess (if any) of (i) the maximum amount allowable as a deduction under section 220(b)(1) ... over (ii) the amount contributed to the accounts for the taxable year". The printed line uses the smaller of lines 3 and 4 where the statute names 220(b)(1) alone; the printed reading is the narrower of the two (line 4 is the 220(b)(4) compensation cap) and is the one followed, because it is the line the taxpayer fills in.
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 ON A RETURN WITH NO ARCHER MSA: line 3, line 4 and line 2 are all hard 0 there, so this is GreaterOf(0, 0 - 0).

Fact.Name: Form 5329 LINE 36 — 2025 Archer MSA distributions from Form 8853 line 8
Fact.Description:
FORM 5329 LINE 36: "2025 distributions from your Archer MSAs from Form 8853, line 8".
THIS IS WHERE THE PART VII MIRROR BREAKS, AND THE BREAK IS DECIDED HERE RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. Part VII's line 44 reads Form 8889 line 16, and Form 8889 is a PER-FILER form, so that line maps one-to-one. Form 8853 line 8 is RETURN-LEVEL by its own printed text ("Total distributions you and your spouse received in 2025 from all Archer MSAs", line 6a), while Form 5329 is filed by an individual ("Name of individual subject to additional tax"). On an unmarried return there is no ambiguity and the two are the same number. On a married return the return-level total cannot be attributed to one spouse by any derivation.
THE ARMS, AND THEIR ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. Unmarried filers read line 8 - that filer is never asked the split and their line 8 is unambiguously theirs. A married filer whose per-spouse split resolves (/archerMsaLine8PerSpouseSplitResolved) reads their OWN answered share of line 8. Every other married filer reads 0, and the intersection that makes that 0 matter — a married return with a nonzero line 8 AND a nonzero line 34 carry-in on some filer — is REFUSED by /archerMsaForm5329PartViAllocationUnresolvable. The 0 is the taxpayer-ADVERSE direction (a smaller line 37, so a larger line 38, so a larger excess), which is the safe direction for a number that only ever appears on a refused return. The middle arm can only be taken when both shares are Complete, so this line cannot become Incomplete on a filer it is otherwise Complete for.
WHY NOT SPLIT IT BY INFERENCE. Halving would invent an allocation no document supports; giving it all to each spouse would double-count it against two carry-ins. The per-spouse share is instead the taxpayer's own statement about their own accounts, which is what IRC 4973(a) and 4973(d)(2)(A) price; the full argument, including the IRS's own Example 2 asking the taxpayer for the same split, is on /filers/*/writableArcherMsaFilerShareOfLine8. The refused cell is narrow: line 36 does nothing at all unless line 34 is nonzero, which the form face says outright ("If zero, go to line 39").
THERE IS NO PER-SPOUSE LINE 8 TO READ, confirmed against the INSTRUCTIONS rather than the form face alone. The 2025 Instructions for Form 8853 carry a statement-Form-8853 rule for Section A Part I (lines 1, 2 and 5 only) and another for Section B (lines 10, 11, 12 and 13b), and NONE for Part II; the Line 6a instruction is "Enter the total distributions you and your spouse received" / "in 2025 from all Archer MSAs." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8853.pdf, page 5, RIGHT column).

Fact.Name: Form 5329 LINE 37 — add lines 35 and 36
Fact.Description: FORM 5329 LINE 37: "Add lines 35 and 36" — the two ways a prior-year excess is used up during 2025: room under this year's limit that nobody filled, and taxable distributions taken out of the account. IRC 4973(d)(2) names the same two reductions.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 LINE 38 — the prior-year excess that survived 2025
Fact.Description: FORM 5329 LINE 38: "Prior year excess contributions. Subtract line 37 from line 34. If zero or less, enter -0-". The printed floor is on this line and is applied here.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 LINE 39 — this filer's 2025 excess Archer MSA contributions
Fact.Description:
FORM 5329 LINE 39: "Excess contributions for 2025 (see instructions)", which the instructions define as "the excess of your contributions to your Archer MSA for 2025 from Form 8853, line 2 ... over your contribution limit (the smaller of line 3 or line 4 of Form 8853). Also include on line 39 any excess contributions your employer made."
TWO ADDENDS, one per printed sentence: the OWN excess and the EMPLOYER excess. Both are already detected in this module as booleans (../archerMsaOwnExcessContributionsExist and ../archerMsaEmployerExcessContributionsExist); this line is the amount those detections stood in for, which is what turns the residual's cell (3) from a refusal into a computation.
A NAMED DIVERGENCE FROM THE PRINTED i5329 SENTENCE, AND IT IS THE ONE A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK FIRST. i5329's line 39 measures the own excess as line 2 over the SMALLER OF LINES 3 AND 4; this fact measures it as line 2 over LINE 5, which is what i8853 says in its own words ("To figure your excess contributions, subtract your deductible contributions (line 5) from your actual contributions (line 2)"). The two agree everywhere EXCEPT the employer-bar cell, where Form 8853 line 5 is -0- by the printed bar while the smaller of lines 3 and 4 is not. There, i5329's literal text would find no own excess at all on money that IRC 4973(d)(1) plainly taxes: the statutory excess is the amount "which is neither excludable from gross income under section 106(b) nor allowable as a deduction under section 220 for such year", and IRC 220(b)(5) makes the barred contribution not allowable as a deduction. The statute and i8853 agree against the narrower reading of i5329, so the line-5 reading is taken.
IT STILL DOES NOT NET OFF A TIMELY WITHDRAWAL, and the printed line says "(unless withdrawn—discussed next)". This dictionary's only withdrawal figure is the mixed Form 8853 line 6b, which also carries rollovers, so it cannot be subtracted here without netting off rollovers too. ADVERSE and NAMED (G11).
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 on a return with no Archer MSA: lines 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 are all hard 0 there.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 LINE 40 — total excess Archer MSA contributions
Fact.Description: FORM 5329 LINE 40: "Total excess contributions. Add lines 38 and 39" — the prior-year carry-in that survived line 38 plus this year's own excess. It is also the figure that becomes NEXT year's line 34, which is why the form asks for it as a total rather than taxing the two halves separately.

Fact.Name: Writable: the value of this filer's Archer MSAs on December 31, 2025
Fact.Description:
The cap on Form 5329 line 41: "6% (0.06) of the smaller of line 40 or the value of your Archer MSAs on December 31, 2025 (including 2025 contributions made in 2026)". IRC 4973(a)'s flush text is the statutory form of the same cap ("The amount of such tax for any taxable year shall not exceed 6 percent of the value of the account ... determined as of the close of the taxable year").
REQUIRED ONCE THERE IS AN EXCESS: when this filer's Form 5329 line 40 is positive and this is unanswered, /flowKnockoutArcherMsaForm5329Line41AccountValueUnsupplied blocks submission, the same rule the HSA sibling /filers/*/writableHsaDecember31AccountValue carries. A filer with no excess is never asked and nothing reads it.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 line 41 — the smaller of line 40 and the December 31 account value
This filer has a positive Form 5329 line 40 excess and no December 31 Archer MSA value to cap it
Fact.Description: A pure detector, read only by the standalone knockout /flowKnockoutArcherMsaForm5329Line41AccountValueUnsupplied. It is not read by ../archerMsaForm5329Line41ExciseTax or by /archerMsaForm5329PartViSuppressed, so it adds no edge to the excise chain whose own suppressors are kept return-level to avoid a resolution cycle. IRC 4973(a)'s flush text and Form 5329 line 41 both make the December 31 account value a mandatory input once there is an excess to tax: the tax "shall not exceed 6 percent of the value of the account". True only when this filer's line 40 is positive AND ../writableArcherMsaDecember31AccountValue has not been answered. Complete false whenever the value is answered; follows line 40's completeness otherwise.

Fact.Name: A filer's Form 5329 line 40 Archer MSA excess with no December 31 account value to cap it
Fact.Description: Screen text: "You reported excess contributions to an Archer MSA, but not the value of your Archer MSAs on December 31, 2025. The 6% tax on Form 5329 line 41 is figured on the smaller of your excess contributions or that account value, so we need the account value (including 2025 contributions made in 2026) before you can file." Blocks submission when either filer's Form 5329 line 40 is positive and that filer's December 31 value was not supplied. The primary filer's detector is read through a count of the /filers items that are the primary filer and trip it; the secondary filer's only on a joint return, because only a joint return carries the spouse's Form 5329. Supplying the value clears it and line 41 computes on the smaller figure.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 LINE 41 — this filer's own 6% excise tax on excess Archer contributions
Fact.Description:
FORM 5329 LINE 41: 6% of ../archerMsaForm5329Line41CapAmount, rounded on THIS FILER'S OWN FORM. "Include this amount on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 8."
THE ROUNDING IS PER FILER for the reason the Part VII sibling /filers/*/hsaForm5329Line49ExciseTax sets out at length and this fact does not repeat: Form 5329 is an individual's form, so on a joint return where both spouses owe this tax there are two Forms 5329, each printing its own whole-dollar line, and Schedule 2 line 8 carries their total.
$0 FOR A FILER ON A RETURN THAT IS REFUSED, which is the rule that keeps the printed Schedule 2 total honest. Two suppressors, both return-level and neither derived from the guard (reading the guard here would close a resolution cycle): the unresolvable Form 5329 line 36 allocation, and a Medicare Advantage MSA whose Section B does not resolve (Not(/archerMsaSectionBResolvedOrAbsent)). Lines 34 to 40 keep their true values either way, so the arithmetic stays witnessed by the fixtures; only the printed line 41 is suppressed.
COMPLETE-SAFE $0 on every return that never reached the Archer interview, because every input is.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 line 41 for the Schedule 2 sum, 0 when it does not resolve
Fact.Description:
The line 41 amount fenced with IsComplete so the return-level CollectionSum stays complete-safe.
THE FENCE IS PROVABLY LOSSLESS, not merely safe. Line 41 is Incomplete only when some Part I or Part II input this filer owes is Incomplete — line 3, line 4, line 5 through the excess legs, or Form 8853 line 8 through line 36 — and every one of those states fails /archerMsaForm8853FullyComputed and fails /archerMsaSectionAPartIFullyComputed, so /flowKnockoutHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType is true and the return does not file. No filing return can lose a dollar of excise tax here.
MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, THAT THE FENCE IS NEEDED.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 Part VI — the 6% excise tax on excess Archer MSA contributions (Schedule 2 line 8)
Fact.Description:
Both filers' Form 5329 line 41, summed for Schedule 2 (Form 1040) line 8, which reaches Schedule 2 line 21 and then Form 1040 line 23.
THE DESTINATION IS THE ONE THE FORM PRINTS and the one this dictionary already reaches twice for Form 5329: line 41 says "Include this amount on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 8", and both form5329:/form5329AdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions (Part I line 4) and /hsaExcessContributionExciseTaxForm5329PartVii (Part VII line 49) are already addends of taxCalculations:/line21OfSchedule2 on that same printed line. It is NOT Schedule 2 line 17e (the 20% tax on Archer distributions, /archerMsaSchedule2Line17eAdditional20PctTax), which is a different printed line for a different tax.
MFJ, NOT MARRIED, AND NOT A CollectionSum. A Switch(IsComplete(/filers) -> CollectionSum(/filers/*/...)) SUMS BOTH FILERS ON AN MFS RETURN, where /filers carries two items and each spouse files their own 1040 — so an MFS filer whose SPOUSE over-contributed would pay the spouse's 6% excise on their own Schedule 2 line 8. The shape used is the one /archerMsaForm8853Line5DeductionTotal ships, and its Description carries the warrant: "A DEDUCTION is not shared: on an MFS return each spouse files their own 1040". Neither is a TAX. The Part VII sibling /hsaExcessContributionExciseTaxForm5329PartVii uses the same Add idiom.
NO OUTER IsComplete(/filers) GUARD: the Add idiom names /primaryFiler and /secondaryFiler directly and never iterates the collection, so the Placeholder-on-a-never-answered-collection hazard such a guard exists for cannot arise. A later editor who reintroduces a CollectionSum must reintroduce the guard with it: a CollectionSum over a never-answered collection resolves Placeholder, and this fact is an addend of a printed total.
COMPLETE-SAFE $0 on every return that answers nothing.

Fact.Name: The AMOUNT of this filer's excess employer Archer MSA contributions
Fact.Description:
The figure ../archerMsaEmployerExcessContributionsExist detects, priced: "the excess, if any, of your employer's contributions over the smaller of (a) your limitation on line 3 or (b) your compensation from the employer(s) who maintained your HDHP (line 4)."
IT IS THE SAME SUBTRACTION THE BOOLEAN ALREADY DOES, expressed once with a floor. The boolean keeps its own body rather than being rewritten as GreaterThan(this, 0): the two are the same predicate, and repointing it would move a fact eight committed fixtures assert.
IT FEEDS TWO PLACES AND THEY ARE NOT DOUBLE-COUNTING. It is an addend of Form 5329 line 39 (the 6% EXCISE on an excess still in the account at year end) and it is the amount of /archerMsaSchedule1Line8zEmployerExcessOtherIncome (the INCOME INCLUSION, because an employer contribution over the limit was never excludable under IRC 106(b) in the first place). Those are two different taxes on one amount, both printed, and i8853 imposes both in the same paragraph.
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 on a return with no Archer MSA: lines 1, 3 and 4 are all hard 0 there.

Fact.Name: Writable: the excess employer Archer contribution is already included in W-2 box 1 wages
Fact.Description:
The condition i8853 puts on the Other-income report: "If the excess wasn't included in income on Form W-2, you must report it as “Other income” on your tax return."
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE WHEN UNANSWERED, i.e. the default assumption is that the excess was NOT already taxed and must be reported. That is the taxpayer-ADVERSE direction, and it is the right one here: the amount reaches this dictionary through box 12 code R, which is by construction the EXCLUDED figure, so "not in box 1" is also the ordinary case rather than merely the safe one. A filer whose employer did include it says so and the leg drops to 0.
WHY IT IS ONE RETURN-LEVEL ANSWER RATHER THAN ONE PER FILER: the leg it gates is a single Schedule 1 line 8z amount, the question is about how one employer filled in one W-2, and splitting it per filer would ask a joint couple two versions of a question whose only effect is on their combined line 9. A NAMED GAP: a joint return where one spouse's employer included the excess and the other's did not cannot express that, and answering yes there would drop BOTH legs. The adverse answer (leave it false) is always available and is the default.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 LINE 8z — the excess employer Archer contribution as "Other income"
Fact.Description:
Both filers' excess employer Archer MSA contributions, reported as Other income on Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 8z unless the return says the employer already included the amount in W-2 box 1 wages.
LINE 8z, NOT 8e. Line 8e is the Archer DISTRIBUTIONS line and is the printed home of Form 8853 lines 8 and 12; the instructions do not name a line for this amount, they say only "report it as “Other income” on your tax return", and Schedule 1 line 8z is this dictionary's — and the Form 1040 instructions' — residual Other-income line. NAMED as an interpretation rather than a citation: no IRS text says "8z" for this amount.
THE SINGLE Round IS HERE, following the i1040gi rule the Schedule 1 line 23 sibling cites: include cents when adding and round the total once. The per-filer amounts keep their cents.
THE IsComplete FENCE IS PROVABLY LOSSLESS by the same argument as the Part VI total and the line 8e leg: a filer whose line 3 or line 4 is Incomplete cannot satisfy /archerMsaForm8853FullyComputed and their return does not file.
MFJ, NOT MARRIED, for exactly the reason the Form 5329 Part VI total gives at length and this fact does not repeat: summing /filers/* would, on an MFS return, put the SPOUSE's excess employer contribution into this filer's Other income. The shape is the /archerMsaForm8853Line5DeductionTotal idiom. The spouse's excess is income on the spouse's own return, which this dictionary does not model.

Fact.Name: The excess employer Archer contribution for the Schedule 1 sum, 0 when it does not resolve
Fact.Description: ../archerMsaEmployerExcessContributionAmount fenced with IsComplete, so the return-level Other-income sum stays complete-safe on the three committed W-2 code-R fixtures whose line 4 compensation is Incomplete by design. Provably lossless for the reason the line 41 sibling gives.

Fact.Name: The return says the excess employer contribution is already in W-2 wages
Fact.Description: /writableArcherMsaEmployerExcessAlreadyInW2Income made complete-safe FALSE, so an unanswered return reports the excess as Other income rather than dropping it. The adverse default is argued on the writable.

Fact.Name: This return has to split Form 8853 line 8 between two spouses
Fact.Description:
THE POPULATION THE PER-SPOUSE INTAKE IS ASKED OF. A MARRIED return with a nonzero Form 8853 line 8: line 8 is return-level by its own printed text ("Total distributions you and your spouse received in 2025 from all Archer MSAs"), Form 5329 is filed by an individual ("Name of individual subject to additional tax"), and on a married return nothing else in this dictionary says whose distribution it was.
IT IS WIDER THAN /archerMsaForm5329PartViAllocationUnresolvable ON PURPOSE, and the difference is the carry-in conjunct. The refusal needs a nonzero line 34 somewhere, because line 36 does nothing without one ("If zero, go to line 39"); the QUESTION does not, because a couple whose line 34s are both zero this year still files a printed line 36 on each Form 5329, and printing the true share beats printing a zero the form did not intend.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE on every return without an Archer MSA: line 8 is a hard 0 there, through the same arms that make /archerMsaForm5329PartViAllocationUnresolvable complete-safe false.

Fact.Name: Writable: how much of Form 8853 line 8 came out of THIS filer's own Archer MSAs
Fact.Description:
Asked only when /archerMsaLine8PerSpouseSplitApplies. It covers the married Form 5329 line 36 cell for /flowKnockoutHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType.
WHAT IS BEING ASKED. Form 8853 line 8 is the couple's combined taxable Archer MSA distribution. This is the part of it that came out of accounts of which THIS filer is the account holder. The two answers must add up to line 8; if they do not, the return is refused rather than repaired.
WHY IT IS ASKED RATHER THAN DERIVED. There is no per-spouse line 8 anywhere on the return: the 2025 Instructions for Form 8853 print their multiple-Form-8853 rules four times and every one of the four leaves lines 6a through 9b on the ONE controlling form. The IRS's own Example 2 nevertheless requires the taxpayer to know this split for line 9b, so the question is one a taxpayer can answer.
NO DEFAULT, DELIBERATELY. A 0 default would give the whole distribution to the spouse who left the box blank; a line-8 default would give it to both. Unanswered stays Incomplete and the return keeps refusing, which is the residue the contract calls the correct permanent refusal.
The question is asked when /archerMsaLine8PerSpouseSplitApplies, deliberately wider than the Part-VI guard.

Fact.Name: This filer's share of Form 8853 line 8, or zero where the question was never reached
Fact.Description:
The IsComplete fence on the intake. Hard 0 off-population and wherever the split question was not asked; BARE - and therefore Incomplete - on the asked-and-blank cell, which is the arm that keeps /archerMsaForm5329PartViAllocationUnresolvable true for an unanswered split.
THE ORDER OF THE THREE ARMS IS THE WHOLE POINT. Off-population comes FIRST, so a return that never had an Archer MSA carries a Complete 0 rather than inheriting the intake's Incompleteness into the return-level total below.
THE SECOND ARM IS THE SPOUSE ON A NON-MFJ MARRIED RETURN, AND IT IS A LATENT-TRAP FIX RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE. /archerMsaLine8PerSpouseSplitApplies reads filers:/isMarried, which is true on a married-filing-separately return; but an MFS filer prepares their OWN Form 8853, so the whole of that return's line 8 is the primary filer's and the spouse is never asked this question. Without this arm the spouse's bare unanswered writable would go Incomplete the moment the primary answered, which would carry Incompleteness through Form 5329 lines 36, 37, 38, 40 and 41 into /filers/*/archerMsaPartIComputedExcessesPriced and RE-REFUSE an MFS return that files. The arm is the exact complement of the MFJ gate on the second addend of /archerMsaLine8PerSpouseSplitTotal: the spouse whose answer the total does not read is the spouse whose answer this fact does not read either.
ON AN MFJ RETURN the second arm's When is false for both filers, so this fact is exactly what it would be without the arm, and off-population the first arm already fires. ON AN MFS RETURN the arm is live: tests/nodes/ty2025/form8889/archer-msa-mfs-line-8-split-answered-secondary-share-arm-holds answers the split on an MFS return and prices a $45 excise (through arm 3), and this arm is what keeps its six secondary-filer completeness rows and the FullyComputed and guard verdicts Complete.

Fact.Name: The two spouses' answered shares of Form 8853 line 8, added
Fact.Description:
The controlling-form total of the per-spouse shares, in the Add(primary fenced, MFJ-gated secondary) idiom this module already uses for /medicareAdvantageMsaForm8853Line12Total and its three siblings.
THE MFJ GATE, NOT filers:/isMarried, ON THE SECOND ADDEND. On a married-filing-separately return the filer prepares their own Form 8853, so the whole of that return's line 8 is the primary filer's and there is no second share to add; gating the secondary out makes the equality below read "the primary's answer IS line 8", which is the right test there. The POPULATION gate above stays filers:/isMarried, exactly as /archerMsaForm5329PartViAllocationUnresolvable's does, so no new MFS behaviour is invented here.
IT IS NOT EXPORTED AND IT IS NOT A PRINTED LINE. Nothing on Form 8853 or Form 5329 prints this sum; it exists only to be compared with line 8.

Fact.Name: The per-spouse split of Form 8853 line 8 is answered and consistent
Fact.Description:
THE PREDICATE THAT NARROWS THE REFUSAL. Both spouses answered their own share and the two answers add up to the return-level line 8 they decompose.
THE EQUALITY IS THE CONTRADICTION TEST AND IS NOT A FENCE. A pair of shares that does not sum to line 8 is not a smaller or larger version of the right answer; it is a return whose two statements about one distribution disagree, and IRC 4973 prices each spouse's own accounts, so neither statement can be preferred. Such a return keeps refusing.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE off-population, because /archerMsaLine8PerSpouseSplitApplies leads and is. On an MFJ return whose secondary share is blank, the IsComplete conjunct is false and the whole All is Complete false rather than Incomplete, which is what keeps the guard above it from ever going Incomplete on a BlockSubmissionOnTrue path.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 line 36 cannot be attributed to a spouse on this return
Fact.Description:
The one cell the Form 5329 Part VI build cannot price: a MARRIED return that has a nonzero Form 8853 line 8 AND a nonzero line 34 carry-in on either filer, and whose per-spouse split of line 8 does not resolve (Not(/archerMsaLine8PerSpouseSplitResolved)).
WHY IT IS A REFUSAL RATHER THAN AN ALLOCATION. Form 8853 line 8 is return-level by its own printed text; Form 5329 line 36 wants that number on ONE spouse's form. Nothing derivable attributes a return-level distribution total to a spouse, and both available guesses are wrong in a measurable direction — halving invents an allocation, and giving it to both double-absorbs one distribution against two carry-ins.
THE SUCCESSOR IS AN INTAKE, /filers/*/writableArcherMsaFilerShareOfLine8. WHAT FILES: a married Archer couple with a carry-in who say, each for their own accounts, how much of Form 8853 line 8 came out of them, and whose two answers add up to line 8. Their Form 5329 line 36 is their own share, their line 41 is not suppressed by /archerMsaForm5329PartViSuppressed, and /archerMsaForm8853FullyComputed can resolve, which is what narrows /flowKnockoutHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType.
WHAT REFUSES IS THE DATA-COMPLETENESS RESIDUE AND NOTHING ELSE, in two cells. (i) THE SPLIT UNANSWERED: the interview reached the question and the boxes are blank, so /filers/*/archerMsaFilerShareOfLine8OrZero is Incomplete and nothing can be attributed. (ii) THE SPLIT CONTRADICTORY: both boxes answered, and the two answers do not add up to the line 8 they decompose. Neither answer can be preferred, because IRC 4973(a) prices each spouse's OWN accounts, so the return is refused rather than silently repaired.
WHY THE CELL IS NARROW. Line 36 has no effect at all unless line 34 is nonzero: the form face says "If zero, go to line 39". So a married Archer couple with distributions and no prior-year excess is completely unaffected and files.
WHY THERE IS NO PER-SPOUSE LINE 8 TO DERIVE. The question is whether the printed Form 8853 is itself per individual — whether a married couple prepares two STATEMENT Forms 8853 whose Part II line 8 each carries one spouse's own figure, in which case line 36 would simply take that figure and no allocation rule would be needed. IT DOES NOT. The 2025 instructions print their multiple-Form-8853 rules four times and every one of the four leaves lines 6a through 9b on the ONE controlling form; the fourth is the Section B beneficiary note at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8853.pdf, page 7 LEFT, per ACCOUNT like the third. (i) The Section A rule is PART I ONLY: "complete a separate Form 8853, Section A," / "Part I, for each spouse. Enter “statement” across the top of each Form 8853, fill in the name and SSN, and complete Part I. Next, add lines 1, 2, and 5 from the two statement Forms 8853 and enter those totals on the respective lines of the controlling Form 8853" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8853.pdf, page 3 LEFT continuing at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8853.pdf, page 3 RIGHT — the page's two columns interleave in the extraction). Lines 1, 2 and 5. Not 6a, not 6c, not 7, not 8. And it fires only in one narrow case, "c. If both spouses have HDHPs with self-only coverage" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8853.pdf, page 3, LEFT). (ii) The Section B rule names lines 10, 11, 12 and 13b (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8853.pdf, page 6, RIGHT). (iii) The beneficiary note is per ACCOUNT, not per spouse: "If, during the tax year, you are the beneficiary of two" / "or more Archer MSAs or you are a beneficiary of an" / "Archer MSA and you have your own Archer MSA, you" / "must complete a separate Form 8853 for each MSA" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8853.pdf, page 2, RIGHT) — several MSAs of ONE individual. THE PART II INSTRUCTION BLOCK CARRIES NO STATEMENT-FORM RULE AT ALL, and its Line 6a paragraph states the opposite affirmatively: "Enter the total distributions you and your spouse received" / "in 2025 from all Archer MSAs. These amounts should be" / "shown in box 1 of Form 1099-SA." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8853.pdf, page 5, RIGHT). So there is no per-spouse line 8 anywhere on the return, and the successor is an INTAKE rather than a derivation. The reading rests on the IRS's own Example 2, which requires the taxpayer to know the split for line 9b and never prints it; the IRC 4973(a)/(d)(2)(A) reading that makes the intake well-founded; a worked case on which the three candidate readings pay $60.00, $42.00 and $24.00; and two derivable narrowings deliberately NOT built because lines 36, 37 and 38 all carry Export mef="true".
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE on every return without an Archer MSA, because line 8 is a hard 0 there and both line 34s are complete-safe 0.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 line 41 is suppressed on this return
Fact.Description:
The two return-level states in which a printed line 41 would move Schedule 2 for a population this dictionary has not finished computing: the unresolvable line 36 allocation, and a Medicare Advantage MSA whose Section B is not built. Both states refuse the return, so suppressing the tax loses nothing that a filing return would have owed.
IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DERIVED FROM /flowKnockoutHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType. The guard reads /archerMsaForm8853FullyComputed, which reads line 41's completeness; reading the guard back here would close a resolution cycle. The two named states are the ones this suppression actually needs, and each is a fact the guard also reads independently.

Fact.Name: This filer's Form 8853 Part I and Form 5329 Part VI both resolve
Fact.Description:
The per-filer half of the SECOND narrowing predicate. It is the sibling ../archerMsaPartIComputedAndClean with the two Not(excess) conjuncts REMOVED and the Form 5329 line 41 completeness added in their place.
THE TWO CONJUNCTS ARE REMOVED BECAUSE THE EXCESSES ARE PRICED: the 6% excise (Form 5329 Part VI) and the Other-income leg are built, so an excess does not have to refuse.
THE SIBLING IS NOT REBODIED. ../archerMsaPartIComputedAndClean keeps its exact body and its exact meaning, and eight committed fixtures keep asserting it; the guard reads BOTH predicates in an Any, so nothing that files on the sibling can stop filing because of this one.
IsComplete FIRST, per the unanswered-collection rule, and line 41's own completeness carries the whole Part VI chain (lines 34 through 40) behind it.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 Section A Part II resolves on this return
Fact.Description:
Every printed Part II line — 6a, 6b, 6c, 7, 8, 9a and 9b — resolves for this return.
IsComplete ON LINE 9b IS NOT REDUNDANT WITH IsComplete ON LINE 8, and that is the one thing to check here: line 9b can be Incomplete while line 8 is Complete, on exactly the return that checked the line 9a exceptions box and did not say how much of line 8 the exception covers. Both conjuncts are stated because they fence different cells.
COMPLETE-SAFE TRUE on every return without an Archer MSA, where all seven lines are hard 0.

Fact.Name: THE SECOND NARROWING PREDICATE: everything this repo builds of Form 8853 resolves
Fact.Description:
Whether Form 8853 Section A — Part I AND Part II — plus the Form 5329 Part VI excise and the excess-employer Other-income leg all resolve for every filer on this return, and nothing it does not cover is present.
WHAT THIS FREES, stated as a cell rather than as a slogan. An Archer MSA holder who took DISTRIBUTIONS in 2025 files: the taxable part reaches Schedule 1 line 8e and the additional 20% tax reaches Schedule 2 line 17e. An Archer MSA holder who OVER-CONTRIBUTED files: the 6% excise reaches Schedule 2 line 8 through Form 5329 Part VI, and an excess EMPLOYER contribution additionally reaches Schedule 1 line 8z as Other income.
WHAT IT STILL REQUIRES, and each conjunct is a cell the residual names: a Medicare Advantage MSA only where its Section B resolves (/archerMsaSectionBResolvedOrAbsent), and a Form 5329 line 36 that can be attributed to a spouse.
THE PART I EXCESS CONJUNCTS ARE GONE AND THE OTHER PREDICATE IS UNTOUCHED. This fact does NOT supersede /archerMsaSectionAPartIFullyComputed; the guard reads the two in an Any, so the Part I population keeps filing on its own predicate whatever this one does.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE on every return without an Archer MSA, because /archerMsaOnThisReturn is, and it leads.

Fact.Name: The return has answered YES to holding a Medicare Advantage MSA
Fact.Description:
THE POPULATION GATE for the whole of Form 8853 Section B, and the fact every Section B leg below reads FIRST. COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: on a return that never reached the Archer/medical savings account interview - it resolves false rather than Incomplete, so no Section B intake is demanded and every Section B figure is a hard 0.
IT IS NOT Not(/archerMsaNoSectionBMedicareAdvantageMsa), AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT. That negation is TRUE on an unanswered return (the shipping fact is All(IsComplete, Not), so its negation is Any(not complete, answered yes)), which would put an unanswered return INSIDE the Section B population and demand line 10 of it. This fact is the positive answer only.
/archerMsaOnThisReturn LEADS because /writableHasMedicareAdvantageMsa is asked only inside the Archer branch of the interview; a return that never answered the medical-savings-account question cannot have answered this one either, and stating the dependency keeps the population gate honest if the screen is ever re-routed.

Fact.Name: Writable: did THIS filer receive Medicare Advantage MSA distributions in 2025?
Fact.Description:
The Section B filing trigger, asked of each spouse separately: "Complete Section B if you (or your spouse, if filing jointly) received distributions from a Medicare Advantage MSA in 2025. If both you and your spouse received distributions, complete a separate Form 8853, Section B, for each spouse."
WHY A SECOND QUESTION WHEN /writableHasMedicareAdvantageMsa ALREADY EXISTS. That one is return-level and asks whether the return HAS the vehicle; it cannot say which spouse received the distributions, and Section B is priced per spouse - each spouse has their own line 12, their own December 31 account value and their own annual deductible. Holding the account and taking a distribution are also different facts: a Medicare Advantage MSA holder with no 2025 distribution has no Section B at all.
REQUIRES THE ANSWER ON A SECTION B RETURN, deliberately. Once /medicareAdvantageMsaOnThisReturn is true, a filer who has not answered this leaves line 10 Incomplete and the return is refused. The alternative - treating silence as "no distributions" - would let an MFJ return whose second spouse was never asked file with that spouse's distributions untaxed, which is the direction this dictionary never takes on a missing amount. OFF the Section B population it is never read at all.
THE BENEFICIARY'S FAIR-MARKET-VALUE LEG IS INSIDE THIS ONE QUESTION rather than a second intake, for the same reason the Archer sibling /writableHasArcherMsaDistributions gives: the instructions route a beneficiary's FMV to the SAME printed lines ("On line 10, enter the fair market value of the Medicare Advantage MSA as of the date of death ... Complete the rest of Section B", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8853.pdf, page 7, LEFT column), so a return that must report it is a return with a line 10.

Fact.Name: This filer is known to have received no Medicare Advantage MSA distributions
Fact.Description: The answered-NO gate, complete-safe. All(IsComplete, Not) rather than a bare Not, so an unanswered question resolves this FALSE and leaves line 10 Incomplete rather than silently zeroing it - the same shape and the same reason as the shipping /archerMsaNoSectionAPartIiDistributions.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 line 10 — this filer's total Medicare Advantage MSA distributions
Fact.Description:
Form 8853 LINE 10: "Total distributions you received in 2025 from all Medicare Advantage MSAs (see instructions)".
"FROM ALL" IS THE STATUTE, NOT A SHORTCUT. IRC 138(c)(2)(C)(i) says "all Medicare Advantage MSAs of the account holder shall be treated as 1 account" and (c)(2)(C)(ii) says all the non-qualified payments in a year "shall be treated as 1 distribution", so one annual figure per account holder is the operative quantity even where the instructions ask a multi-account holder to prepare a separate statement Form 8853 for each account.
THREE EXCLUSIONS THE SCREEN OWES AND THIS DICTIONARY CANNOT DERIVE, carried here rather than silenced. The instructions say the figure "should be shown in box 1 of Form 1099-SA" (this dictionary has no Medicare Advantage 1099-SA collection) and that it "shouldn't include any erroneous contributions made by Medicare (or any earnings on the erroneous contributions) or any amounts from a trustee-to-trustee transfer from one Medicare Advantage MSA to another Medicare Advantage MSA of the same account holder" - both exclusions are IRC 138(c)(3) and 138(c)(4) respectively.
THE BENEFICIARY CASE ENTERS HERE TOO: after the account holder's death, a beneficiary who is not the surviving spouse enters the account's fair market value as of the date of death on this same line 10.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 10 — this filer's Medicare Advantage MSA distributions, fenced
Fact.Description:
The line 10 figure the rest of Section B reads. Hard 0 on every return without Medicare Advantage MSA distributions, the raw intake otherwise.
THE TWO HARD-0 ARMS ARE WHAT MAKE THIS FACT COMPLETE-SAFE, and the order matters, exactly as it does on the Archer line 6a sibling. The FIRST arm is Not(/medicareAdvantageMsaOnThisReturn), complete-safe FALSE on every return in the repo that never reached the interview - that is what holds every committed scenario at $0 on Schedule 1 line 8e and Schedule 2 line 17f. The SECOND is ../medicareAdvantageMsaFilerNoDistributions, the answered-NO gate, itself an All(IsComplete, Not) that never leaks an Incomplete - and it is what lets an MFJ return where only one spouse took distributions file.
THE THIRD ARM IS DELIBERATELY BARE. A filer who says they took distributions and does not say how much has an Incomplete line 10, an Incomplete line 12 and a refused return.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 line 11 — qualified medical expenses of the ACCOUNT HOLDER only
