Fact.Description:
Form 8853 LINE 11: "Unreimbursed qualified medical expenses (see instructions)".
THIS LINE IS NARROWER THAN ITS ARCHER TWIN AND THE STATUTE IS WHY. Archer line 7 reaches the expenses of the holder, the spouse and the dependents; here IRC 138(c)(1)(A) says "qualified medical expenses shall not include amounts paid for medical care for any individual other than the account holder", and the instructions follow it exactly - line 11 takes only distributions "used only for the account holder's qualified medical expenses". A screen that reuses the Archer wording here would over-shelter the distribution. That is a SCREEN-WORDING obligation.
THE Schedule A CAUTION IS THE SAME AS THE ARCHER LINE'S: "You can't take a deduction on Schedule A (Form 1040) or Schedule A (Form 1040-NR) for any amount you include on line 11." Nothing in this dictionary enforces it; it is screen wording and it is routed, not silenced.
THE BENEFICIARY CASE ENTERS HERE TOO, with its own printed definition: "for a beneficiary other than the estate, enter qualified medical expenses incurred by the account holder before the date of death that you paid within 1 year after the date of death."
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 WHEN UNANSWERED, which is the taxpayer-ADVERSE direction (the whole distribution becomes taxable). Fence on ../medicareAdvantageMsaForm8853Line11QualifiedMedicalExpenses.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 11 — this filer's qualified medical expenses, complete-safe 0
Fact.Description: The line 11 figure, 0 when nobody answered. The leading Not(/medicareAdvantageMsaOnThisReturn) arm is not decoration: without it the IsComplete arm below passes a PLACEHOLDER-backed writable through on a return with no Medicare Advantage MSA at all, which is what degraded the Archer Schedule 1 line 8e leg from Complete 0.00 to Placeholder 0.00 on the L2 strategies spike case. See the note on /archerMsaSchedule1Line8eTaxableDistributions.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 12 — this filer's taxable Medicare Advantage MSA distributions
Fact.Description:
FORM 8853 LINE 12: "Taxable Medicare Advantage MSA distributions. Subtract line 11 from line 10. If zero or less, enter -0-. Also include this amount in the total on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8e".
THE PRINTED FLOOR IS HERE AND ONLY HERE, and it is PER SPOUSE, which is not the same arithmetic as flooring the couple's combined figure: a spouse whose expenses exceed their distributions contributes 0, not a negative that would shelter the other spouse's taxable amount. That is what the printed "complete a separate Section B for each spouse" plus "add lines 10, 11, 12 ... from the two statement Forms 8853" means, taken literally.
Cents are preserved; the single Round on this chain happens on the Schedule 1 line 9 total, which is where i1040gi puts it.
THE DESTINATION IS SHARED WITH FORM 8853 LINE 8 AND THAT IS PRINTED, NOT INFERRED. Both the Archer taxable distribution (line 8) and this one say "Also include this amount in the total on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8e", so the Schedule 1 leg ADDS to the Archer leg and never replaces it.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 line 13a — some line 12 distributions meet an exception to the 50% tax
Fact.Description:
Form 8853 LINE 13a: "If any of the distributions included on line 12 meet any of the Exceptions to the Additional 50% Tax (see instructions), check here".
THE EXCEPTIONS ARE TWO, NOT THREE, AND THE DIFFERENCE FROM THE ARCHER CHECKBOX IS STATUTORY. IRC 138(c)(2)(B) excepts a payment or distribution "made on or after the date the account holder ... becomes disabled within the meaning of section 72(m)(7), or ... dies" - and there is NO age-65 exception, which IRC 220(f)(4)(B) does give the Archer 20% tax. A screen that reuses the Archer wording here would except distributions the statute taxes.
THE PRINTED DATE BOUNDARY ALSO DIFFERS AND IT IS QUOTED RATHER THAN PARAPHRASED: the Archer instruction excepts distributions "made after the date" of the event, the Medicare Advantage one "made on or after the date". Neither is derivable here - both are per-distribution and per-date, and line 10 is one annual total - which is why this is a checkbox and why line 13b needs its own amount.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE WHEN UNANSWERED, the taxpayer-ADVERSE direction (the whole of line 12 enters the 50% base). Fence on ../medicareAdvantageMsaForm8853Line13aExceptionChecked.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 13a — the exceptions checkbox, complete-safe false
Fact.Description: The line 13a checkbox, false when nobody answered. False is the ADVERSE reading: it sends the whole of line 12 into the 50% tax base.

Fact.Name: Writable: the part of Form 8853 line 12 that does NOT meet a 50%-tax exception
Fact.Description:
Asked only when line 13a is checked. The printed Additional 50% Tax Worksheet line 1 defines it: "Enter the total distributions included on Form 8853, line 12, that don't meet either of the exceptions to the additional 50% tax."
WHY IT IS ASKED RATHER THAN DERIVED, the same answer the Archer sibling /writableArcherMsaDistributionsSubjectTo20PctTax gives: the split is per distribution and per date (the date disability began, the date of death), and line 10 is one annual total. There is nothing in the graph to split.
INCOMPLETE WHEN LINE 13a IS CHECKED AND THIS IS BLANK, deliberately, and the instructions leave the taxpayer a way to say "all of it": "if either of the exceptions applies to all the distributions included on line 12, enter -0- on line 13b" - which on this design is answering this intake 0, not leaving it blank. 0 by default would except the whole distribution on the strength of a checkbox; line 12 by default would make the checkbox meaningless.

Fact.Name: Additional 50% Tax Worksheet LINE 1 — the line 12 amount that meets no exception
Fact.Description:
The base of the whole worksheet: the whole of line 12 when no exception is claimed, and the claimed unexcepted part when line 13a is checked.
THE LesserOf IS A FENCE, NOT ARITHMETIC, and the argument is the Archer sibling's: the taxed part is by definition "included on Form 8853, line 12", so it can never exceed line 12; capping it here means a wrong answer over-states nobody and cannot manufacture a tax on a distribution the return never reported. It does NOT rescue an under-stated answer, which only the screen can police.
THE THIRD ARM IS WHAT KEEPS THE CHAIN COMPLETE-SAFE, and the Archer twin measured why: on a return with no distributions, LesserOf(blank writable, hard-0 line 12) is still Incomplete, so the no-exception arm must come FIRST and must be reachable. It is - line 13a is complete-safe false.

Fact.Name: Writable: worksheet step 2 — did this filer have a Medicare Advantage MSA on December 31, 2024?
Fact.Description:
The printed Additional 50% Tax Worksheet step 2 asks it in exactly these words: "Did you have a Medicare Advantage MSA on December 31, 2024?" - "No. STOP Enter one-half of line 1 above on Form 8853, line 13b." / "Yes. Enter the value of your Medicare Advantage MSA on December 31, 2024".
WHY IT IS A SEPARATE QUESTION FROM THE VALUE. The No branch never asks for a value at all, and an account opened during 2025 has no December 31, 2024 value to give; a single Dollar intake would make "no account" and "an account worth zero" indistinguishable, and they take different printed branches.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE WHEN UNANSWERED, and false is provably the ADVERSE branch: the No branch taxes one-half of worksheet line 1, the Yes branch taxes one-half of line 1 less a subtraction that is never negative, so the Yes branch can only ever be smaller or equal. A filer who really did hold an account on December 31, 2024 and does not say so over-pays; that is a SCREEN-REACH question and it is routed rather than silenced.

Fact.Name: Worksheet step 2 — the December 31, 2024 account answer, complete-safe false
Fact.Description: The worksheet's branch selector, false when nobody answered. False takes the printed No branch, which is the larger tax.

Fact.Name: Writable: worksheet line 2 — the value of the Medicare Advantage MSA on December 31, 2024
Fact.Description:
Asked only in the yes branch of worksheet step 2. The printed cell reads "Yes. Enter the value of your Medicare Advantage MSA on December 31, 2024", and IRC 138(c)(2)(A)(ii)(I) says what "value" means: "the fair market value of the assets in such MSA as of the close of the calendar year preceding the calendar year in which the taxable year begins".
THE FIGURE IS REPORTED TO THE ACCOUNT HOLDER AND THE SCREEN SHOULD SAY SO. IRC 138(e)(1) makes the trustee's section 220(h) report "include the fair market value of the assets in such Medicare Advantage MSA as of the close of each calendar year", furnished by January 31; this dictionary has no Form 5498-SA collection, so the figure is asked rather than harvested. That is a SCREEN-WORDING obligation.
INCOMPLETE WHEN THE YES BRANCH IS TAKEN AND THIS IS BLANK, deliberately: a 0 default would make the Yes branch identical to the No branch and silently discard the taxpayer's answer, and nothing in the graph can supply the value.

Fact.Name: Additional 50% Tax Worksheet LINE 2 — the December 31, 2024 account value, fenced
Fact.Description:
The worksheet line 2 figure. 0 in the No branch, the raw intake in the Yes branch.
0 IN THE NO BRANCH REPRODUCES THE PRINTED "STOP" EXACTLY, which is why this worksheet needs no second computation path. With line 2 at 0, worksheet line 5 is GreaterOf(0, 0 - line 4) = 0 whatever line 3 says, line 6 is line 1 less 0 = line 1, and line 7 is one-half of line 1 - which is verbatim what the No cell instructs ("No. STOP Enter one-half of line 1 above on Form 8853, line 13b."). The identity is arithmetic, not an approximation.
THE YES ARM IS BARE. A filer who answers Yes and gives no value has an Incomplete line 2, an Incomplete line 13b and a refused return.

Fact.Name: Writable: worksheet line 3 — the HDHP annual deductible on January 1, 2025
Fact.Description:
Asked only in the yes branch of worksheet step 2. The printed cell reads "Enter the amount of the annual deductible for your HDHP policy on January 1, 2025", and the statute says the same thing from the plan's side: "the deductible under the Medicare Advantage MSA plan covering the account holder as of January 1 of the calendar year in which the taxable year begins".
IT IS NOT THE ARCHER LINE 3 DEDUCTIBLE AND MUST NOT BE PREFILLED FROM IT. The Archer Line 3 Limitation Chart reads the deductible of the ARCHER high deductible health plan, month by month; this reads the deductible of the MEDICARE ADVANTAGE MSA plan on one printed date. A filer can hold both, and IRC 138(b)(4) makes the Medicare Advantage plan a different plan ("established in connection with an MSA plan described in section 1859(b)(3) of the Social Security Act"). That is a SCREEN-WORDING obligation.
INCOMPLETE WHEN THE YES BRANCH IS TAKEN AND THIS IS BLANK, deliberately, and the direction is what settles it: a 0 default makes worksheet line 4 zero, so line 5 absorbs the WHOLE December 31 value and the tax comes out SMALLER than the printed worksheet gives. A taxpayer-favourable default on an unanswered question is the one this dictionary refuses.

Fact.Name: Additional 50% Tax Worksheet LINE 3 — the January 1, 2025 annual deductible, fenced
Fact.Description: The worksheet line 3 figure. 0 wherever line 2 is 0 - the No branch never reaches line 3 and its value cannot change the answer there, because line 5 is already floored at 0 - and the raw intake in the Yes branch, bare, so a Yes with no deductible refuses.

Fact.Name: Additional 50% Tax Worksheet LINE 4 — 60% of the annual deductible
Fact.Description: WORKSHEET LINE 4: "Multiply line 3 by 60% (0.60)". The statute prints the same figure as "an amount equal to 60 percent of the deductible". Cents are preserved; the single Round on this chain is on line 13b, the printed line that reaches Schedule 2.

Fact.Name: Additional 50% Tax Worksheet LINE 5 — the December 31 value above the 60% floor
Fact.Description:
WORKSHEET LINE 5: "Subtract line 4 from line 2. If zero or less, enter -0-". The statute is the inner excess of 138(c)(2)(A)(ii): the excess of the prior-year-close fair market value over 60 percent of the January 1 deductible.
THE PRINTED FLOOR IS HERE BECAUSE THE PRINTED LINE CARRIES IT, and the statute agrees - both excesses in 138(c)(2)(A) are "the excess (if any) of", which is a floor at zero.

Fact.Name: Additional 50% Tax Worksheet LINE 6 — the distribution above the minimum balance
Fact.Description:
WORKSHEET LINE 6: "Subtract line 5 from line 1. If zero or less, enter -0-". This is the outer excess of IRC 138(c)(2)(A) and it is the whole of what the 50% tax is charged on: the excess of the unexcepted distribution over the account's own minimum-balance headroom.
WHAT THE SUBTRACTION IS FOR, stated because the shape is otherwise opaque: the penalty exists to keep a minimum balance in the account, so a distribution is forgiven to the extent the account was above 60% of the plan deductible at the start of the year. That is why the heading of 138(c)(2) reads "Penalty for distributions from Medicare Advantage MSA not used for qualified medical expenses if minimum balance not maintained".

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 13b — this filer's additional 50% tax (Schedule 2 line 17f)
Fact.Description:
FORM 8853 LINE 13b: "Additional 50% tax. Enter 50% (0.50) of the distributions included on line 12 that are subject to the additional 50% tax. See instructions for the amount to enter if you had a Medicare Advantage MSA at the end of 2024. Also include this amount in the total on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 17f", computed through worksheet line 7 ("Enter one-half of line 6 here and on Form 8853, line 13b").
ROUNDED HERE AND PER FILER, because line 13b is a printed line of a per-spouse statement Form 8853 and the controlling form adds the two rounded figures - which is what "add lines 10, 11, 12, and 13b from the two statement Forms 8853" says to do. The same placement, for the same reason, as the per-filer Form 5329 line 41 sibling.
LINE 17f, NOT 17e AND NOT 17c, AND THE STATUTE IS THE REASON RATHER THAN THE FORM ALONE. IRC 138(c)(2)(A)'s flush text says "Section 220(f)(4) shall not apply to any payment or distribution from a Medicare Advantage MSA" - the Archer 20% tax is switched OFF for this vehicle and the 50% tax replaces it, so routing this to 17e would not merely double-book a printed line, it would charge a tax the statute disapplies.

Fact.Name: This filer's Form 8853 Section B resolves
Fact.Description:
Every printed Section B line this repo builds - 10, 11, 12, 13a and 13b - resolves for this filer.
IsComplete ON LINE 13b IS NOT REDUNDANT WITH IsComplete ON LINE 12, the same non-redundancy the Archer /archerMsaPartIiComputedAndClean records: line 13b can be Incomplete while line 12 is Complete, on the filer who checked line 13a without an amount, and on the filer who answered the December 31, 2024 question Yes without a value or without a deductible. Three different cells, one conjunct.
COMPLETE-SAFE TRUE on every return without a Medicare Advantage MSA, where all five lines are hard 0 or hard false.

Fact.Name: Controlling Form 8853 LINE 10 — both spouses' Medicare Advantage MSA distributions
Fact.Description: Line 10 of the controlling Form 8853: the two statement forms' line 10 figures added. On a single or separate return it is the primary filer's own line 10 alone.

Fact.Name: Controlling Form 8853 LINE 11 — both spouses' qualified medical expenses
Fact.Description: Line 11 of the controlling Form 8853, the two statement forms' line 11 figures added. It carries no downstream leg of its own; it exists because the instructions name it as one of the four lines the controlling form combines, and a printed line that is computed is a printed line that can be checked.

Fact.Name: Controlling Form 8853 LINE 12 — both spouses' taxable Medicare Advantage MSA distributions
Fact.Description:
Line 12 of the controlling Form 8853, and the figure that reaches Schedule 1 line 8e.
THE ADDITION HAPPENS AFTER THE PER-SPOUSE FLOOR, NOT BEFORE, and that is the printed order: each statement Form 8853 carries its own "If zero or less, enter -0-" on line 12, and only then are the two line 12 figures added. Flooring the combined figure instead would let one spouse's excess medical expenses shelter the other spouse's taxable distribution, which no printed line authorises.

Fact.Name: Controlling Form 8853 LINE 13b — both spouses' additional 50% tax
Fact.Description: Line 13b of the controlling Form 8853, and the figure that reaches Schedule 2 line 17f. Each spouse's line 13b is rounded on their own statement form before the two are added, which is the same per-individual rounding the Form 5329 siblings use.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 LINE 8e — the Medicare Advantage MSA leg
Fact.Description:
The controlling Form 8853 line 12 amount as an addend of Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 9, BESIDE the Archer line 8 leg and never in place of it. Schedule 1 line 8e is printed "Income from Form 8853" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s1.pdf, page 1) - ONE line for the WHOLE form, which is why both Form 8853 line 8 and Form 8853 line 12 say "Also include this amount in the total on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8e" and why this is an addend rather than a selection.
THE LEADING POPULATION ARM IS THE COMPLETE-SAFETY ARGUMENT, not a convenience: /medicareAdvantageMsaOnThisReturn is complete-safe false on every committed scenario, so this addend is a Complete $0 there and /schedule1TotalOtherIncome is byte-identical. Without it the IsComplete arm would pass a placeholder-backed input through on a return with no Medicare Advantage MSA at all, which is exactly what degraded the Archer sibling to Placeholder 0.00 on the L2 strategies spike case.
THE IsComplete FENCE IS PROVABLY LOSSLESS on a filing return. Line 12 is Incomplete only when a filer said they took distributions and did not say how much, and such a return fails /medicareAdvantageMsaSectionBFullyComputed, so /flowKnockoutHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType is true and the return does not file.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 LINE 17f — the additional 50% Medicare Advantage MSA distribution tax
Fact.Description:
The controlling Form 8853 line 13b amount as an addend of taxCalculations:/line21OfSchedule2, reaching it through the printed Schedule 2 line 18 exactly as the 17c, 17d and 17e legs do.
LINE 17f IS ITS OWN PRINTED LINE and this leg is the only thing in the dictionary that reaches it: 17c is the Form 8889 line 17b HSA 20% tax, 17d the Form 8889 line 21 testing-period 10% tax, 17e the Form 8853 line 9b ARCHER 20% tax. There is no double-book, and IRC 138(c)(2)(A)'s flush text is the reason the Archer 20% leg can never carry a Medicare Advantage distribution: "Section 220(f)(4) shall not apply to any payment or distribution from a Medicare Advantage MSA."
Same two fences, same two arguments, as the Schedule 1 line 8e sibling above.

Fact.Name: THE THIRD NARROWING PREDICATE: Form 8853 Section B resolves for every filer on this return
Fact.Description:
Whether this return HAS a Medicare Advantage MSA and every printed Section B line resolves for every filer who could carry one.
WHAT THIS FREES. A Medicare Advantage MSA holder who took distributions in 2025 files: the taxable part reaches Schedule 1 line 8e beside any Archer amount, and the additional 50% tax reaches Schedule 2 line 17f through the printed Additional 50% Tax Worksheet. On a return whose Section B does not resolve, /archerMsaForm5329PartViSuppressed holds the Archer 6% excise at $0 so that a refused filing cannot move Schedule 2.
IT IS FALSE, NOT TRUE, ON A RETURN WITH NO MEDICARE ADVANTAGE MSA, because /medicareAdvantageMsaOnThisReturn leads. That is deliberate and it is why this predicate is combined with the shipping /archerMsaNoSectionBMedicareAdvantageMsa in an Any at /archerMsaSectionBResolvedOrAbsent rather than replacing it: "no Section B" and "a Section B that resolves" are two different states and both must satisfy the Archer predicates.
THE PRIMARY READ IS FENCED WITH IsComplete, and the secondary is gated on filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ, for the reason measured on the L2 strategies spike: a return with no /filers item at all must not turn a return-level Boolean non-complete.

Fact.Name: This return's Section B is either absent or fully computed
Fact.Description:
THE SECTION B OPERAND of the two Archer narrowing predicates and of /archerMsaForm5329PartViSuppressed: an Any over /archerMsaNoSectionBMedicareAdvantageMsa and /medicareAdvantageMsaSectionBFullyComputed.
IT IS AN Any, SO IT IS WIDER THAN EITHER DISJUNCT ALONE. A disjunct can only make the predicates truer and the suppression falser, and the Form 5329 Part VI hold lifts for exactly the filers whose Section B resolves and no wider: a return whose Section B does NOT resolve still has /medicareAdvantageMsaSectionBFullyComputed false, still fails /archerMsaSectionBResolvedOrAbsent, and is still both refused and suppressed.
COMPLETE-SAFE TRUE on a return with no Medicare Advantage MSA (the first disjunct is), and complete-safe FALSE on a return that has one and has not answered Section B (both disjuncts are).

Fact.Name: Married to each other on the first day of every month of the tax year
Fact.Description: Whether all twelve /hsaMarriedOnFirstDayMonthNN are true. THIS IS THE CONDITION THE IRC 223(b)(5)(B) EQUAL DIVISION NEEDS BESIDE "treated as having family coverage for each month". The Line 6 first bullet halves line 5 for a couple treated as having family coverage every month; the statute divides only what it first SHARED, and it shares only "in the case of individuals who are married to each other". A couple who married mid-year and held family coverage all twelve months satisfies the printed bullet and NOT the statute's own condition for the months before the marriage, and halving their whole line 5 understates each spouse's limitation. They belong in the four steps, whose Step 1 month set is already (family AND married). On a return that has not answered the marital vector each row falls back to the year-end filers:/isMarried.

It is the gate /flowKnockoutMaritalChangeAffectsContributionLimit now narrows on: a filer who attests that a marital change affected their contribution limit is still refused until all twelve rows are answered.

Fact.Name: Every month of the MFS spouse's coverage vector has an answer
Fact.Description: True only when all twelve of the non-filing spouse's coverage rows have been answered. This is what makes /hsaLine3VectorGoverns' married branch satisfiable on a separate return, and it is therefore what narrows /flowKnockoutMFSLine6Check.

Fact.Name: On a separate return, the spouse has an HSA of their own
Fact.Description: The MFS analogue of /bothFilersHaveHsa. /bothFilersHaveHsa counts members of /filersWithHsaContributions and is FALSE on every separate return by construction, because the spouse is not a filer there; but the Form 8889 Line 6 instruction opens on "Spouses who have separate HSAs", and on an MFS return the fact that answers that question is the primary filer's own ../mfsLine6Check attestation - "whether a Health Savings Account (HSA) had contributions for the tax year" for the spouse. Without this fact an MFS couple freed by the spouse-coverage intake would fall through to the UNDIVIDED line 5 and both spouses would carry the whole shared family limitation, which is the error /flowKnockoutMFSLine6Check exists to prevent.

Fact.Name: Line 6 Step 1 — the worksheet amounts for the shared family months only
Fact.Description: The total of the Line 3 Limitation Chart month lines, counting ONLY the months in which this filer was treated as having family coverage AND was married to the other spouse on the first day of the month. Step 1 says to refigure line 5 "if you had entered on line 3 the total of the worksheet amounts only for the months you were treated as having family coverage", so this is that restricted total; the worksheet's own divide-by-12 is applied to it at ../hsaLine6Step1RefiguredLine3.

Fact.Name: Line 6 Step 1 — the worksheet amounts for the months Step 1 counts, DEEMED year included
Fact.Description:
The number Step 1 refigures line 3 from: "the total of the worksheet amounts only for the months you were treated as having family coverage", intersected with the months of the marriage because IRC 223(b)(5) shares a limitation only between "individuals who are married to each other". Outside one population it is ../hsaLine6SharedFamilyMonthsChartTotal. It diverges on ONE population, the one ../hsaLine6DeemedFamilyYearGoverns names: a married filer whose line 3 came from the last-month rule with a family December and who was not married every month. There the months the filer was "treated as having family coverage" are not the chart's — the Line 3 narrative rule 2 treats them as holding December's family plan for the entire year — so Step 1's total is December's chart amount counted once for each month of the marriage.
WHY A SEPARATE FACT AND NOT A WIDENING OF ../hsaLine6SharedFamilyMonthsChartTotal. The same separation, for the same reason, that put ../hsaLine6TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth beside ../hsaLine3TreatedAsFamilyEveryMonth and ../hsaLine6EqualDivisionHalfShare beside ../hsaLine3EqualDivisionHalfShare: the chart's literal twelve-month vector is still asked for elsewhere and is asserted at that meaning by committed node tests, so the deeming is composed beside it rather than folded into it. ../hsaLine6SharedFamilyMonthsChartTotal keeps its meaning and every pinned row it carries; what differs is which total Step 1 divides.
THE DEEMED MONTHS ARE ALL TWELVE AND THEY ALL CARRY DECEMBER'S AMOUNT, which is why the deemed arm needs no coverage test per month — it is the same identity ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleAmount is built on ("every one of the twelve chart rows would then carry December's amount"). The only per-month question left is the marital one, and that is the whole of the month-keying: months inside the marriage are shared and divided under 223(b)(5)(B); months outside it were nobody else's and are left whole by ../hsaLine6ChartTotalAllMonths less this total, at Step 4.
COMPLETE-SAFE. The gate is complete-safe false, so an unanswered return takes the else arm and this fact is ../hsaLine6SharedFamilyMonthsChartTotal, which is a hard $0 on a return that never answered the monthly vector.

Fact.Name: The whole-year chart total the Line 6 steps decompose, DEEMED year included
Fact.Description:
The twelve-month total Step 4 takes its remainder out of. Outside the deemed year it is ../hsaLine3ChartTotalAllMonths — the chart's own "Total for all months". On the deemed year ../hsaLine6DeemedFamilyYearGoverns names, it is December's chart amount counted twelve times, which is the same identity ../hsaLine3LastMonthRuleAmount rests on and is exactly twelve times that filer's line 3.
WHY STEP 4 NEEDS IT. Step 4's "any other contribution limits that apply for the tax year" are read by this dictionary as the months Step 1 excluded, and for a deemed filer those months are deemed too: their limitation for January is December's plan, not the nothing the chart records. Reading the chart total here would subtract a shared total built out of deemed months from a whole-year total built out of real ones, and the two halves would not sum to the filer's line 3. With this fact they do: (this total less ../hsaLine6Step1MonthSetChartTotal) / 12 plus that total / 12 is the filer's own line 3, which is the property the four steps need in order to decompose it at all.
COMPLETE-SAFE. The gate is complete-safe false, so an unanswered return takes the else arm and this fact is ../hsaLine3ChartTotalAllMonths, a hard $0 there.

Fact.Name: Line 6 Step 1 — the refigured line 3
Fact.Description: The shared-family-month total divided by 12, i.e. what line 3 would have been had the worksheet counted only those months. CENTS ARE KEPT, exactly as ../hsaLine3WorksheetLimitation keeps them: the worksheet prints no rounding instruction. THE LAST-MONTH RULE IS NOT APPLIED HERE: Step 1 names the number it wants ("the total of the worksheet amounts"), so it displaces the rule-4 greater-of, and a filer whose real line 3 came from IRC 223(b)(8)(A) instead of the worksheet cannot be decomposed this way at all.

Fact.Name: Line 6 Step 1 — the refigured line 5
Fact.Description: The refigured line 3 less line 4, floored at zero, which is line 5's own printed arithmetic. Step 1 is explicit that the Archer reduction is not refigured with it: "When refiguring line 5, use the same amount you previously entered on line 4." NOTE the consequence, named rather than left to be found: because the whole of line 4 is subtracted inside the halved part, the Archer reduction is effectively halved for this population. That is what the printed step says to do. It is inert on every committed return, since ../hsaLine4ArcherMsaContributions is complete-safe 0 without an Archer MSA.

Fact.Name: Line 6 Step 2 — the spouse's half of the refigured limit
Fact.Description: Step 2 divides the Step 1 amount equally between the spouses, unless they agree on a different allocation. When this filer states an agreed share (../writableHsaAgreedFamilyLimitShare), the spouse's part is the Step 1 amount less that share, capped so neither part is negative; otherwise it is half.

Fact.Name: Line 6 Step 3 — Step 1 less the spouse's share
Fact.Description: Step 3 subtracts "the part of the contribution limit allocated to your spouse in Step 2 from the amount determined in Step 1". It is written as the printed subtraction rather than as a second halving so that a Step 1 amount with an odd half-cent lands wholly on this filer instead of being rounded twice.

Fact.Name: Line 6 Step 4 — the other contribution limits that apply for the tax year
Fact.Description:
Step 4 says to "determine any other contribution limits that apply for the tax year and add that amount to the result in Step 3". THE READING, argued because the step names no figure: the months Step 1 excluded are the months whose limitation is this filer's alone - nobody else's coverage put a limit on them - so the "other contribution limits" are the worksheet amounts for exactly those months, divided by 12 like every other worksheet total. The arithmetic check is that the two spouses' line 6 amounts then sum to the couple's true combined limitation: for six family months and six self-only months each, 2 x ($51,300/12/2) = $4,275, which is the six-month family limitation, plus each spouse's own $2,150 of self-only months. NO IRS EXAMPLE WORKS THESE STEPS NUMERICALLY - the instruction prints them as prose and Publication 969's married examples are all first-bullet cases - so every figure pinned here is derived from the printed chart amounts by this dictionary and is labelled ai-only.
BOTH OPERANDS ARE THE LINE 6 TWINS, ../hsaLine6ChartTotalAllMonths and ../hsaLine6Step1MonthSetChartTotal, each of which equals the chart fact it stands beside everywhere except on the deemed year ../hsaLine6DeemedFamilyYearGoverns names. The reason is that the reading itself - "the months Step 1 excluded" - is a statement about the SAME twelve months Step 1 counted from, and on a deemed year those are December's plan repeated, not the chart's rows. Mixing the two would leave Step 3 plus Step 4 summing to something other than the filer's own line 3, which is the arithmetic check this paragraph sets for itself. On the deemed cell the check passes at cents: six deemed months inside a mid-year marriage give each spouse $2,137.50 of a shared $4,275.00 plus $4,275.00 of their own six unmarried months, and the couple's $12,825.00 is one shared six-month family limitation plus two unshared ones.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 LINE 6 under the second bullet — Step 3 plus Step 4
Fact.Description: "Enter the total on line 6." THE LANDING FACT OF ARM (b) of the kind="rebody" contract at /flowKnockoutHsaCoverage. NOT ROUNDED, matching its first-bullet sibling ../hsaLine6EqualDivisionHalfShare and the cents-keeping worksheet above it; the legacy line 6 arms round, and that pre-existing split of the two paths is recorded rather than changed here. THE AGE-55 ADDITIONAL AMOUNT IS NOT INSIDE ANY OF THESE FIGURES and needs no exclusion conjunct: ../hsaLine3AdditionalContributionIncluded is FALSE for every filer this fact serves, because that fact already excludes a married filer who had family coverage at any time during the year, which is exactly this population. That is IRC 223(b)(5)(B)'s "without regard to any additional contribution amount under paragraph (3)" satisfied structurally.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 CONTROLLING FORM, LINE 3, the return's limitation
Fact.Description: The amount printed on line 3 of the Form 8853 this return files: "Limitation from the Line 3 Limitation Chart and Worksheet in the instructions". It is the third member of the /archerMsaControllingForm8853Line1Total and /archerMsaControllingForm8853Line2Total family and is built in the same shape, one fenced primary read added to a spouse read that only a joint return reaches. THE Add IS AN ARITHMETIC IDENTITY, NOT A PRINTED RULE. Where either spouse has Archer family coverage, IRC 220(b)(3)(B) divides one limitation equally between them and the twelve chart facts already carry each half at 37.5 percent of the governing deductible, so the two halves add back to the one shared limitation a single Part I would print. On a single or separate return the sum is the primary filer's own limitation and nothing else. PRINT ONLY IN THE CASE (2)(c) SHAPE UNTIL THE OBLIGATION IS MET: when /archerMsaSeparatePartIForEachSpouse is true the instructions say "Don't complete lines 3 and 4 of the controlling Form 8853" because the two limitations belong on the two statement forms, and this repo renders the controlling form only. Until a render gate suppresses the line in that case this total prints there, which is the debt the obligation records.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 3, the primary filer's limitation fenced to 0
Fact.Description: The primary filer's Form 8853 line 3 limitation, or $0 when that filer path does not resolve. It is the first operand of the controlling form's line 3 total and it exists for the same reason the shipping /archerMsaControllingForm8853Line1Total wraps its own primary read in an IsComplete Switch: the fence can only fire on a filer path that does not exist, where $0 is the right contribution, because /filers/*/archerMsaForm8853Line3Limitation is a hard 0 on every return that never reached the Archer interview. Cents survive, because the single Round in the Form 8853 chain stays at /archerMsaForm8853Line5DeductionTotal.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 3, the secondary filer's limitation fenced to 0
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's Form 8853 line 3 limitation, or $0 when there is no secondary filer. The IsComplete test comes first because the unanswered collection trap is what a bare /secondaryFiler read walks into: on a single, head of household or qualifying surviving spouse return the path does not resolve, and an Incomplete operand would make the whole controlling total Incomplete rather than the primary filer's own limitation. This fact says nothing about whether the spouse's limitation belongs on the controlling form; that is the filing status question its sibling /archerMsaSecondaryFilerForm8853Line3LimitationWhenJoint answers.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 3, the spouse's limitation only on a joint return
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's fenced line 3 limitation on a joint return, and $0 on every other filing status. MFJ, NOT MARRIED, and the divergence is deliberate for the reason /archerMsaForm8853Line5DeductionTotal already gives: on a married filing separately return each spouse files their own 1040 with their own controlling Form 8853, and their line 3 limitations are already the halved shares the Line 3 Limitation Chart prints under Married filing separately. Adding the spouse's share here would put both halves of one shared limitation on one separate return.

Fact.Name: Form 8889 line 18 - this filer's last-month-rule testing-period income
Fact.Description:
Form 8889 Part III line 18 (Last-month rule) for this filer: the gross income increase IRC 223(b)(8)(B)(i)(I) imposes when the last-month rule raised the contribution limit and the individual then failed to be an eligible individual during the testing period.
COMPUTED (for /flowKnockoutHsaTestingPeriodAdditionalIncomeYes): the value is the ATTESTED ../writableHsaLastMonthRuleExcessContributions - the excess of the prior-year contributions over the prior-year limitation redetermined without the last-month rule, which the Line 18 instructions put on the taxpayer to determine - zeroed where ../hsaTestingPeriodExceptionAttested (the 223(b)(8)(B)(ii) death-or-disability ground, which disapplies the inclusion AND the 10% tax). The refusal is only for the filer in the testing-period flow whose intake group is unanswered (../hsaTestingPeriodPriorYearIntakeMissing). THE WRITABLE WINS where answered, whatever the screening yes/no said, on ../writableHsaTestingPeriodFirstIneligibleMonth's precedent. $0 and Complete where the intake is unanswered - the missing answer is reported by the knockout, not by contagion.
CONSUMED: ../form8889Line20TestingPeriodIncome is the printed line 20, "Add lines 18 and 19", and it adds this leaf; /hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncomeAndAdditionalTax sums that per filer line 20 across /filers, and ../hsaTestingPeriodFailureAdditionalTax takes 10% of the same line 20.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 20, qualified LTC payments plus accelerated death benefits
Fact.Description: FORM 8853 LINE 20: "Add lines 18 and 19". The gross figure whose taxable part lines 21 through 26 carve out, and the minuend of line 26. It adds line 18 rather than line 17 because line 17's non qualified remainder is routed off this form by the printed Caution.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 23, the larger of the per diem figure or actual costs
Fact.Description: FORM 8853 LINE 23: "Enter the larger of line 21 or line 22". The statute lets the recipient of periodic payments keep the greater of the indexed per diem allowance and the costs actually incurred, so the printed instruction is a GreaterOf and not a cap in either direction.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 25, the per diem limitation
Fact.Description: FORM 8853 LINE 25: "Per diem limitation. Subtract line 24 from line 23". The exclusion ceiling for the year: the greater of the indexed allowance and actual costs, reduced by what insurance or any other source already reimbursed, so the same care is not excluded twice. The declared nonnegative line-24 reimbursement is floored at $0 before this subtraction; line 25 itself remains an unfloored difference because reimbursements can exceed the line-23 exclusion amount, and the form's only printed floor is on line 26.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 26, taxable long term care payments
Fact.Description: FORM 8853 LINE 26: "Taxable payments. Subtract line 25 from line 20. If zero or less, enter -0-. Also include this amount in the total on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8e". The one figure Section C sends off the form, and the excess of the per diem and accelerated death benefit stream over the limitation the statute allows to be excluded. CONSUMED: income:/schedule1Line8eForm8853LtcPaymentsOrZero is the complete safe wrapper of this fact (this one is not complete safe - the subtraction under its printed floor reads Section C intakes an ordinary return never answers), income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome adds that wrapper as the THIRD leg of Schedule 1 line 8e beside the Archer line 8 and Medicare Advantage line 12 legs, and /schedule1Line8eForm8853Income, the printed line 8e cell, adds the same wrapper so the cell and the total foot to one number.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 26 before its floor, line 20 less line 25
Fact.Description: The raw subtraction behind line 26, "Subtract line 25 from line 20", kept as its own fact so the printed floor is a separate and visible step. It is NOT the printed cell and carries no mapping: line 26 says "If zero or less, enter -0-", and a payment stream inside its per diem limitation makes this difference negative.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 LINE 26, the printed zero floor
Fact.Description: The $0 that line 26 prints when the subtraction is zero or less: "If zero or less, enter -0-". A named literal so the floor is a GreaterOf against something a reader can point at rather than an unexplained constant, which is the idiom /form8606ZeroDollarFloor already uses.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 CONTROLLING FORM, LINE 13a, the exceptions checkbox
Fact.Description: The line 13a checkbox printed on the Form 8853 this return files: "If any of the distributions included on line 12 meet any of the Exceptions to the Additional 50% Tax (see instructions), check here". It is the Section B counterpart of the shipping return level line 9a checkbox /archerMsaForm8853Line9aExceptionChecked, and it is an Any rather than an Add because a checkbox combines by disjunction: line 12 of the controlling form is both spouses' taxable distributions, so an exception claimed by either spouse is an exception claimed against a distribution included on the printed line 12. Complete safe false throughout, which is the adverse direction.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 13a, the primary filer's checkbox fenced to false
Fact.Description: The primary filer's line 13a checkbox, false when that filer path does not resolve. False is the ADVERSE reading and it is the reading /filers/*/medicareAdvantageMsaForm8853Line13aExceptionChecked already takes for an unanswered filer: it sends the whole of line 12 into the 50 percent tax base. The fence exists so the controlling checkbox is complete safe rather than Incomplete on a graph whose filers collection is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 13a, the secondary filer's checkbox fenced to false
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's line 13a checkbox, false when there is no secondary filer. The IsComplete test comes first for the same unanswered collection reason the Section A siblings give: an Incomplete member of an Any makes the whole aggregate Incomplete rather than false, and a checkbox that cannot resolve would take the controlling Form 8853 with it.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 13a, the spouse's checkbox only on a joint return
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's fenced line 13a checkbox on a joint return, and false on every other filing status. It mirrors the MFJ operand the shipping Section B totals /medicareAdvantageMsaForm8853Line10Total, Line11Total, Line12Total and Line13bTotal already carry: the controlling Form 8853 that combines two statement Section Bs is the JOINT return's, and on a married filing separately return each spouse files their own Form 8853, where the spouse's exception claim has no place.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 LINE 17, gross LTC payments received on a per diem basis
Fact.Description: FORM 8853 LINE 17, return level: "Gross LTC payments received on a per diem or other periodic basis. Enter the total of the amounts from box 1 of all Forms 1099-LTC you received with respect to the insured on which the 'Per diem' box in box 3 is checked." IT IS AN INTAKE: the figure is the taxpayer's own total of the per diem box 1 amounts. /form1099Ltcs carries per-item writableGrossLongTermCareBenefitsPaid (box 1) and writableBenefitsArePerDiem (box 3), but this line is not summed from it: summing the collection would change a computed number, and it is not done here. It carries no downstream leg of its own: line 18, not this line, is what enters the line 20 subtotal, because line 17 is the gross figure before the qualified contract split.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 LINE 18, the part of line 17 from qualified LTC contracts
Fact.Description: FORM 8853 LINE 18, return level: "Enter the part of the amount on line 17 that is from qualified LTC insurance contracts". IT IS AN INTAKE AND NOT A DERIVATION OF LINE 17. Whether a contract is a qualified long term care insurance contract is a contract level fact about the policy, not an arithmetic property of the gross figure, and the printed Caution under line 17 is explicit that a non qualified contract's benefits leave this computation entirely and are reported directly on Schedule 1. Nothing in the graph can make that split.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 LINE 19, accelerated death benefits received periodically
Fact.Description: FORM 8853 LINE 19, return level: "Accelerated death benefits received on a per diem or other periodic basis. Don't include any amounts you received because the insured was terminally ill." IT IS AN INTAKE. /form1099Ltcs/*/writableAcceleratedDeathBenefitsPaid (box 2) and /form1099Ltcs/*/writableInsuredTerminallyIll (box 5) exist, but the terminally-ill exclusion is per-payment, not per-form, and box 2 is not split by it. The terminally ill exclusion the line carries on its face is the reason line 16 exists on the printed form, and it is honoured inside this intake rather than by a derivation: an amount paid because the insured was terminally ill is excluded outright under IRC 101(g)(1)(A) and never enters the per diem limitation at all.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 LINE 21, $420 times the days in the LTC period
Fact.Description: FORM 8853 LINE 21, return level: "Multiply $420 by the number of days in the LTC period". IT IS AN INTAKE RATHER THAN A PRODUCT, AND THE REASON IS BOTH SIDES OF THE MULTIPLICATION. The graph has no LTC period at all, so the day count does not exist to be multiplied; and the seventeen candidate templates carry no Multiply, so even a day count intake could not be turned into this dollar without abusing the ratable allocation template. The $420 is the 2025 indexed per diem limitation figure printed on the form itself. THE SUBSTANTIVE LIMIT IS IRC 7702B(d), WHICH IS NOT VENDORED UNDER sources/; the anchor here is IRC 101(g), whose paragraph (4) is the cross reference to it.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 LINE 22, costs incurred for qualified LTC services
Fact.Description: FORM 8853 LINE 22, return level: "Costs incurred for qualified LTC services provided for the insured during the LTC period". IT IS AN INTAKE BECAUSE NO MEDICAL EXPENSE IN THIS GRAPH IS RESTRICTED TO QUALIFIED LTC SERVICES OR TO THE LTC PERIOD. Schedule A's medical expense intake is a year long total of every deductible medical cost, which is a different population of dollars over a different span, and reading it here would overstate the alternative to the per diem cap.

Fact.Name: Writable: Form 8853 LINE 24, reimbursements for qualified LTC services
Fact.Description: FORM 8853 LINE 24, return level: "Reimbursements for qualified LTC services provided for the insured during the LTC period". IT IS AN INTAKE FOR THE SAME REASON LINE 22 IS, and it carries one more caveat the form prints beside it: reimbursements from LTC contracts issued before August 1, 1996 follow a different instruction, which is a contract vintage this graph does not record.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 16 No, the insured was not a terminally ill individual
Fact.Description: The bool_not twin of /writableForm8853InsuredWasTerminallyIll: the printed No box of the line 16 Yes/No pair.

Fact.Name: The Form 8853 Section C policyholder is the secondary filer
Fact.Description: The bool_not twin of /writableForm8853LtcPolicyholderIsPrimaryFiler: the arm that selects the spouse's name into the printed policyholder box.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 Section C policyholder name, primary filer arm
Fact.Description: The primary filer's full name when the policyholder is the primary filer, the empty string otherwise. The printed box maps this and the secondary arm as two tokens, so exactly one of them contributes text. Print only until the Section C collection named in this fact's obligation exists.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 Section C policyholder name, secondary filer arm
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's full name when the policyholder is the spouse, the empty string otherwise. Paired with the primary arm as the second token of the printed policyholder box.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 15 No, no other payee received payments on this contract
Fact.Description: The bool_not twin of /writableForm8853OtherPayeeReceivedLtcPayments: the printed No box of the line 15 Yes/No pair.

Fact.Name: Social security number of the Archer MSA account holder
Fact.Description: The SSN printed in the Form 8853 page 1 identity box. The controlling form this repo renders covers both spouses but the printed box takes ONE SSN, and no fact in hsa or filers says which spouse holds the Archer MSA, so this is an intake rather than an alias of /primaryFiler/tin. A bool_switch over a which spouse Bool cannot serve it: the bool_switch default literal has no TIN type, so a TIN cannot be selected between two filers with the templates available.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 14a name of the insured
Fact.Description: The insured under the long term care contract. The insured is not a filer, not a dependent and not an item of any collection this graph has, so line 14a is an intake. Print only until the Section C collection named in this fact's obligation exists.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 14b social security number of the insured
Fact.Description: The insured's SSN, the identity half of line 14. Same gap as line 14a: the graph models no insured. Print only until the Section C collection named in this fact's obligation exists.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 16 Yes, the insured was a terminally ill individual
Fact.Description: Line 16 is a fact about the insured. Its arithmetic consequence is already honoured inside the built chain because line 19 excludes amounts received because the insured was terminally ill, so a terminally ill only payment stream reaches line 26 as zero through lines 18 and 19; this fact carries the printed answer. Print only until the Section C collection named in this fact's obligation exists.

Fact.Name: The Form 8853 Section C policyholder is the primary filer
Fact.Description: Which filer is the policyholder of the long term care insurance contract Section C reports. The printed page 2 box takes one name while the page 1 header takes both, so the return must say which. Print only until the Section C collection named in this fact's obligation exists.

Fact.Name: Social security number of the Form 8853 Section C policyholder
Fact.Description: The SSN printed under the Section C policyholder name. It is an intake rather than a switch over /primaryFiler/tin and /secondaryFiler/tin because the bool_switch default literal has no TIN type, so no template selects a TIN between two filers. Print only until the Section C collection named in this fact's obligation exists.

Fact.Name: More than one Form 8853 Section C is attached
Fact.Description: The Section C header checkbox. It is an intake today because the ten Section C amount facts in hsa.xml are return level scalars that model exactly one copy, so nothing in the graph can count them. It becomes a collection_any style derivation once the Section C collection named in this fact's obligation exists.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 line 15 Yes, another payee received payments on this contract
Fact.Description: Line 15 asks whether anyone other than the filer received per diem or other periodic payments under a qualified LTC contract covering the insured, or accelerated death benefits under a life policy covering the insured. Its consequence is the Multiple Payees instruction, which reallocates lines 21 through 25 between payees; the built chain prices the single payee case only. Print only until the Section C collection named in this fact's obligation exists.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8e, income from Form 8853
Fact.Description:
The whole of printed Schedule 1 line 8e, which is one line for the whole of Form 8853. The dictionary carries it as THREE legs that income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome already adds separately: /archerMsaSchedule1Line8eTaxableDistributions (Form 8853 line 8), /medicareAdvantageMsaSchedule1Line8eTaxableDistributions (Form 8853 line 12) and income:/schedule1Line8eForm8853LtcPaymentsOrZero (Form 8853 Section C line 26, "Also include this amount in the total on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8e"). All three are complete safe zero, so the printed line is complete on every return.
THE THIRD LEG IS READ FROM THE income MODULE RATHER THAN WRAPPED AGAIN HERE, and that is deliberate. /form8853Line26TaxableLtcPayments is NOT complete safe - the subtraction under its printed $0 floor reads Section C intakes a return without a long term care contract never answers - so the leg has to be a wrapper, and income.xml already carries exactly that wrapper for the line 9 total. Coining a second wrapper here would be two facts for one quantity, and the two could then disagree; reading that one is what makes the printed cell and the line 9 total foot to the same number by construction. The direction is safe: income:/schedule1Line8eForm8853LtcPaymentsOrZero depends only on hsa:/form8853Line26TaxableLtcPayments, which does not depend on income, so there is no cycle. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8f, income from Form 8889
Fact.Description:
The whole of printed Schedule 1 line 8f, which is one line for the Form 8889 income routes. The dictionary carries it as THREE legs that income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome already adds separately, so this printed box and line 9 foot by construction: /hsaCollectionRouteTaxableDistributions (Form 8889 line 16), /hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncomeAndAdditionalTax (Form 8889 Part III line 20) and form8889:/schedule1Line8fPledgedHsaFmvIncome, the IRC 408(e)(4) pledged-as-security deemed distribution. The excess contribution earnings leg /hsaExcessContributionEarningsOtherIncome is NOT here: the 2025 Instructions for Form 8889 send those earnings to Other income rather than to a numbered Form 8889 line, which is Schedule 1 line 8z.
THE THIRD LEG MUST BE NAMED HERE AS WELL AS IN THE TOTAL. Wired into income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome (Schedule 1 line 9, the total) alone, the pledge amount would sit in the line-9 total with $0 in the PRINTED 8f box that dictionary/pdf/2025/reviews/forms/IRS1040S1.json binds to field f1_18[0], and the schedule would not foot. THE RULE: an amount routed to a numbered Schedule 1 box must be named BOTH in that box's fact and in the line-9 total, because income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome adds the legs individually and never reads this fact.
The pledge leg is complete-safe $0. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8z, the other income write in amount
Fact.Description:
The amount printed in the right hand box of Schedule 1 line 8z. Every leg is already a separate addend of income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome (line 9), so this printed box and line 9 foot by construction. The legs: /hsaSchedule1Line8zEmployerExcessOtherIncome and /archerMsaSchedule1Line8zEmployerExcessOtherIncome (the excess employer contributions the Excess Employer Contributions paragraphs send to Other income); /hsaExcessContributionEarningsOtherIncome (the earnings on excess contributions withdrawn before the due date, which the same instructions send to Other income); form1099Misc:/form1099MiscOtherIncome, the non-Alaska-PFD Form 1099-MISC box 3 amounts the recipient instruction sends to the Other income line; form8814:/form8814TotalLine12OtherIncome (the Form 8814 line 12 write-in); income:/schedule1Line8zEntriesTotal (the generic per-entry write-in collection: substitute payments in lieu of dividends, RTAA payments, taxable grants, and Form 6251 line 2b recoveries); income:/schedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureLeg, the Form 4797 line 35 section 179 / section 280F recapture the filer allocates to no Schedule C and no Schedule F, which the instructions send to Other income; form8621:/form8621OrdinaryIncome, the Form 8621 ordinary income — the QEF ordinary earnings of line 6c, the section 1296 mark-to-market ordinary income and loss, and the section 1291 current-year and pre-PFIC allocations — which the 2025 Instructions for Form 8621 route to Other income, "include this amount as 'other income' on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8z"; income:/schedule1Line8zCasualtyLossRecoveryIncome, the part of this year's casualty or theft reimbursement that recovers a loss deducted on an earlier year's return, which Pub. 525 sends to "other income on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8z"; income:/schedule1Line8zAtRiskRecaptureIncome, the section 465(e) at-risk recapture; income:/schedule1Line8zForm1099GRtaaPayments, the Form 1099-G box 5 RTAA payments; income:/schedule1Line8zForm1099GTaxableGrants, the Form 1099-G box 6 personal taxable grants; income:/schedule1Line8zCooperativeDistributionsWithoutScheduleF, the Form 1099-PATR boxes 1, 2, 3 and 5 on a return without Schedule F (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-56).
THE RULE: an amount routed to a numbered Schedule 1 box must be named BOTH in that box's fact and in the line-9 total, because income:/schedule1TotalOtherIncome adds the legs individually and never reads this fact. A leg that reaches line 9 alone leaves this printed box short, and the filed Part I does not foot (line 9 is "Add lines 8a through 8z").
COMPLETENESS: every leg is complete safe zero except the Form 4797 leg, which is complete safe zero on every return with no Part IV line 35 amount and INCOMPLETE, deliberately, when a nonzero line 35 is not fully allocated (form4797:/hasUnallocatedPartIVLine35Recapture reads true). So this box is Incomplete exactly when line 9 is. The Form 8621 leg and the casualty recovery leg are complete safe $0 on every return with no Form 8621 and no measurable prior-year recovery. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8z write-in type
Fact.Description: The filer's own words for the Schedule 1 line 8z type space, for income this dictionary does not already name there. The printed space is /schedule1Line8zPrintedType, which starts with this text and adds a label for each computed leg of the line 8z amount box (hsa:/schedule1Line8zOtherIncome): the excess employer contributions to a health savings account or Archer MSA, the earnings on an excess HSA contribution withdrawn before the due date, the Form 1099-MISC amounts, the Form 8814 line 12 inclusion, the Form 1099-G box 5 RTAA payments and the other computed legs, so the filer does not retype them. Nothing computes from it. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540) line 8z printed type).

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8z, the printed type beside the amount
Fact.Description: What prints in the "List type and amount" space of Schedule 1 line 8z: every kind of income the line 8z amount box (/schedule1Line8zOtherIncome) carries, named once each and joined with "; ". It starts with the filer's own write-in (/writableSchedule1Line8zOtherIncomeType) when answered, then adds a fixed label for each computed leg whose amount is not $0: HSA excess employer contributions, Archer MSA excess employer contributions, HSA excess contribution earnings, Form 1099-MISC (the box 3, box 8 and box 15 amounts that module sends here), Form 8814 (the label the Form 8814 line 12 instruction prints), RTAA payments (Form 1099-G box 5), Taxable grants (Form 1099-G box 6), Form 4797 recapture, Form 8621, Casualty loss recovery, Section 465(e) recapture, Form 1099-PATR, and "See attached statement" for the /schedule1Line8zEntries list, whose entries each carry their own type and amount and are shown on the statement the instruction allows when the space is not enough. The Form 8814 label is the form's own; the others are this dictionary's wording, since no instruction prints one. Paste drops an empty label, so a line with one kind of income prints that label alone. Each leg is tested for completeness before it is read, so this fact is always Complete: an empty String when line 8z carries nothing.

Fact.Name: The return has a Form 8853 Section C long term care payment stream
Fact.Description:
Whether this return has answered the Form 8853 Section C intakes, so Section C has a value to print. It is IsComplete(/form8853Line26TaxableLtcPayments), the line 26 taxable payments cell, which resolves only once the Section C chain under it resolves - lines 18 and 19 (the payment stream) and the line 21 to 25 per diem limitation.
IsComplete IS A REAL PREDICATE HERE AND NOT A TAUTOLOGY, which is the distinction the reconciliation rule about answered ness predicates turns on. /form8853Line26TaxableLtcPayments is floored at $0 by a printed GreaterOf but is NOT complete safe: the subtraction under the floor reads /writableForm8853Line18QualifiedLtcContractPayments, /writableForm8853Line19AcceleratedDeathBenefits and the line 24 reimbursement intake, none of which a return without a long term care insurance contract ever answers. So this fact is FALSE on every return in the repo today and true exactly on the Section C population. Taking IsComplete on income:/schedule1Line8eForm8853LtcPaymentsOrZero instead would be the tautology the rule forbids, because that wrapper is complete safe by construction.
A THIRD POPULATION: Form 8853 Section C is long-term care (LTC), and its filing trigger is being a policyholder who received payments under an LTC insurance contract rather than holding any MSA. This fact names that population; it does not join it to the Archer or Medicare Advantage ones.

Fact.Name: Form 8853 renders on this return
Fact.Description:
The population gate for the WHOLE of Form 8853, all three sections: Any of /archerMsaOnThisReturn (Section A), /medicareAdvantageMsaOnThisReturn (Section B) and /form8853SectionCOnThisReturn (Section C).
WHY IT IS A NEW FACT AND NOT A SECTION C ARM ON /archerMsaOnThisReturn. The obligation as written asks for "a Section C arm on the IRS8853 render gate", and /archerMsaOnThisReturn is what dictionary/pdf/2025/gates.tsv line 51 uses as that gate. But that fact is not only a render gate: eleven other facts in this module read it as the ARCHER predicate - the Form 8889 line 4 Archer contribution reduction, the Part I line 2 chain, the Section B population gate itself, and several complete safe fences that state "complete safe false on every return without an Archer MSA". Making it true for a long term care policyholder with no MSA at all would make every one of those fire on a return that has no Archer MSA, which is a wrong answer in eleven places to fix a render gate in one. The gate is therefore lifted out into this fact, which is what the register should read, and /archerMsaOnThisReturn keeps its Archer meaning.
COMPLETE SAFE FALSE: each of the three operands is (each carries its own IsComplete fence), so this resolves false rather than Incomplete on every return that never reached the questions, and it is false on every return committed to this repo today.
